**Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 24, verses 1–2 (part 1 of 2):**

Surat al-Nur (The Light)
It is Medinan.
In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.
* *
Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿This is a surah which We have sent down﴾. This draws attention to the importance of this surah, and does not negate what is other than it. [[In A: "ila" (to) instead of "ala" (upon).]]

﴿And We have made it obligatory﴾. Mujahid and Qatadah said: that is, We have explained the lawful and the unlawful, the commands and the prohibitions, and the hudud (the prescribed punishments).

Al-Bukhari said: Whoever reads "faradnaha" (with the tashdid, intensive form) says: "We have made it obligatory upon you and upon those after you."

﴿And We have sent down in it clear verses﴾, that is, explained and manifest, ﴿so that you may remember﴾.

Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿The adulteress and the adulterer, flog each one of them a hundred lashes﴾. This noble verse contains the ruling on the punishment (hadd) for the adulterer, and the scholars have differing views and detailed discussion on it. The adulterer is either a bikr (one who has not married) or muhsan (one who has had intercourse in a valid marriage), and is free, adult and sane. As for the one who is a bikr and has never married, his punishment is a hundred lashes, as in the verse, and to this is added exile for a year [from his city], according to the majority of scholars, unlike Abu Hanifah, may Allah have mercy on him, who holds that exile is left to the judgment of the ruler: if he wishes he may exile, and if he wishes he may not.

The majority's evidence for this is what is established in the two Sahihs, from the narration of al-Zuhri, from Ubayd Allah ibn Abd Allah ibn Utbah ibn Mas'ud, from Abu Hurayrah and Zayd ibn Khalid al-Juhani, concerning the two Bedouin men who came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. One of them said: "O Messenger of Allah, my son was a laborer (asif, i.e., a hired worker) for this man, and he committed adultery with his wife. I ransomed my son from him with a hundred sheep and a slave-girl. Then I asked the people of knowledge, and they informed me that upon my son is a hundred lashes and a year's exile, and upon this man's wife is stoning." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, I will judge between you both by the Book of Allah: the slave-girl and the sheep are returned to you, and upon your son is a hundred lashes and a year's exile. And go out, O Unays, to a man of Aslam, to this man's wife, and if she confesses, stone her." So he went to her, she confessed, and he stoned her. [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (2314, 6633) and Sahih Muslim no. (1697).]]

In this there is evidence for the exile of the adulterer together with the hundred lashes when he is a bikr who has not married. As for the muhsan, he is stoned, as Imam Malik said: Ibn Shihab narrated to me, informing us from Ubayd Allah ibn Abd Allah ibn Utbah ibn Mas'ud, that Ibn Abbas informed him that Umar, may Allah be pleased with him, stood, praised Allah and extolled Him, then said: "As to what follows, O people, indeed Allah sent Muhammad with the truth and sent down the Book upon him, and among what was sent down to him was the verse of stoning. We recited it and understood it, and the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stoned, and we stoned after him. I fear that a long time will pass over the people and someone will say: 'We do not find the verse of stoning in the Book of Allah,' and they will go astray by abandoning an obligation that Allah has sent down. So stoning in the Book of Allah is a truth upon whoever commits adultery, when he is muhsan, whether man or woman, when the evidence is established, or pregnancy, or confession."

They both (al-Bukhari and Muslim) reported it in the two Sahihs from the hadith of Malik at length, and this is a portion of it, in which is our purpose here. [[Al-Muwatta' (2/822), Sahih al-Bukhari nos. (6829, 6830) and Sahih Muslim no. (1691), and it is in both of them with this context from the hadith of Ibn Shihab al-Zuhri.]]

Imam Ahmad narrated from Hushaym, from al-Zuhri, from Ubayd Allah ibn Abd Allah, from Ibn Abbas: Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf narrated to me that Umar ibn al-Khattab addressed the people, and I heard him saying: "Beware, some people say: 'What is the matter with stoning? In the Book of Allah there is only flogging.' But the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stoned, and we stoned after him. Had it not been that people would say—or speakers would speak—that Umar added to the Book of Allah what is not in it, I would have affirmed it as it was revealed."

An-Nasa'i also reported it, from the hadith of Ubayd Allah ibn Abd Allah, with the same chain. [[Al-Musnad (1/29) and al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra (7154).]]

Imam Ahmad also narrated from Hushaym, from Ali ibn Zayd, from Yusuf ibn Mihran, from Ibn Abbas, who said: Umar ibn al-Khattab delivered a sermon and mentioned stoning, and said: "Do not be deceived concerning it, for it is one of the hudud (limits) of Allah. Indeed the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stoned, and we stoned after him. Had it not been that people would say: 'Umar added to the Book of Allah what is not in it,' I would have written in a corner of the mushaf: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, Abd al-Rahman ibn Awf, and so-and-so and so-and-so bear witness that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stoned and we stoned after him.' Beware, there will come after you a people who deny stoning, and the Dajjal, and intercession, and the punishment of the grave, and a people who will come out of the Fire after they have been burned." [[Al-Musnad (1/23).]]

Imam Ahmad also narrated from Yahya al-Qattan, from Yahya al-Ansari, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, from Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him: "Beware of perishing through the verse of stoning."

The hadith was narrated by al-Tirmidhi from the hadith of Sa'id, from Umar, and he said: sahih (authentic). [[Al-Musnad (1/36) and Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (1431).]]

Al-Hafiz Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili said: Ubayd Allah ibn Umar al-Qawariri narrated to us, Yazid ibn Zurayʿ narrated to us, Ibn Awn narrated to us, from Muhammad—that is Ibn Sirin—who said: I was informed by Kathir ibn al-Salt who said: "We were with Marwan, and Zayd was among us, and Zayd said: 'We used to recite: "The elderly man and the elderly woman, if they commit adultery, stone them absolutely." Marwan said: "Why did you not write it in the mushaf?" He said: "We mentioned that, and Umar ibn al-Khattab was among us, and he said: 'I will relieve you of that doubt.' We said: 'How?' He said: 'A man came to the Prophet ﷺ,' and he mentioned such-and-such, and mentioned stoning, and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, write for me the verse of stoning.' He said: 'I cannot do so now.'" This, or something similar to it.

An-Nasa'i also narrated it from Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna, from Ghundar, from Shu'bah, from Qatadah, from Yunus ibn Jubayr, from Kathir ibn al-Salt, from Zayd ibn Thabit, with the same wording. [[Al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra no. (7148).]]

All these chains are multiple and mutually supporting [[In F and A: "mutaʿadidah" replaced by "mutaʿadiyah"/ "mutaʿadidah"; the variant reads "mutaʿadiyah" (mutually reinforcing).]] and indicate that the verse of stoning was written and its recitation was abrogated (naskh al-tilawah), while its ruling remained in effect. And to Allah belongs all praise. [[In F and A: "And Allah knows best."]]

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded the stoning of this woman, who was the wife of the man who hired the laborer, when she committed adultery with the laborer. The Prophet ﷺ also stoned Ma'iz and the Ghamidiyyah. None of these is reported from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ as having been flogged before being stoned. Rather, the numerous sound hadiths, with multiple chains and wordings, mention only their stoning, and there is no mention of flogging in them. For this reason this is the position of the majority of scholars, and Abu Hanifah, Malik and al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on them all, adopted it. But Imam Ahmad, may Allah have mercy on him, held that the muhsan adulterer must be subjected to both flogging, on the basis of the verse, and stoning, on the basis of the Sunnah, as is narrated from the Commander of the Faithful Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, that when Shurahah, who had committed adultery while being muhsanah, was brought to him, he flogged her on Thursday and stoned her on Friday, and then said: "I flogged her by the Book of Allah, and I stoned her by the Sunnah of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ." [[In A: "Busurajah" for "Shurahah".]]

Imam Ahmad, Muslim, and the authors of the four Sunan narrated from the hadith of Qatadah, from al-Hasan, from Hittan [[In A: "Ata'" for "Hittan".]] ibn Abd Allah al-Raqashi, from Ubadah ibn al-Samit, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Take from me, take from me; Allah has made a way for them: the virgin with the virgin, a hundred lashes and a year's exile [[In A: "am" for "sanah".]]; and the non-virgin (thayyib) with the non-virgin, a hundred lashes and stoning." [[Al-Musnad (5/317), Sahih Muslim no. (1690), Sunan Abi Dawud no. (4416), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (1434), al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra no. (11092) and Sunan Ibn Majah no. (2550).]]
* *
And His saying: ﴿And let not pity for them take hold of you in the religion of Allah﴾, that is, in the judgment of Allah. Do not refrain from stoning them and show them pity in the law of Allah. What is forbidden is not the natural feeling of pity [that is not present] upon abandoning the hadd [and it is only the pity that moves the judge to abandon the hadd], so it is not permissible.

Mujahid said: ﴿And let not pity for them take hold of you in the religion of Allah﴾ — he said: the establishing of the hudud once they are brought before the authority, so that they are established and not suspended. Similarly it is narrated from Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Ata' ibn Abi Rabah. And it has come in a hadith: "Pardon the hudud among yourselves, for whatever hadd reaches me is obligatory." [[Narrated by Abu Dawud in al-Sunan no. (4376) and al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan (8/70) from the hadith of Amr ibn Shu'ayb, from his father, from his grandfather.]] And in another hadith: "A hadd established on the earth is better for its people than being rained upon for forty mornings." [[Al-Musnad (2/362) and al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan (8/75), from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him.]]

It was also said: the meaning is: ﴿And let not pity for them take hold of you in the religion of Allah﴾, so do not establish the hadd as it should be, in terms of the severity of the beating that deters from sin; and the intended meaning is not a beating that is excessively brutal.

Amir al-Sha'bi said: ﴿And let not pity for them take hold of you in the religion of Allah﴾ — he said: mercy in the severity of the beating. Ata' said: a beating that is not brutal (mubarrih). Sa'id ibn Abi Arubah narrated from Hammad ibn Abi Sulayman: "The slanderer (qadhif) is flogged while wearing his clothes, and the adulterer is stripped of his clothes." Then he recited: ﴿And let not pity for them take hold of you in the religion of Allah﴾. I said: "Is this regarding the ruling?" He said: "This is regarding the ruling and the flogging"—meaning in the establishing of the hadd and in the severity of the beating.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Amr ibn Abd Allah al-Awdi [[In F: "al-Azdi"; in A: "al-Armazi".]] narrated to us, Waki' narrated to us, from Nafi', [from] [[Added from J and A.]] Ibn Amr, from Ibn Abi Mulaykah, from Ubayd Allah [[In F and A: "Abd Allah".]] ibn Abd Allah ibn Umar: that a slave-girl of Ibn Umar committed adultery, so he struck her legs—Nafi' said: "I think he said: and her back." He said: I said: ﴿And let not pity for them take hold of you in the religion of Allah﴾. He said: "O my son, do you see that pity has taken hold of me? Allah did not command me to kill her, nor to make her flogging on her head; and she has been made to suffer where she was struck." [[Also narrated by al-Tabari in his tafsir (18/52) through the chain of Nafi', from Ibn Umar, and mentioned it.]]
* *
And His saying: ﴿If you believe in Allah and the Last Day﴾, that is: then do this—establish the hudud upon whoever commits adultery, and be severe in the beating, but not brutal, so that he and whoever does the like of it may be deterred by it. And it has come in al-Musnad from one of the Companions that he said: "O Messenger of Allah, I slaughter a sheep while I have mercy on it." He said: "For you in that there is a reward." [[Al-Musnad (3/436), from the hadith of Qurrah al-Muzani, may Allah be pleased with him.]]
* *
And His saying: ﴿And let a group of the believers witness their punishment﴾: This contains a public humiliation (tankil) of the two adulterers when they are flogged in the presence of people, for that is more effective in restraining them and more conducive to deterring them, since in it is reproach, rebuke, and disgrace when people are present.

Al-Hasan al-Basri, regarding His words ﴿And let a group of the believers witness their punishment﴾, said: it means publicly.

Then Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿And let a group of the believers witness their punishment﴾: the group (ta'ifah) is one man or more.

Mujahid said: the ta'ifah is from one man up to a thousand. Ikrimah said the same. For this reason Ahmad said: the term ta'ifah applies to a single person.

Ata' ibn Abi Rabah said: it is two. Ishaq ibn Rahawayh also held this view. Likewise Sa'id ibn Jubayr said, regarding ﴿a group of the believers﴾: it means two men or more.

Al-Zuhri said: three persons or more.

Abd al-Razzaq said: Ibn Wahb narrated to me from Imam Malik, regarding His words ﴿And let a group of the believers witness their punishment﴾, that he said: the ta'ifah is four persons or more, because testimony in the case of adultery is not valid with fewer than four witnesses or more. Al-Shafi'i also held this view.

Rabi'ah said: five. Al-Hasan al-Basri said: ten. Qatadah said: Allah commanded that a group of the believers, meaning a number of the Muslims, witness their punishment, so that it would be an admonition, a lesson, and a deterrent.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: my father narrated to us, Yahya ibn Uthman narrated to us, Baqiyyah narrated to us, who said: I heard Nasr ibn Alqamah regarding His words ﴿And let a group of the believers witness their punishment﴾, who said: that is not for disgrace; rather, it is so that Allah the Exalted is invoked for them to repent and for mercy.

He said: I said: ﴿And let not pity for them take hold of you in the religion of Allah﴾. He said: "O my son, do you see that pity has taken hold of me? Allah did not command me to kill her, nor to make her flogging on her head; and she has been made to suffer where she was struck." [[Also narrated by al-Tabari in his tafsir (18/52) through the chain of Nafi', from Ibn Umar, and mentioned it.]]
* *
And His saying: ﴿If you believe in Allah and the Last Day﴾, that is: then do this—establish the hudud upon whoever commits adultery, and be severe in the beating, but not brutal, so that he and whoever does the like of it may be deterred by it. And it has come in al-Musnad from one of the Companions that he said: "O Messenger of Allah, I slaughter a sheep while I have mercy on it." He said: "For you in that there is a reward." [[Al-Musnad (3/436), from the hadith of Qurrah al-Muzani, may Allah be pleased with him.]]
* *
And His saying: ﴿And let a group of the believers witness their punishment﴾: This contains a public humiliation (tankil) of the two adulterers when they are flogged in the presence of people, for that is more effective in restraining them and more conducive to deterring them, since in it is reproach, rebuke, and disgrace when people are present.

Al-Hasan al-Basri, regarding His words ﴿And let a group of the believers witness their punishment﴾, said: it means publicly.

Then Ali ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn Abbas, regarding ﴿And let a group of the believers witness their punishment﴾: the group (ta'ifah) is one man or more.

Mujahid said: the ta'ifah is from one man up to a thousand. Ikrimah said the same. For this reason Ahmad said: the term ta'ifah applies to a single person.

Ata' ibn Abi Rabah said: it is two. Ishaq ibn Rahawayh also held this view. Likewise Sa'id ibn Jubayr said, regarding ﴿a group of the believers﴾: it means two men or more.

Al-Zuhri said: three persons or more.

Abd al-Razzaq said: Ibn Wahb narrated to me from Imam Malik, regarding His words ﴿And let a group of the believers witness their punishment﴾, that he said: the ta'ifah is four persons or more, because testimony in the case of adultery is not valid with fewer than four witnesses or more. Al-Shafi'i also held this view.

Rabi'ah said: five. Al-Hasan al-Basri said: ten. Qatadah said: Allah commanded that a group of the believers, meaning a number of the Muslims, witness their punishment, so that it would be an admonition, a lesson, and a deterrent.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: my father narrated to us, Yahya ibn Uthman narrated to us, Baqiyyah narrated to us, who said: I heard Nasr ibn Alqamah regarding His words ﴿And let a group of the believers witness their punishment﴾, who said: that is not for disgrace; rather, it is so that Allah the Exalted is invoked for them to repent and for mercy.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 24, verse 3 (part 1 of 2):

This is a report from Allah, exalted is He, that the fornicator does not marry except a fornicatress or a polytheist. That is: none will comply with his desire for fornication except a sinful fornicatress or a polytheist who does not regard its prohibition. Likewise: ﴿The fornicatress - none marries her except a fornicator﴾, meaning one who is sinful through his fornication, ﴿or a polytheist﴾ who does not believe in its prohibition.

Sufyan al-Thawri narrated from Habib ibn Abi 'Amra, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, regarding ﴿The fornicator does not marry except a fornicatress or a polytheist﴾, that he said: "This is not about marriage (nikah); it is about intercourse (jima'). None has intercourse with her except a fornicator or a polytheist."

This is a sound chain of narration from him, and it has been narrated from him through more than one route. It has also been narrated in similar terms from Mujahid, 'Ikrimah, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, 'Urwa ibn al-Zubayr, al-Dahhak, Makhul, Muqatil ibn Hayyan, and others.

* *

As for His saying, exalted is He, ﴿And that is forbidden to the believers﴾, that is: engaging in it, and marrying prostitutes, or marrying chaste women to immoral men.

Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said: Qays narrated to us, from Abu Husayn, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding ﴿And that is forbidden to the believers﴾, that he said: "Allah has forbidden fornication to the believers."

Qatada and Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: Allah has forbidden to the believers marriage to prostitutes. And it was mentioned earlier in this regard, when He said: ﴿And that is forbidden to the believers.﴾

This verse is like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿chaste, not fornicating openly, nor taking secret lovers﴾ [al-Nisa': 25], and His saying: ﴿chaste, not fornicating openly, nor taking secret lovers﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 5]. From this, Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal, may Allah have mercy on him, held that the marriage contract of a chaste man to a prostitute is not valid for as long as she remains so, until she repents; if she repents, the contract with her is valid, and otherwise it is not. Likewise, the marriage of a free, chaste woman to an immoral fornicating man is not valid until he repents a sound repentance, based on His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And that is forbidden to the believers.﴾

Imam Ahmad said: 'Arim [[In F, A: "'Arim ibn al-Fadl."]] narrated to us, Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us, saying: My father said to me: al-Hadrami narrated to us, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr, may Allah be pleased with them both, that a man among the Muslims asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for permission regarding a woman called "Umm Mahzul" who used to commit fornication and stipulated that she would spend on him. He said: So he asked the Messenger of Allah ﷺ - or he mentioned her matter to him - and the Prophet ﷺ recited to him: ﴿The fornicator does not marry except a fornicatress or a polytheist, and the fornicatress is not married except by a fornicator or a polytheist, and that is forbidden to the believers.﴾ [[Al-Musnad (2/159).]]

Al-Nasa'i said: 'Amr ibn 'Ali informed us, al-Mu'tamir ibn Sulayman narrated to us, from his father, from al-Hadrami, from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr, who said: There was a woman called "Umm Mahzul" who used to commit fornication, and a man from the companions of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ wanted to marry her, so Allah, mighty and majestic, revealed: ﴿The fornicator does not marry except a fornicatress or a polytheist, and the fornicatress is not married except by a fornicator or a polytheist, and that is forbidden to the believers.﴾ [[Al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra, no. (11359).]]

[And] [[Addition in F, A.]] al-Tirmidhi said: 'Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us, Rawh ibn 'Ubada ibn 'Ubayd Allah ibn al-Akhnas narrated to us, 'Amr ibn Shu'ayb informed me, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: There was a man called "Marthad ibn Abi Marthad," who used to carry captives from Makkah until he brought them to Madinah. He said: There was a prostitute in Makkah called "'Anaq," who was a friend of his, and he had arranged with a captive from Makkah whom he would carry. He said: I came until I reached the shade of a wall of one of the gardens of Makkah on a moonlit night. He said: 'Anaq came and saw the black shadow of me beneath the wall, and when she reached me she recognised me and said: "Marthad?" I said: "Marthad." She said: "Welcome and well come, come and spend the night with us." He said: I said: "O 'Anaq, Allah has forbidden fornication." She said: "O people of the tents, this man is carrying off your captives!" He said: Eight men followed me, and I entered the orchard [[In F, A: "al-Hadiqa."]] and reached a cave or a cavern, and I entered it. They came and stood over my head and urinated, and their urine fell upon my head, but Allah blinded them to me. He said: Then they returned, and I returned to my companion and carried him, and he was a heavy man, until I reached al-Idhkhir, and I unfastened his shackles, and I kept carrying him while he helped me, until I brought him [[In F: "I arrived at"]] Madinah. I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of Allah, shall I marry 'Anaq? Shall I marry 'Anaq?" - twice. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ remained silent and did not answer me at all, until ﴿The fornicator does not marry except a fornicatress or a polytheist, and the fornicatress is not married except by a fornicator or a polytheist, and that is forbidden to the believers﴾ was revealed. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ then said: "O Marthad, ﴿The fornicator does not marry except a fornicatress or a polytheist [and the fornicatress is not married except by a fornicator or a polytheist]﴾, so do not marry her." [[Addition from F, A.]] Then al-Tirmidhi said: This is a hasan gharib hadith; we do not know it except through this route.

Abu Dawud and al-Nasa'i also narrated it in the Book of Marriage in their Sunan, from the hadith of 'Ubayd Allah ibn al-Akhnas, with this chain. [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3177), Sunan Abi Dawud no. (2051), and Sunan al-Nasa'i (6/66).]]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Musaddad Abu al-Hasan narrated to us, 'Abd al-Warith narrated to us, from Habib al-Mu'allim, who said: 'Amr ibn Shu'ayb narrated to me, from Sa'id al-Maqburi, from Abu Hurayra, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The fornicator who has been flogged does not marry except one like him."

Abu Dawud included it likewise in his Sunan, from Musaddad and Abu Ma'mar - 'Abdullah ibn 'Amr - both from 'Abd al-Warith, with this chain. [[Sunan Abi Dawud no. (2052).]]

Imam Ahmad said: Ya'qub narrated to us, 'Asim ibn Muhammad ibn Zayd ibn 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar ibn al-Khattab narrated to us, from his brother 'Umar ibn Muhammad, from 'Abdullah ibn Yasar - the client of Ibn 'Umar - who said: I testify that I heard Salim say: 'Abdullah said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Three will not enter Paradise, and Allah will not look at them on the Day of Resurrection: the one who disobeys his parents, the woman who masculinises herself (the one who imitates men), and the dayyuth. And three Allah will not look at on the Day of Resurrection: the one who disobeys his parents, the habitual drinker of wine, and the one who reminds of what he has given."

al-Nasa'i narrated it from 'Amr ibn 'Ali al-Fallas, from Yazid ibn Zuray', from 'Umar ibn Muhammad al-'Umari, from 'Abdullah ibn Yasar, with this chain. [[Al-Musnad (2/134) and Sunan al-Nasa'i (8/80).]]

Imam Ahmad also said: Ya'qub narrated to us, my father narrated to us, al-Walid ibn Kathir narrated to us, from Qatan ibn Wahb, from 'Uwaymir ibn al-Ajda', from one who narrated to him, from Salim ibn 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar, who said: 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar narrated to me that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Three, Allah has forbidden Paradise to them: the habitual drinker of wine, the one who disobeys his parents, and the dayyuth who allows impurity to persist in his household." [[Al-Musnad (2/69). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (8/147): "In it is a narrator who is unnamed."]]

Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said in his Musnad: Shu'ba narrated to us, a man from the family of Sahl ibn Hunayf narrated to me, from Muhammad ibn 'Ammar, from 'Ammar ibn Yasir, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The dayyuth will not enter Paradise." [[Musnad al-Tayalisi no. (642).]]

This is cited in support of the preceding hadiths.

Ibn Majah said: Hisham ibn 'Ammar narrated to us, Salam ibn Sawwar narrated to us, Kathir ibn Sulaym narrated to us, from al-Dahhak ibn Muzahim: I heard Anas ibn Malik say: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ [say] [[Addition from F, A.]]: "Whoever wishes to meet Allah pure and purified, let him marry free women."

There is weakness in its chain. [[Sunan Ibn Majah no. (1862). The weakness of its chain lies in Kathir ibn Sulaym, who is weak; and Salam is Ibn Sulayman ibn Sawwar al-Mada'ini. Ibn 'Adi said: "He has munkar (rejected) narrations," and al-'Uqayli said: "In his hadith there are munkar narrations." This was stated by al-Busiri in Misbah al-Zujajah (2/73).]]

Imam Abu Nasr Isma'il ibn Hammad al-Jawhari said in his book "al-Sihah fi al-Lugha": "The dayyuth is the qunadhi', who is one without jealousy (ghayra)." [[Al-Sihah (1/282).]]

As for the hadith narrated by Imam Abu 'Abd al-Rahman al-Nasa'i in the Book of "Marriage" of his Sunan: Muhammad ibn Isma'il ibn 'Ulayya informed us, from Yazid ibn Harun, from Hammad ibn Salama and others, from Harun ibn Ri'ab, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr - and 'Abd al-Karim, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr, from Ibn 'Abbas - 'Abd al-Karim raised it to Ibn 'Abbas, while Harun did not raise it - they both said: A man came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and said: "I have a wife [who is] [[Addition from F, A, and al-Nasa'i.]] among the people most beloved to me, and she does not withhold the hand of one who touches her." He said: "Divorce her." He said: "I cannot endure being without her." He said: "Then enjoy her." Then al-Nasa'i said: This hadith is not established; 'Abd al-Karim is not strong, Harun is more reliable than him, and he (Harun) transmitted it as a mursal, and he is trustworthy, and his hadith is closer to the correct version than the hadith of 'Abd al-Karim. [[Sunan al-Nasa'i (6/67).]]

I say: He is Ibn Abi al-Mukhariq al-Basri al-Mu'addib, a weak narrator among the Successors (tabi'un). Harun ibn Ri'ab contradicted him, and he is a trustworthy Successor from the narrators of Muslim, so his mursal narration is preferable, as al-Nasa'i said. However, al-Nasa'i narrated it in the Book of "Divorce" from Ishaq ibn Rahawayh, from al-Nadr ibn Shumayl, from Hammad ibn Salama, from Harun ibn Ri'ab, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, as a musnad report, and he mentioned it with this chain; its narrators are on the condition of Muslim. But after narrating it, al-Nasa'i said: "This is an error, and the correct version is mursal." [[Sunan al-Nasa'i (6/170).]] Others besides al-Nadr narrated it correctly.

Al-Nasa'i and Abu Dawud also narrated it from al-Husayn ibn Hurayth: al-Fadl ibn Musa informed us, al-Husayn ibn Waqid informed us, from 'Umara ibn Abi Hafsa, from 'Ikrima, from Ibn 'Abbas, from the Prophet ﷺ, and he mentioned it. This is a good chain. [[Sunan al-Nasa'i (6/169).]]

The scholars have differed regarding this hadith, between those who declared it weak, as mentioned earlier, citing al-Nasa'i, and as Imam Ahmad said: "It is a munkar hadith."

Ibn Qutayba said: He only meant that she is generous and does not refuse a beggar. al-Nasa'i related this in his Sunan from some of them, saying: "It was also said: 'a generous woman who gives.'" This was refuted on the grounds that if that were the intended meaning, he would have said: "she does not reject the hand of one who asks."

It was also said: the meaning is that her disposition does not turn away the hand of one who touches her, not that this actually happens from her and that she commits the immorality. For the Messenger of Allah ﷺ would not permit companionship with a woman described in this way. In that case her husband would be a cuckold (dayyuth), and the warning concerning that has already been mentioned. But since her disposition is such that there is no resistance or refusal toward anyone who desires her, if someone were to be alone with her, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ commanded him to separate from her. When he mentioned that he loved her, he permitted him to remain with her, because his love for her is certain, whereas the occurrence of immorality from her is merely presumed. Harm that is immediate is not to be imposed on account of a presumed future possibility. And Allah, glorified and exalted, knows best.

They said: As for when repentance has taken place, then marriage becomes lawful, as the Imam Abu Muhammad ibn Abi Hatim, may Allah have mercy on him, said:

Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj related to us, Abu Khalid related to us, from Ibn Abi Dhi'b, who said: I heard [Shu'bah] [added from F and A] the client (mawla) of Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with him, say: I heard Ibn 'Abbas, and a man asked him, saying: "I used to have intercourse with a woman, [doing] with her what Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, had forbidden me. Then Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, granted me repentance from that, and I wanted to marry her." Some people said: "Indeed, the adulterer does not marry except an adulteress." Ibn 'Abbas said: "This does not apply to this case. Marry her, and whatever sin there is, it is upon me."

Another group of scholars claimed that this verse is abrogated (mansukh). Ibn Abi Hatim said:

Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj related to us, Abu Khalid related to us, from Yahya ibn Sa'id, from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, who said: It was mentioned in his presence: ﴿The adulterer does not marry except an adulteress or a polytheist, and the adulteress is not married except by an adulterer or a polytheist﴾. He said: It used to be said that it was abrogated by the verse after it: ﴿And marry off the single among you﴾ [al-Nur: 32]. He said: It used to be said that "the single" (al-ayama) refers to the Muslims.

Likewise, Imam Abu 'Ubayd al-Qasim ibn Sallam narrated it in his book "al-Nasikh wal-Mansukh" from Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab. The Imam Abu 'Abd Allah Muhammad ibn Idris al-Shafi'i, may Allah have mercy on him, also explicitly stated this.

This noble verse explains the ruling on flogging the one who falsely accuses a *muhsanah* (a free, adult, chaste woman). If the accused is a man, the same applies: his accuser is also flogged, and there is no dispute among the scholars on this. However, if the accuser produces evidence (*bayyinah*) to prove the truth of what he said, the punishment (*hadd*) is waived from him. For this reason, God Most High said: ﴿Then they do not produce four witnesses, so flog them eighty lashes, and never accept their testimony. Those are the defiantly disobedient.﴾ Thus, when the accuser does not produce evidence for the truth of his claim, three rulings are obligatory upon him:

First: he is to be flogged eighty lashes.

Second: his testimony is to be rejected permanently. [[In manuscript F: "that"]]

Third: he is to be a transgressor (*fasiq*), not a person of integrity (*'adl*), neither in the sight of God nor in the sight of people.

Then God Most High said: ﴿Except those who repent after that and make amends, for indeed God is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾ The scholars differed regarding this exception (*istithna'*): does it refer only to the last sentence, so that repentance removes the transgression alone while the rejection of his testimony remains permanent even if he repents? Or does it refer to the second and third sentences? As for the flogging, it has passed and ended, whether he repents or persists, and there is no ruling attached to it after that, without any dispute. Imam Malik, al-Shafi'i and Ahmad ibn Hanbal held that if he repents, his testimony is accepted and the ruling of transgression is lifted from him. This was affirmed by Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab, the leader of the Successors (*tabi'un*), and by a group of the early generations (*salaf*) as well.

Abu Hanifah said: the exception refers only to the last sentence, so transgression is removed by repentance, but his testimony remains rejected forever. Among the early scholars who held this view were the judge Shurayh, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Makhul, and Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam. [[In manuscript F: "Jabir".]]

Al-Sha'bi and al-Dahhak said: his testimony is not accepted even if he repents, unless he confesses on himself that he uttered the slander (*buhtan*); in that case his testimony is accepted. And God knows best.

This noble verse provides relief for spouses and a way out for them. When one of them accuses his wife and it is difficult for him to produce evidence, he may invoke a mutual oath (li'an), as Allah, Exalted and Majestic, commanded. This is that he brings her before the ruler (imam) and makes a claim against her for what he accused her of. The judge then has him swear four testimonies by Allah in place of four witnesses, ﴿Indeed, he is surely among the truthful﴾, meaning in what he accused her of, namely adultery. ﴿And the fifth [oath is] that the curse of Allah be upon him if he is among the liars﴾. When he says this, she is separated from him by this very li'an according to al-Shafi'i and a great many scholars, and she is forbidden to him forever. He gives her her dowry. The punishment for adultery becomes due upon her, and it is averted from her only if she performs li'an, testifying four times by Allah that he is surely among the liars, meaning in what he accused her of. ﴿And the fifth [oath is] that the wrath of Allah be upon her if he is among the truthful﴾. Therefore He said: ﴿And it averts from her the punishment﴾,

meaning the legal penalty (hadd), ﴿that she testify four testimonies by Allah that he is surely among the liars. And the fifth [oath is] that the wrath of Allah be upon her if he is among the truthful﴾. He singled her out for wrath because it is generally the case that a man does not expose his family and accuse her of adultery unless he is truthful and excused, and she knows his truthfulness in what he accused her of. For this reason the fifth oath concerning her is that the wrath of Allah be upon her. And the one upon whom wrath falls is the one who knows the truth and then deviates from it.

Then He mentioned His kindness to His creatures and His compassion toward them, and that He legislated for them relief and a way out from the severe distress they may be in. He said: ﴿And were it not for the bounty of Allah upon you and His mercy﴾, meaning you would have been ruined, and many of your affairs would have been burdensome for you. ﴿And that Allah is Oft-Returning [to forgiveness]﴾, [meaning] toward His servants, even if that occurs after the swearing and the solemn oaths. ﴿Wise﴾ in what He legislates, commands, and forbids.

Traditions have come concerning the practice of this verse, the cause of its revelation, and the companion about whom it was revealed. Imam Ahmad said:

Yazid related to us, ʿAbbad ibn Mansur informed us, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: When the verse was revealed, ﴿And those who accuse chaste women and then do not produce four witnesses - lash them eighty lashes and do not accept from them testimony ever﴾, Saʿd ibn ʿUbadah, who was the chief of the Ansar, said: "Is it revealed like this, O Messenger of Allah?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O assembly of the Ansar, do you not hear what your chief is saying?" They said: "O Messenger of Allah, do not blame him, for he is a man of great jealousy. By Allah, he has never married a woman except as a virgin, and he has never divorced a wife of his. So a man among us dared to marry her, out of the intensity of his jealousy." Saʿd said: "By Allah, O Messenger of Allah, I know that it is the truth and that it is from Allah, but I am amazed: if I found a woman [with] a man between her thighs, I would not be permitted to disturb him or stir him until I bring four witnesses. By Allah, I will not bring them until he has finished his need." He said: They did not wait long before Hilal ibn Umayyah came - and he was one of the three whose repentance was accepted - and he came from his land at night. He found a man with his wife, and he saw with his own eyes and heard with his own ears, but he did not disturb them until morning. Then he went to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I came to my family at night and found a man with her. I saw with my own eyes and heard with my own ears." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) disliked what he had brought and it weighed heavily upon him. The Ansar gathered and said: "We have been tested with what Saʿd ibn ʿUbadah said. Now the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) will strike Hilal ibn Umayyah and invalidate his testimony among the Muslims." Hilal said: "By Allah, I hope that Allah will make a way out for me from it." Hilal said: "O Messenger of Allah, I see what has weighed heavily upon you from what I have brought, and Allah knows that I am truthful." By Allah, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was about to order that he be struck when Allah sent down revelation to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). When revelation came down upon him, they would recognize it in the change of his face. That is: they stopped speaking to him until he finished receiving the revelation. Then the verse was revealed: ﴿And those who accuse their wives and have no witnesses except themselves - then the testimony of one of them [is] four testimonies by Allah﴾, and so forth. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was relieved, and he said: "Rejoice, O Hilal, for Allah has made for you relief and a way out." Hilal said: "I had hoped for that from my Lord, Mighty and Majestic." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Send for her."

They sent for her, and she came. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited [the verses] to them both, reminded them, and informed them that the punishment of the Hereafter is more severe than the punishment of this world. Hilal said: "By Allah, O Messenger of Allah, I have spoken the truth about her." She said: "He lied." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Perform li'an between them." It was said to Hilal: "Testify." He testified four testimonies by Allah that he is surely among the truthful. When it came to the fifth, it was said to him: "O Hilal, fear Allah, for the punishment of this world is easier than the punishment of the Hereafter, and this is the [oath] that will make the punishment obligatory upon you." He said: "By Allah, Allah will not punish me for it, just as He did not flog me for it." He testified in the fifth that the curse of Allah be upon him if he was among the liars. Then it was said to her: "Testify four testimonies by Allah that he is surely among the liars." When it came to the fifth, it was said to her: "Fear Allah, for the punishment of this world is easier than the punishment of the Hereafter, and this is the [oath] that will make the punishment obligatory upon you." She hesitated for a moment, then said: "By Allah, I will not disgrace my people," and she testified in the fifth that the wrath of Allah be upon her if he was among the truthful. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) then separated them, and he decided that her child should not be attributed to a father, nor should her child be accused. Whoever accuses her or her child is liable to the legal penalty. He also decided that she had no right to a dwelling or maintenance from him, because they were separated without divorce and without the death of a spouse. And he said: "If she brings forth a child who is light-skinned, straight-haired, thin-legged, then he belongs to Hilal. But if she brings forth one who is dark-complexioned, curly-haired, with fat calves and full buttocks, then he is the one she was accused of [fathering]." She brought forth one who was dark-complexioned, curly-haired, with fat calves and full buttocks. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Had it not been for the oaths, there would have been a matter between me and her."

Ikrimah said: After that he became a governor of Egypt, and he was called [the son] of his mother and was not called [the son] of a father.

Abu Dawud related it from al-Hasan ibn ʿAli, from Yazid ibn Harun, with similar wording but in abridged form.

There are many corroborating reports for this tradition in the Sahih collections and elsewhere, from many routes. Among them is what al-Bukhari said: Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to me, Ibn Abi ʿAdi related to us, from Hisham ibn Hassan, Ikrimah related to me, from Ibn ʿAbbas, that Hilal ibn Umayyah accused his wife before the Prophet (ﷺ) with Shurayk ibn Sahma'. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Produce evidence, or the legal penalty will be upon your back." He said: "O Messenger of Allah, when one of us sees a man upon his wife, is he to go out seeking evidence?" The Prophet (ﷺ) kept saying: "Evidence, or else the legal penalty upon your back." Hilal said: "By Him who sent you with the truth, I am truthful, and Allah will surely send down what will clear my back from the penalty." Then Gabriel descended and revealed to him: ﴿And those who accuse their wives﴾, and he recited until he reached: ﴿if he is among the truthful﴾. The Prophet (ﷺ) then turned away and sent for them both. Hilal came and testified, while the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Allah knows that one of you two is a liar; will one of you repent?" Then she stood and testified. When she reached the fifth [oath], they stopped her and said: "It will make the punishment obligatory." Ibn ʿAbbas said: She hesitated and drew back until we thought she would retract. Then she said: "I will not disgrace my people for the rest of the day," and she proceeded. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Watch her. If she brings forth a child with dark eyes, full buttocks, and fat calves, then he belongs to Shurayk ibn Sahma'." She brought forth one such, and the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "Had it not been for what has already passed of the Book of Allah, there would have been a matter between me and her."

Al-Bukhari alone narrated it through this route, and he narrated it through other routes from Ibn ʿAbbas and others.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Mansur al-Ziyadi related to us, Yunus ibn Muhammad related to us, Salih - that is, Ibn ʿUmar - related to us, ʿAsim - meaning Ibn Kulayb - related to us, from his father, Ibn ʿAbbas related to me, who said: A man came to the Messenger of Allah, and he accused his wife of [adultery] with a man. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) disliked that, and he kept repeating it until Allah revealed: ﴿And those who accuse their wives and have no witnesses except themselves﴾, and he recited until he finished the two verses. He sent for them both and summoned them, and said: "Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has revealed [a ruling] concerning you two." He called the man and recited to him, and he testified four testimonies by Allah that he is surely among the truthful. Then he ordered that he be stopped at his mouth, and he admonished him, saying: "Everything is easier for him than the curse of Allah." Then he released him and [the man] said: ﴿that the curse of Allah be upon him if he is among the liars﴾. Then he called her and recited to her, and she testified four testimonies by Allah that he is surely among the liars. Then he ordered that she be stopped at her mouth and admonished her, and said: "Woe to you! Everything is easier than the wrath of Allah." Then he released her, and she said: ﴿that the wrath of Allah be upon her if he is among the truthful﴾. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Surely, by Allah, I will issue between you two a decisive judgment." He said: She gave birth, and I did not see a child in Medina who was more [closely] resembling him. He said: "If she brings forth a child like such-and-such, then he is such-and-such; and if she brings forth a child like such-and-such, then he is such-and-such." She brought forth a child resembling the one she had been accused of.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 24, verses 6–10 (part 2 of 2):

Imam Ahmad said: Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, 'Abd al-Malik ibn Abi Sulayman narrated to us, who said: I heard Sa'id ibn Jubayr say: I was asked about the two who perform li'an (mutual imprecation, the oath-sworn accusation between spouses), whether they are to be separated, during the governorship of Ibn al-Zubayr. I did not know what to answer, so I got up from my place and went to the house of Ibn 'Umar and said: "Abu 'Abd al-Rahman, are the two who perform li'an to be separated?" He said: "Subhan Allah! The first person to ask about this was so-and-so the son of so-and-so, who said: 'O Messenger of Allah, what do you think of a man who sees his wife committing an immoral act? If he speaks, he speaks of a grave matter, and if he remains silent, he remains silent over such a thing.' He (ﷺ) remained silent and did not answer him. Then, after that, the man came to him and said: 'The thing I asked you about has befallen me.' So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed these verses (in the Arabic, "الآية" in one manuscript) in Surah al-Nur: ﴿And those who accuse their wives...﴾ until He said: ﴿that the wrath of Allah be upon her if he is of the truthful.﴾ He began with the man, admonished him and reminded him, and informed him that the punishment of this world is lighter than the punishment of the Hereafter. The man said: 'By the One who sent you with the truth, I have not lied against you.' Then he turned to the woman, admonished and reminded her, and informed her that the punishment of this world is lighter than the punishment of the Hereafter. She said: 'By the One who sent you with the truth, he is surely lying.' He said: So he began with the man, and he testified four testimonies by Allah that he is surely of the truthful, and the fifth that the curse of Allah be upon him if he is of the liars. Then he turned to the woman, and she testified four testimonies by Allah that he is surely of the liars, and the fifth that the wrath of Allah be upon her if he is of the truthful. Then he separated them."

Al-Nasa'i narrated it in his Tafsir, from the hadith of 'Abd al-Malik ibn Abi Sulayman, with this chain. [Al-Musnad (2/19) and al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra, no. 11357.] Al-Bukhari and Muslim both narrated it in their Sahihs from the hadith of Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas. [Sahih al-Bukhari no. 5312 and Sahih Muslim no. 1493.]

Imam Ahmad said: Yahya ibn Hammad narrated to us, Abu 'Awana narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, from 'Alqama, from 'Abd Allah (Ibn Mas'ud), who said: We were sitting in the mosque on a Friday evening when a man from the Ansar said: "If one of us sees a man with his wife and kills him, you kill him; and if he speaks, you flog him; and if he remains silent, he remains silent out of rage?" By Allah, if I wake up well, I will surely ask the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He said: So he asked him, and said: "O Messenger of Allah, if one of us sees a man with his wife and kills him, you kill him; and if he speaks, you flog him; and if he remains silent, he remains silent out of rage?" Then he said: "O Allah, judge." He said: So the verse of li'an was revealed, and that man was the first to be tested by it.

Muslim alone narrated it, transmitting it through several routes from Sulayman ibn Mihran al-A'mash, with this chain. [Al-Musnad (1/421) and Sahih Muslim no. 1495.]

Imam Ahmad also said: Abu Kamil narrated to us: Ibrahim ibn Sa'd narrated to us, from Ibn Shihab, from Sahl ibn Sa'd, who said: 'Uwaymir came to 'Asim ibn 'Adi and said: "Ask the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): What do you say of a man who finds another man with his wife and kills him; will he be killed for him, or what should he do?" So 'Asim asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) disapproved of the questions. He said: Then 'Uwaymir met him and said: "What have you done?" He said: "What I have done! You have not brought me any good. I asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and he disapproved of the questions." 'Uwaymir said: "By Allah, I will certainly go to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and ask him myself." So he went to him and found that the revelation had come down concerning them both. He said: So he called for the two of them, and he had them perform li'an between them. 'Uwaymir said: "O Messenger of Allah, if I were to keep her, I would have lied about her." He said: So he divorced her before the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) commanded him to, and it became the sunnah of those who perform li'an. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Look at her: if she gives birth to a child who is dark-skinned, with very black eyes and large buttocks, then I think he is only truthful; and if she gives birth to one who is reddish, like a lizard, then I think he is only lying." Then she gave birth to him in the disliked description.

Al-Bukhari and Muslim narrated it in their Sahihs, and the rest of the compilers except al-Tirmidhi, through several routes, from al-Zuhri, with this chain. [Al-Musnad (5/334), Sahih al-Bukhari no. 4745, Sahih Muslim no. 1492, Sunan Abi Dawud no. 2245, Sunan al-Nasa'i (6/143) and Sunan Ibn Majah no. 2066.]

Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said: Ishaq ibn al-Dayf narrated to us, al-Nadr ibn Shumayl narrated to us, Yunus ibn Abi Ishaq narrated to us, from his father, from Zayd ibn Yuthay', from Hudhayfa, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to Abu Bakr: "If you saw a man with Umm Ruman, what would you do to him?" He said: "By Allah, I would do something evil to him." He said: "And you, O 'Umar?" He said: "By Allah, I would do... I would say: 'May Allah curse the weakest one (al-a'jaz), and he is wicked.'" He said: Then this was revealed: ﴿And those who accuse their wives, and have no witnesses except themselves...﴾

Then he said: We do not know anyone who transmitted it with a chain except al-Nadr ibn Shumayl, from Yunus ibn Abi Ishaq. Then he narrated it from the hadith of al-Thawri, from Abu Ishaq, from Zayd ibn Yuthay', as a mursal (a report lacking a companion in its chain). Allah knows best. [Musnad al-Bazzar no. 2237, "Kashf al-Astar." Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/74): "Its narrators are trustworthy (thiqat)."]

Al-Hafiz Abu Ya'la said: Muslim ibn Abi Muslim al-Jarmi narrated to us, Mukhallad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, from Hisham, from Ibn Sirin, from Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The first li'an in Islam was when Hilal ibn Umayya accused his wife with Shurayk ibn Sahma'. He brought it to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Four witnesses, or else a hadd (legal punishment) on your back." He said: "O Messenger of Allah, Allah knows that I am truthful, and surely Allah will reveal to you what will clear my back from the lashing." So Allah revealed the verse of li'an: ﴿And those who accuse their wives, and have no witnesses except themselves...﴾ to the end of the verse. He said: The Prophet (ﷺ) called him and said: "Swear by Allah that you are surely of the truthful regarding what you accused her of, of adultery." So he testified to that four times. Then he said to him at the fifth: "And the curse of Allah be upon you if you are of the liars regarding what you accused her of, of adultery." And he did so. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called her and said: "Stand up and testify by Allah that he is surely of the liars regarding what he accused you of, of adultery." So she testified to that four times. Then he said to her at the fifth: "And the wrath of Allah be upon you if he is of the truthful regarding what he accused you of, of adultery." She said... When it was the fourth or the fifth, she paused for a moment, so that they thought she would confess. Then she said: "I will not disgrace my people for the rest of the day." So she went on with her statement. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) separated them, and said: "Watch her: if she gives birth to one with curly hair, thin calves, then he belongs to Shurayk ibn Sahma'; and if she gives birth to one who is white, straight-haired, with weak eyes, then he belongs to Hilal ibn Umayya." She gave birth to one who was brown, curly-haired, with thin calves. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Had it not been for what Allah's Book revealed concerning them both, there would have been a matter between me and her."

[Musnad Abi Ya'la (5/207). Muslim also narrated it in his Sahih no. 1496 by way of Hisham, from Muhammad, with this chain.]

This noble verse provides relief for spouses and a way out for them. When one of them accuses his wife and it is difficult for him to produce evidence, he may invoke a mutual oath (li'an), as Allah, Exalted and Majestic, commanded. This is that he brings her before the ruler (imam) and makes a claim against her for what he accused her of. The judge then has him swear four testimonies by Allah in place of four witnesses, ﴿Indeed, he is surely among the truthful﴾, meaning in what he accused her of, namely adultery. ﴿And the fifth [oath is] that the curse of Allah be upon him if he is among the liars﴾. When he says this, she is separated from him by this very li'an according to al-Shafi'i and a great many scholars, and she is forbidden to him forever. He gives her her dowry. The punishment for adultery becomes due upon her, and it is averted from her only if she performs li'an, testifying four times by Allah that he is surely among the liars, meaning in what he accused her of. ﴿And the fifth [oath is] that the wrath of Allah be upon her if he is among the truthful﴾. Therefore He said: ﴿And it averts from her the punishment﴾,

meaning the legal penalty (hadd), ﴿that she testify four testimonies by Allah that he is surely among the liars. And the fifth [oath is] that the wrath of Allah be upon her if he is among the truthful﴾. He singled her out for wrath because it is generally the case that a man does not expose his family and accuse her of adultery unless he is truthful and excused, and she knows his truthfulness in what he accused her of. For this reason the fifth oath concerning her is that the wrath of Allah be upon her. And the one upon whom wrath falls is the one who knows the truth and then deviates from it.

Then He mentioned His kindness to His creatures and His compassion toward them, and that He legislated for them relief and a way out from the severe distress they may be in. He said: ﴿And were it not for the bounty of Allah upon you and His mercy﴾, meaning you would have been ruined, and many of your affairs would have been burdensome for you. ﴿And that Allah is Oft-Returning [to forgiveness]﴾, [meaning] toward His servants, even if that occurs after the swearing and the solemn oaths. ﴿Wise﴾ in what He legislates, commands, and forbids.

Traditions have come concerning the practice of this verse, the cause of its revelation, and the companion about whom it was revealed. Imam Ahmad said:

Yazid related to us, ʿAbbad ibn Mansur informed us, from ʿIkrimah, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: When the verse was revealed, ﴿And those who accuse chaste women and then do not produce four witnesses - lash them eighty lashes and do not accept from them testimony ever﴾, Saʿd ibn ʿUbadah, who was the chief of the Ansar, said: "Is it revealed like this, O Messenger of Allah?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "O assembly of the Ansar, do you not hear what your chief is saying?" They said: "O Messenger of Allah, do not blame him, for he is a man of great jealousy. By Allah, he has never married a woman except as a virgin, and he has never divorced a wife of his. So a man among us dared to marry her, out of the intensity of his jealousy." Saʿd said: "By Allah, O Messenger of Allah, I know that it is the truth and that it is from Allah, but I am amazed: if I found a woman [with] a man between her thighs, I would not be permitted to disturb him or stir him until I bring four witnesses. By Allah, I will not bring them until he has finished his need." He said: They did not wait long before Hilal ibn Umayyah came - and he was one of the three whose repentance was accepted - and he came from his land at night. He found a man with his wife, and he saw with his own eyes and heard with his own ears, but he did not disturb them until morning. Then he went to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I came to my family at night and found a man with her. I saw with my own eyes and heard with my own ears." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) disliked what he had brought and it weighed heavily upon him. The Ansar gathered and said: "We have been tested with what Saʿd ibn ʿUbadah said. Now the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) will strike Hilal ibn Umayyah and invalidate his testimony among the Muslims." Hilal said: "By Allah, I hope that Allah will make a way out for me from it." Hilal said: "O Messenger of Allah, I see what has weighed heavily upon you from what I have brought, and Allah knows that I am truthful." By Allah, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was about to order that he be struck when Allah sent down revelation to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). When revelation came down upon him, they would recognize it in the change of his face. That is: they stopped speaking to him until he finished receiving the revelation. Then the verse was revealed: ﴿And those who accuse their wives and have no witnesses except themselves - then the testimony of one of them [is] four testimonies by Allah﴾, and so forth. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was relieved, and he said: "Rejoice, O Hilal, for Allah has made for you relief and a way out." Hilal said: "I had hoped for that from my Lord, Mighty and Majestic." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Send for her."

They sent for her, and she came. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited [the verses] to them both, reminded them, and informed them that the punishment of the Hereafter is more severe than the punishment of this world. Hilal said: "By Allah, O Messenger of Allah, I have spoken the truth about her." She said: "He lied." The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Perform li'an between them." It was said to Hilal: "Testify." He testified four testimonies by Allah that he is surely among the truthful. When it came to the fifth, it was said to him: "O Hilal, fear Allah, for the punishment of this world is easier than the punishment of the Hereafter, and this is the [oath] that will make the punishment obligatory upon you." He said: "By Allah, Allah will not punish me for it, just as He did not flog me for it." He testified in the fifth that the curse of Allah be upon him if he was among the liars. Then it was said to her: "Testify four testimonies by Allah that he is surely among the liars." When it came to the fifth, it was said to her: "Fear Allah, for the punishment of this world is easier than the punishment of the Hereafter, and this is the [oath] that will make the punishment obligatory upon you." She hesitated for a moment, then said: "By Allah, I will not disgrace my people," and she testified in the fifth that the wrath of Allah be upon her if he was among the truthful. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) then separated them, and he decided that her child should not be attributed to a father, nor should her child be accused. Whoever accuses her or her child is liable to the legal penalty. He also decided that she had no right to a dwelling or maintenance from him, because they were separated without divorce and without the death of a spouse. And he said: "If she brings forth a child who is light-skinned, straight-haired, thin-legged, then he belongs to Hilal. But if she brings forth one who is dark-complexioned, curly-haired, with fat calves and full buttocks, then he is the one she was accused of [fathering]." She brought forth one who was dark-complexioned, curly-haired, with fat calves and full buttocks. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Had it not been for the oaths, there would have been a matter between me and her."

Ikrimah said: After that he became a governor of Egypt, and he was called [the son] of his mother and was not called [the son] of a father.
