Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ahmad ibn Mansur al-Ziyadi related to us, Yunus ibn Muhammad related to us, Salih - that is, Ibn ʿUmar - related to us, ʿAsim - meaning Ibn Kulayb - related to us, from his father, Ibn ʿAbbas related to me, who said: A man came to the Messenger of Allah, and he accused his wife of [adultery] with a man. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) disliked that, and he kept repeating it until Allah revealed: ﴿And those who accuse their wives and have no witnesses except themselves﴾, and he recited until he finished the two verses. He sent for them both and summoned them, and said: "Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has revealed [a ruling] concerning you two." He called the man and recited to him, and he testified four testimonies by Allah that he is surely among the truthful. Then he ordered that he be stopped at his mouth, and he admonished him, saying: "Everything is easier for him than the curse of Allah." Then he released him and [the man] said: ﴿that the curse of Allah be upon him if he is among the liars﴾. Then he called her and recited to her, and she testified four testimonies by Allah that he is surely among the liars. Then he ordered that she be stopped at her mouth and admonished her, and said: "Woe to you! Everything is easier than the wrath of Allah." Then he released her, and she said: ﴿that the wrath of Allah be upon her if he is among the truthful﴾. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Surely, by Allah, I will issue between you two a decisive judgment." He said: She gave birth, and I did not see a child in Medina who was more [closely] resembling him. He said: "If she brings forth a child like such-and-such, then he is such-and-such; and if she brings forth a child like such-and-such, then he is such-and-such." She brought forth a child resembling the one she had been accused of.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 24, verses 6–10 (part 2 of 2):

Imam Ahmad said: Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, 'Abd al-Malik ibn Abi Sulayman narrated to us, who said: I heard Sa'id ibn Jubayr say: I was asked about the two who perform li'an (mutual imprecation, the oath-sworn accusation between spouses), whether they are to be separated, during the governorship of Ibn al-Zubayr. I did not know what to answer, so I got up from my place and went to the house of Ibn 'Umar and said: "Abu 'Abd al-Rahman, are the two who perform li'an to be separated?" He said: "Subhan Allah! The first person to ask about this was so-and-so the son of so-and-so, who said: 'O Messenger of Allah, what do you think of a man who sees his wife committing an immoral act? If he speaks, he speaks of a grave matter, and if he remains silent, he remains silent over such a thing.' He (ﷺ) remained silent and did not answer him. Then, after that, the man came to him and said: 'The thing I asked you about has befallen me.' So Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, revealed these verses (in the Arabic, "الآية" in one manuscript) in Surah al-Nur: ﴿And those who accuse their wives...﴾ until He said: ﴿that the wrath of Allah be upon her if he is of the truthful.﴾ He began with the man, admonished him and reminded him, and informed him that the punishment of this world is lighter than the punishment of the Hereafter. The man said: 'By the One who sent you with the truth, I have not lied against you.' Then he turned to the woman, admonished and reminded her, and informed her that the punishment of this world is lighter than the punishment of the Hereafter. She said: 'By the One who sent you with the truth, he is surely lying.' He said: So he began with the man, and he testified four testimonies by Allah that he is surely of the truthful, and the fifth that the curse of Allah be upon him if he is of the liars. Then he turned to the woman, and she testified four testimonies by Allah that he is surely of the liars, and the fifth that the wrath of Allah be upon her if he is of the truthful. Then he separated them."

Al-Nasa'i narrated it in his Tafsir, from the hadith of 'Abd al-Malik ibn Abi Sulayman, with this chain. [Al-Musnad (2/19) and al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra, no. 11357.] Al-Bukhari and Muslim both narrated it in their Sahihs from the hadith of Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas. [Sahih al-Bukhari no. 5312 and Sahih Muslim no. 1493.]

Imam Ahmad said: Yahya ibn Hammad narrated to us, Abu 'Awana narrated to us, from al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, from 'Alqama, from 'Abd Allah (Ibn Mas'ud), who said: We were sitting in the mosque on a Friday evening when a man from the Ansar said: "If one of us sees a man with his wife and kills him, you kill him; and if he speaks, you flog him; and if he remains silent, he remains silent out of rage?" By Allah, if I wake up well, I will surely ask the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). He said: So he asked him, and said: "O Messenger of Allah, if one of us sees a man with his wife and kills him, you kill him; and if he speaks, you flog him; and if he remains silent, he remains silent out of rage?" Then he said: "O Allah, judge." He said: So the verse of li'an was revealed, and that man was the first to be tested by it.

Muslim alone narrated it, transmitting it through several routes from Sulayman ibn Mihran al-A'mash, with this chain. [Al-Musnad (1/421) and Sahih Muslim no. 1495.]

Imam Ahmad also said: Abu Kamil narrated to us: Ibrahim ibn Sa'd narrated to us, from Ibn Shihab, from Sahl ibn Sa'd, who said: 'Uwaymir came to 'Asim ibn 'Adi and said: "Ask the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ): What do you say of a man who finds another man with his wife and kills him; will he be killed for him, or what should he do?" So 'Asim asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) disapproved of the questions. He said: Then 'Uwaymir met him and said: "What have you done?" He said: "What I have done! You have not brought me any good. I asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and he disapproved of the questions." 'Uwaymir said: "By Allah, I will certainly go to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and ask him myself." So he went to him and found that the revelation had come down concerning them both. He said: So he called for the two of them, and he had them perform li'an between them. 'Uwaymir said: "O Messenger of Allah, if I were to keep her, I would have lied about her." He said: So he divorced her before the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) commanded him to, and it became the sunnah of those who perform li'an. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Look at her: if she gives birth to a child who is dark-skinned, with very black eyes and large buttocks, then I think he is only truthful; and if she gives birth to one who is reddish, like a lizard, then I think he is only lying." Then she gave birth to him in the disliked description.

Al-Bukhari and Muslim narrated it in their Sahihs, and the rest of the compilers except al-Tirmidhi, through several routes, from al-Zuhri, with this chain. [Al-Musnad (5/334), Sahih al-Bukhari no. 4745, Sahih Muslim no. 1492, Sunan Abi Dawud no. 2245, Sunan al-Nasa'i (6/143) and Sunan Ibn Majah no. 2066.]

Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said: Ishaq ibn al-Dayf narrated to us, al-Nadr ibn Shumayl narrated to us, Yunus ibn Abi Ishaq narrated to us, from his father, from Zayd ibn Yuthay', from Hudhayfa, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to Abu Bakr: "If you saw a man with Umm Ruman, what would you do to him?" He said: "By Allah, I would do something evil to him." He said: "And you, O 'Umar?" He said: "By Allah, I would do... I would say: 'May Allah curse the weakest one (al-a'jaz), and he is wicked.'" He said: Then this was revealed: ﴿And those who accuse their wives, and have no witnesses except themselves...﴾

Then he said: We do not know anyone who transmitted it with a chain except al-Nadr ibn Shumayl, from Yunus ibn Abi Ishaq. Then he narrated it from the hadith of al-Thawri, from Abu Ishaq, from Zayd ibn Yuthay', as a mursal (a report lacking a companion in its chain). Allah knows best. [Musnad al-Bazzar no. 2237, "Kashf al-Astar." Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/74): "Its narrators are trustworthy (thiqat)."]

Al-Hafiz Abu Ya'la said: Muslim ibn Abi Muslim al-Jarmi narrated to us, Mukhallad ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, from Hisham, from Ibn Sirin, from Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The first li'an in Islam was when Hilal ibn Umayya accused his wife with Shurayk ibn Sahma'. He brought it to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Four witnesses, or else a hadd (legal punishment) on your back." He said: "O Messenger of Allah, Allah knows that I am truthful, and surely Allah will reveal to you what will clear my back from the lashing." So Allah revealed the verse of li'an: ﴿And those who accuse their wives, and have no witnesses except themselves...﴾ to the end of the verse. He said: The Prophet (ﷺ) called him and said: "Swear by Allah that you are surely of the truthful regarding what you accused her of, of adultery." So he testified to that four times. Then he said to him at the fifth: "And the curse of Allah be upon you if you are of the liars regarding what you accused her of, of adultery." And he did so. Then the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) called her and said: "Stand up and testify by Allah that he is surely of the liars regarding what he accused you of, of adultery." So she testified to that four times. Then he said to her at the fifth: "And the wrath of Allah be upon you if he is of the truthful regarding what he accused you of, of adultery." She said... When it was the fourth or the fifth, she paused for a moment, so that they thought she would confess. Then she said: "I will not disgrace my people for the rest of the day." So she went on with her statement. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) separated them, and said: "Watch her: if she gives birth to one with curly hair, thin calves, then he belongs to Shurayk ibn Sahma'; and if she gives birth to one who is white, straight-haired, with weak eyes, then he belongs to Hilal ibn Umayya." She gave birth to one who was brown, curly-haired, with thin calves. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Had it not been for what Allah's Book revealed concerning them both, there would have been a matter between me and her."

[Musnad Abi Ya'la (5/207). Muslim also narrated it in his Sahih no. 1496 by way of Hisham, from Muhammad, with this chain.]

This passage, that is, these ten verses, was all revealed concerning ʿĀʾishah, the Mother of the Believers, may Allah be pleased with her, when the people of the slander (Ahl al-Ifk) and the calumny from among the hypocrites accused her of what they said, pure falsehood and a fabrication that Allah, exalted is His majesty, was jealous over, on behalf of Himself and His Prophet, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed her innocence, safeguarding the honor of the Messenger, upon him be the best of prayers and peace [[In A: "may Allah bless him and grant him peace."]]. He said: ﴿Indeed, those who brought the slander are a group among you﴾, meaning: a group of you, that is, not one or two but a band. The leader in this calumny was ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, the chief of the hypocrites, for he would gather it and spread it, until it entered the minds of some of the Muslims, so they spoke of it, and others among them permitted it. The matter remained so for nearly a month, until the Qur'an was revealed. The full account is in the authentic hadiths.

Imam Ahmad said:

Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Ma'mar narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, who said:

Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib, Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, ʿAlqamah ibn Waqqas, and ʿUbayd Allah ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUtbah ibn Mas'ud informed me, concerning the account of ʿĀʾishah, the wife of the Prophet (ﷺ), when the people of the slander said what they said, and Allah cleared her. Each of them narrated to me a portion of her account, and some of them were more retentive of her narration than others and more precise in relating it. I have retained from each of them the narration he related to me, and some of their accounts confirm one another:

They mentioned that ʿĀʾishah, the wife of the Prophet (ﷺ), said:

"When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) intended to set out on a journey, he would draw lots among his wives, and whichever of them the lot fell upon, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would take her with him." ʿĀʾishah said:

"He drew lots among us during a military campaign he undertook, and my lot came out, so I went out with the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ). This was after the veil had been revealed. I would be carried in my howdah and lowered within it along our journey. When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) finished his campaign and turned back, and we drew near Madinah, he announced the departure one night, so I got up when they announced the departure, and I walked until I had passed the army. When I had finished my need, I returned to the riding-saddle and touched my chest, and behold, my necklace of Zafar onyx had broken, so I turned back and searched for my necklace, and its search detained me.

"Meanwhile, the men who used to load my howdah came and lifted it and fastened it onto my camel, which I used to ride, thinking that I was inside it." She said:

"Women in those days were light; they had not grown heavy, nor had flesh covered them. They only ate a small morsel of food." She said:

"So the people did not notice the weight of the howdah when they loaded and lifted it. I was a young girl of tender age. So they sent off the camel and went on. I found my necklace after the army had moved on, so I came to their camping place, and there was no one there to call or to answer. So I headed to my place where I had been, thinking that the people would miss me and return for me.

"While I was sitting in my place, my eyes overcame me and I slept. Safwan ibn al-Mu'attal al-Sulami, then al-Dhakwani, had stayed behind the army. He set out in the last part of the night and reached my place at morning, and he saw the shape of a sleeping person. He came to me and recognized me when he saw me, for he had seen me before the veil was ordained over me. I awoke at his saying 'Inna lillah' when he recognized me, so I covered my face with my outer garment. By Allah, he did not speak a single word to me, and I did not hear from him a word other than his 'Inna lillah', until he made his mount kneel, and stepped on its forelegs, and I mounted it. He set off leading the mount with me until we reached the army after they had halted in the heat of midday.

"So whoever was destroyed was destroyed concerning me, and the one who took the greatest part in it was ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul."

"I came to Madinah and fell ill for a month after we arrived, while the people were spreading the talk of the people of the slander, and I was unaware of any of it. What troubled me during my illness was that I did not recognize from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) the tenderness I used to see from him when I was ill. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would only enter, greet, and then say: 'How are you?' That troubled me, and I was unaware of the evil. Until I went out after I had recovered, along with Umm Mistah, toward al-Manasi' — which was our place for relieving ourselves — and we did not go out except at night to night, and that was before we had made latrines near our houses. Our custom was the custom of the early Arabs regarding relieving oneself, and we were troubled by the latrines when we made them in our houses."

"So I set out, I and Umm Mistah — she being the daughter of Abu Ruhm ibn al-Muttalib ibn ʿAbd Manaf, and her mother was the daughter of Sakhr ibn ʿAmir, the maternal aunt of Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, and her son was Mistah ibn Uthathah ibn ʿAbbad ibn al-Muttalib. We came back toward my house when we had finished our business, and Umm Mistah tripped in her garment, and she said: 'May Mistah perish!'

"I said to her: 'What an evil thing you have said! Will you curse a man who witnessed Badr?'

"She said: 'O you, did you not hear what he said?'

"I said: 'And what did he say?'

"So she told me the saying of the people of the slander, and my illness increased upon my illness.

"When I returned to my house, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) entered upon me, greeted, and then said: 'How are you?'

"I said: 'Will you permit me to go to my parents?' — she said: 'I wanted at that time to ascertain the news from them' — so the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) permitted me. I came to my parents and said to my mother: 'O mother, what are the people talking about?'

"She said: 'O daughter, ease your mind. By Allah, rarely is there a woman who is beautiful, with a husband who loves her, and who has co-wives, but that they do not multiply talk about her.'

"I said: 'Glory be to Allah! Have the people really spoken of this?'

"She said: 'So I wept that night until morning, my tears would not dry up, and I did not close my eyes in sleep. Then I woke up weeping.'

"The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) summoned ʿAli and Usamah ibn Zayd when the revelation was delayed, consulting them about parting from his family." She said:

"As for Usamah ibn Zayd, he advised the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) according to what he knew of the innocence of his family and the affection he held in his heart for him. He said: 'O Messenger of Allah, they are your family, and we know nothing but good.'

"As for ʿAli ibn Abi Talib, he said: 'Allah has not constricted you, and women other than her are many. But if you ask the slave girl, she will tell you the truth.'"

She said: "So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) summoned Barirah and said: 'O Barirah, have you seen anything from ʿĀʾishah that causes you doubt?'

"Barirah said to him: 'By Him who sent you with the truth, if I have seen anything in her that I could find fault with, it is no more than that she is a young girl of tender age, who falls asleep over her family's dough, and then a domestic sheep comes and eats it.'"

"The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) stood up and sought to be excused from ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul." She said:

"The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said while he was on the pulpit: 'O assembly of Muslims, who will excuse me from a man whose harm has reached me concerning my household? By Allah, I know nothing of my family but good. They have mentioned a man, and I know nothing of him but good, and he never entered upon my family except in my company.'"

Sa'd ibn Mu'adh al-Ansari stood up and said: "I will excuse you from him, O Messenger of Allah. If he is from Aws, we will strike off his neck; and if he is from our brothers of Khazraj, you command us and we will do your command."

She said: "Then Sa'd ibn ʿUbadah stood up — and he was the chief of Khazraj, a righteous man, but zealous pride had overcome him — and he said to Sa'd ibn Mu'adh: 'By Allah's life, you will not kill him, nor are you able to kill him.'

"Then Usayd ibn Hudayr — and he was the cousin of Sa'd ibn Mu'adh — stood up and said to Sa'd ibn ʿUbadah: 'You lie! By Allah's life, we will certainly kill him. You are a hypocrite who argues on behalf of the hypocrites.'

"So the two clans, Aws and Khazraj, stirred up and nearly came to fighting, while the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was standing on the pulpit. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not cease calming them until they fell silent, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) fell silent." She said:

"I wept that entire day, my tears would not dry up, and I did not close my eyes in sleep, while my parents thought that weeping would split my liver."

She said: "While they were both sitting with me and I was weeping, a woman from the Ansar asked permission to enter upon me, so I permitted her, and she sat weeping with me. While we were in that state, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) entered upon us, greeted, and sat down." She said: "He had not sat with me since the saying was spread about me, and he had remained a month without any revelation being sent down to him concerning my affair." She said:

"The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recited the tashahhud when he sat down, then said: 'As to what follows, O ʿĀʾishah, I have received word of such and such about you. If you are innocent, Allah will surely clear you; and if you have committed a sin, then seek forgiveness from Allah and repent to Him, for when a servant confesses a sin and then repents, Allah turns to him in forgiveness.'"

She said: "When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had finished his speech, my tears dried up until I could not feel even a drop of them. So I said to my father: 'Answer the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) on my behalf.'

"He said: 'By Allah, I do not know what to say to the Messenger.'

"I said to my mother: 'Answer the Messenger of Allah on my behalf.'

"She said: 'By Allah, I do not know what to say to the Messenger of Allah.'"

She said: "So I said — and I was a young girl of tender age, not memorizing much of the Qur'an: 'Indeed, by Allah, I know that you have heard this, until it has settled in your hearts and you have believed it. If I say to you that I am innocent — and Allah knows that I am innocent — you will not believe me. And if I confess to you a matter, while Allah, Mighty and Majestic, knows that I am innocent, you will believe me. By Allah, I find no example for myself and for you except what Abu Yusuf said: ﴿So patience is most fitting, and Allah is the One whose help is sought against what you describe﴾ [Yusuf 12:18].'"

She said: "Then I turned over and lay down on my bed." She said: "By Allah, at that time I knew that I was innocent, and that Allah would clear me by my innocence. But by Allah, I never thought that a revelation would be sent down concerning my affair that would be recited, and my affair was too insignificant in my own eyes for Allah to speak of it with a matter to be recited. Rather, I hoped that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would see a dream in his sleep by which Allah would clear me."

She said: "By Allah, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had not moved from his place, nor had anyone left the household, when Allah sent down revelation upon His Prophet. He was seized by the distress that he used to feel at the time of revelation, until sweat poured from him like pearls on a winter day, because of the weight of the word that was being revealed to him."

She said: "When the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) recovered from it, smiling, the first word he spoke was: 'Rejoice, O ʿĀʾishah! As for Allah, He has cleared you.'

"My mother said to me: 'Stand up and go to him.'

"I said: 'By Allah, I will not stand up to him, and I will praise none but Allah, Mighty and Majestic. It is He who sent down my innocence.' And Allah, Mighty and Majestic, sent down..."

[She said: "...a beautiful woman, with a husband who loves her, having co-wives who envied her, and things were said about her, though he did not reach from her what he reached from me." I said: "Did my father know of it?" She said: "Yes." I said: "And the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)?" She said: "Yes, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)." So I wept, and Abu Bakr heard my voice while he was above the house reciting, so he came down and said to my mother: "What is the matter with her?" She said: "What was mentioned about her has reached her." So his eyes overflowed, and he said: "I adjure you, O daughter, to return to your house," so I returned. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) came to my house and asked about me my servant. She said: "By Allah, I know nothing of her but that she used to sleep until a sheep came and ate her dough — or..."]

...[her dough]... and one of his companions rebuked her, saying: "Tell the Messenger of Allah ﷺ the truth," until they made her a target of (accusation) because of it. She said: "Glory be to Allah! By Allah, I know nothing about her except what a goldsmith knows about red gold ingots." (ʿĀʾishah said:) The matter reached the man who had been accused, and he said: "Glory be to Allah! By Allah, I have never uncovered the veil of any woman, ever," and he was killed as a martyr in the way of Allah.

She said: My parents came to me and remained with me until the Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered upon me after he had prayed the ʿAsr prayer. Then he entered while my parents were on either side of me, on my right and on my left. He praised Allah and extolled Him, then said: "To proceed, O ʿĀʾishah: if you have committed an evil or wronged (someone), then repent to Allah, for Allah accepts repentance from His servants."

She said: A woman from the Ansar had come and was sitting at the door. I said: "Are you not ashamed of this woman, that she should mention something?" The Messenger of Allah ﷺ then admonished (the people). I turned to my father and said to him: "Answer him!" He said: "What should I say?" I turned to my mother and said: "Answer him!" She said: "What should I say?" When they did not answer him, I recited the tashahhud, praised Allah and extolled Him as is fitting for Him, then said: "To proceed: by Allah, if I tell you that I did not do it, and Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, bears witness that I am truthful, that will not benefit me with you; you have spoken about it and it has taken hold of your hearts. And if I say, 'I have done it,' and Allah knows that I have not done it, you will surely say, 'She has brought this upon herself.' By Allah, I cannot find for myself or for you an example, except (that of) the father of Yusuf when he said: ﴿So patience is beautiful, and Allah is the One whose help is sought against what you describe﴾ [Yusuf: 18]." (She said:) I had searched for the name of Yaʿqub but could not recall it.

Allah immediately sent down (revelation) upon His Messenger ﷺ, and then we fell silent, and it was lifted from him. I could see the joy in his face as he wiped his forehead and said: "Rejoice, O ʿĀʾishah, for Allah has revealed your innocence." She said: I was at my most angry, and my parents said to me: "Get up and go to him." I said: "No, by Allah, I will not get up to him, nor will I praise him, nor will I praise you two; rather I praise Allah, who revealed my innocence. You heard it and you did not deny it or change it."

ʿĀʾishah used to say: As for Zaynab bint Jahsh, Allah protected her through her religion, so she said nothing but good. As for her sister Hamnah bint Jahsh, she was destroyed among those who were destroyed. The ones who spoke about it were Mistah and Hassan ibn Thabit. As for the hypocrite ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, he was the one who spread it and gathered (the reports), and he was the one who took the lead in it, together with Hamnah.

She said: Abu Bakr swore that he would never again benefit Mistah with any benefit. Then Allah revealed: ﴿And let not those of virtue and wealth among you swear not to give﴾ until the end of the verse, meaning Abu Bakr, ﴿and wealth [to] give to the near of kin and the needy﴾, meaning Mistah, up to His saying: ﴿Do you not like that Allah should forgive you? And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [al-Nur: 22]. Abu Bakr said: "Yes, by Allah, our Lord! We indeed love that You forgive us," and he returned to giving him (support) as he used to do.

Thus al-Bukhari narrated it through this route, in suspended form with a categorical wording [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4757], from Abu Usamah Hammad ibn Usamah, one of the trustworthy imams. Ibn Jarir also narrated it in his Tafsir, from Sufyan ibn Waki, from Abu Usamah, in a longer version like it or similar to it [Tafsir al-Tabari (18/74)]. Al-Hafiz Ibn Dizil narrated it in his juz' no. 1 through the route of Isma'il ibn Abi Uways, from his father, from Hisham ibn ʿUrwah, from his father, from ʿĀʾishah, similar to it. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it from Abu Saʿid al-Ashajj, from Abu Usamah, a part of it.

Imam Ahmad said: Hushaym narrated to us, Umar [in A: "Amr"] ibn Abi Salamah informed us, from his father, from ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: When my innocence was revealed from the heavens, the Prophet ﷺ came to me and informed me of it. I said: "We praise Allah, not you" [al-Musnad (6/30)].

Imam Ahmad also said: Ibn Abi ʿAdi narrated to me, from Muhammad ibn Ishaq, from ʿAbd Allah ibn Abi Bakr, from ʿAmrah, from ʿĀʾishah, who said: When my innocence was revealed, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ stood up, mentioned that, and recited the Qur'an. When (the revelation) came down, he ordered that two men and a woman be punished with their prescribed penalty [al-Musnad (6/35); Sunan Abi Dawud no. 4474; Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 3181; Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra no. 7351; Sunan Ibn Majah no. 2567].

The people of the four Sunan collections narrated it, and al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a hasan hadith." In Abu Dawud the names are given: Hassan ibn Thabit, Mistah ibn Uthathah, and Hamnah bint Jahsh.

These are multiple routes from Umm al-Mu'minin ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, found in the Musnads, the Sahih collections, the Sunan and others.

It has also been narrated from the hadith of her mother, Umm Ruman, may Allah be pleased with her. Imam Ahmad said: ʿAli ibn ʿAsim narrated to us, Husayn informed us, from Abu Wa'il, from Masruq, from Umm Ruman, who said: While I was with ʿĀʾishah, a woman from the Ansar entered upon her and said: "May Allah do such-and-such to her son!" ʿĀʾishah said: "Why?" She said: "He was among those who spread the report." ʿĀʾishah said: "And what report?" She said: "Such-and-such." She said: "Has that reached the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?" She said: "Yes." "And has it reached Abu Bakr?" She said: "Yes." So ʿĀʾishah fainted, and she did not regain consciousness until she had a fever with shivering. She said: I got up and covered her. She said: The Prophet ﷺ came and said: "What is the matter with this one?" I said: "O Messenger of Allah, she has been seized by a fever with shivering." He said: "Perhaps it is because of a report you have been told about." She said: Then ʿĀʾishah sat up for him and said: "By Allah, if I swear to you, you will not believe me, and if I offer an excuse to you, you will not accept my excuse. My situation and yours is like that of Yaʿqub and his sons: ﴿And Allah is the One whose help is sought against what you describe﴾ [Yusuf: 18]." She said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ went out, and Allah revealed her innocence. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ returned with Abu Bakr accompanying him, and he entered and said: "O ʿĀʾishah, indeed Allah, the Exalted, has revealed your innocence." She said: "Praise be to Allah, not to you." Abu Bakr said to her: "Do you say this to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ?" She said: "Yes." She said: Among those who spread this report was a man whom Abu Bakr used to support, so Abu Bakr swore that he would not give him anything. Then Allah revealed: ﴿And let not those of virtue and wealth among you swear not to give﴾ until the end of the verse [al-Nur: 22]. Abu Bakr said: "Yes," and he resumed giving.

Al-Bukhari alone narrated it, without Muslim, through the route of Husayn [al-Musnad (6/367); Sahih al-Bukhari no. 4751]. Al-Bukhari also narrated it from Musa ibn Isma'il, from Abu ʿAwanah, and from Muhammad ibn Salam, from Muhammad ibn Fudayl, both of them from Husayn, with the same chain [Sahih al-Bukhari no. 4143 through the narration of Musa ibn Isma'il, and no. 3388 through the narration of Muhammad ibn Salam]. In the wording of Abu ʿAwanah: "Umm Ruman narrated to me." This is explicit evidence that Masruq heard from her. A group of the hadith memorizers denied this, among them al-Khatib al-Baghdadi, because historians have mentioned that she died during the lifetime of the Prophet ﷺ. Al-Khatib said: Masruq used to narrate it as a mursal report, saying: "Umm Ruman was asked," and then he would continue the narration, so perhaps some of them wrote "sualat" (was asked) with an alif, and the narrator understood it as "sa'alat" (she asked), and thus considered it connected. Al-Khatib said: "Al-Bukhari narrated it in this way too, and its defect did not become apparent to him." Thus he said, and Allah knows best.

His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who came with the slander﴾, that is, with the lie, the calumny and the fabrication, ﴿are a group among you﴾, that is, a company from among you, ﴿do not consider it bad for you﴾, that is, O family of Abu Bakr, ﴿rather it is good for you﴾, that is, in this world and the Hereafter: a true tongue in this world and an elevation of ranks in the Hereafter, and a display of honor for them through Allah's care for ʿĀʾishah, Mother of the Believers, in that Allah, the Exalted, revealed her innocence in the Great Qur'an, ﴿which falsehood cannot approach from before it or behind it, a revelation from the Wise, Praiseworthy﴾ [Fussilat: 42]. For this reason, when Ibn ʿAbbas, may Allah be pleased with him, entered upon her while she was in her last illness, he said to her: "Rejoice, for you are the wife of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and he loved you, and he did not marry a virgin other than you, and your innocence was revealed from the heavens" [Sahih al-Bukhari no. 4753].

Ibn Jarir said in his Tafsir: Muhammad ibn ʿUthman al-Wasiti narrated to me, Ja'far ibn ʿAwn narrated to us, from al-Mu'alla ibn ʿIrfan, from Muhammad ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn Jahsh, who said: ʿĀʾishah and Zaynab, may Allah be pleased with them both, boasted, and Zaynab said: "I am the one whose marriage was revealed from the heavens." He said: ʿĀʾishah said: "I am the one whose innocence was revealed in His Book, when Ibn al-Mu'attal carried me on the mount." Zaynab said to her: "O ʿĀʾishah, what did you say when you mounted it?" She said: "I said: 'Allah is sufficient for me, and He is the best Disposer of affairs.'" She said: "You said the words of the believers" [Tafsir al-Tabari (18/70)].

* *

His saying: ﴿For every person among them is what he has earned of sin﴾, that is, for every one who spoke about this matter and accused Umm al-Mu'minin ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, of something of indecency, there is a great share of punishment.

﴿And the one who took upon himself the greater part thereof﴾ — it was said: he initiated it. And it was said: he is the one who gathered it, sought it out, spread it and disseminated it. ﴿For him is a great punishment﴾, that is, for that.

Then the majority hold that what is meant by this is only ʿAbd Allah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, may Allah curse him and disgrace him, who is the one whose identity was explicitly mentioned in the hadith above. This was said by Mujahid and others.

It was also said: rather, what is meant is Hassan ibn Thabit. This is a rare opinion. Had it not been that what occurs in Sahih al-Bukhari may seem to indicate this, there would be no great benefit in mentioning it, for he was among the Companions who had virtues, merits and accomplishments, and the best of his qualities is that he used to defend the Messenger of Allah ﷺ with his poetry. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: "Satirize them, and Jibril is with you."

Al-Aʿmash narrated, from Abu al-Duha, from Masruq, who said: I was with ʿĀʾishah, may Allah be pleased with her, when Hassan ibn Thabit entered. She ordered that a cushion be placed for him. When he left, I said to ʿĀʾishah: "Why do you do this with him?" meaning: he enters upon you. In another narration, it was said to her: "Do you permit this one to enter upon you, when Allah has said: ﴿And the one who took upon himself the greater part thereof among them, for him is a great punishment﴾?" She said: "And what punishment is greater than blindness?" — and his sight had gone — "perhaps Allah will make that the great punishment." Then she said: "Indeed he used to defend the Messenger of Allah ﷺ."

In another narration, when he entered upon her, he recited to her a poem praising her, saying:

*A chaste, dignified woman, not suspected of any doubt,*
*She wakes up free from the flesh of the heedless.*

She said: "As for you, you are not like that." In another narration: "But you are not like that" [Sahih al-Bukhari no. 4146: Bishr ibn Khalid narrated to us, from Muhammad ibn Ja'far, from Shu'bah, from al-A'mash, with it].

Ibn Jarir said: Al-Hasan ibn Qaza'a narrated to us, Salamah ibn 'Alqamah narrated to us, Dawud narrated to us, from 'Amir, from 'A'ishah, that she said: "I have never heard anything more beautiful than the poetry of Hassan, and whenever I recited it, I hoped Paradise for him. [He said] to Abu Sufyan, meaning Ibn [al-Harith] [[added from F, A.]] ibn 'Abd al-Muttalib:

You satirized Muhammad, so I answered on his behalf, and with Allah is the recompense for that.
Indeed my father, his father, and my honor are a shield for the honor of Muhammad from you.
Do you curse him, when you are not his equal? So the evil of you both is the ransom of the better of you both.
My tongue is a sharp sword with no flaw in it, and my sea is not made turbid by buckets."

It was said to her: "O Mother of the Believers, is this not idle talk (laghw)?" She said: "No. Idle talk is only what is said in the presence of women." It was said: "Does Allah not say ﴿And he who took upon himself the greater part of it, for him is a great punishment﴾?" She said: "Has he not suffered a great punishment? Has his sight not gone, and was he not struck on the head (kunni'a) with the sword?" She meant the blow that Safwan ibn al-Mu'attal [al-Sulami] [[added from F, A.]] struck him with, when news reached him that he was speaking about that matter, so he struck him with the sword and nearly killed him.

This is a divine admonition to the believers concerning the matter of 'Aishah, may Allah be pleased with her, when some of them spread that wicked talk and what was mentioned of the affair of the slander (*ifk*). Allah said: ﴿Why did you not, when you heard it, think well of one another?﴾ Here "why" (*lawla*) means "why not." ﴿When you heard it﴾ means that talk, that is, the accusation with which the Mother of the Believers was charged. ﴿The believing men and believing women thought good of their own kind﴾ means they judged that talk by themselves. If it is unbecoming of them, then the Mother of the Believers is more deserving of being cleared of it by way of greater priority and fitness.

It has been said that this verse was revealed concerning Abu Ayyub Khalid ibn Zayd al-Ansari and his wife, may Allah be pleased with them both, as stated by the Imam Muhammad ibn Ishaq ibn Yasar, from his father, from some men of Banu al-Najjar: that Abu Ayyub Khalid ibn Zayd was told by his wife, Umm Ayyub: "O Abu Ayyub, do you not hear what people are saying about 'Aishah, may Allah be pleased with her?" He said: "Yes, and that is a lie. Would you have done such a thing, O Umm Ayyub?" She said: "No, by Allah, I would not have done it." He said: "By Allah, 'Aishah is better than you." He said: "When the Qur'an was revealed, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, mentioned those who spoke the obscene words of the slanderers: ﴿Indeed, those who came with the slander are a group among you﴾ [al-Nur: 11], and that refers to Hassan and his companions, who said what they said. Then He said: ﴿Why, when you heard it, did the believing men and believing women not think well of their own kind﴾ and so on," meaning, as Abu Ayyub and his wife had said.

Al-Waqidi, Muhammad ibn Umar, said: Ibn Abi Habibah narrated to me, from Dawud ibn al-Husayn, from Abu Sufyan, from Aflah, the freed slave of Abu Ayyub, that Umm Ayyub said to Abu Ayyub: "Do you not hear what people are saying about 'Aishah?" He said: "Yes, and that is a lie. Would you have done it, O Umm Ayyub?" She said: "No, by Allah." He said: "By Allah, 'Aishah is better than you." Then, when the Qur'an was revealed and mentioned the people of the slander, Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, said: ﴿Why, when you heard it, did the believing men and believing women not think well of their own kind and say, "This is a clear lie"?﴾ meaning Abu Ayyub, when he said to Umm Ayyub what he said.

It is also said that it was Ubayy ibn Ka'b who said it.

* *

His saying ﴿the believing men and believing women thought well of their own kind﴾ means: "Why did they not think good?" For the Mother of the Believers is more deserving of it and more fitting for it. This is what relates to the inner thought. ﴿And said﴾ means with their tongues ﴿"This is a clear lie"﴾, that is, an evident falsehood against the Mother of the Believers. What occurred was not a matter of suspicion. That is because the Mother of the Believers came riding openly on the mount of Safwan ibn al-Mu'attal at midday, while the whole army was watching, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was among them. Had this matter involved any suspicion, it would not have happened in this open manner, nor would the two of them have proceeded in such a way before the eyes of witnesses. Rather, had it happened, it would have been hidden and concealed. Thus it is established that what the people of the slander brought, of what they accused the Mother of the Believers, is pure falsehood, a false statement, reckless wickedness, a shameful (*al-fajirah*) act, and a losing bargain.

Allah, may He be exalted, said: ﴿Why did they not bring four witnesses for it?﴾ "Why not," meaning, for what they said, ﴿bring four witnesses for it﴾ who would testify to the truth of what they brought. ﴿Since they did not bring the witnesses, those are the liars in the sight of Allah﴾, meaning: by the judgment of Allah, they are liars and wicked transgressors.

Allah says: ﴿And were it not for the grace of Allah upon you and His mercy in this world and the Hereafter﴾, O you who spread rumors concerning the matter of 'Aishah, by accepting your repentance and your turning back to Him in this world, and by pardoning you for your faith in relation to the Abode of the Hereafter, ﴿a great punishment would have touched you for what you plunged into﴾, namely the affair of the slander (al-ifk), ﴿a great punishment﴾. This applies to those who had faith, whom Allah enabled, by means of it, to repent to Him, such as Mistah, Hassan, and Hamnah bint Jahsh, the sister of Zaynab bint Jahsh. As for those among the hypocrites who plunged into it, such as 'Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul and his like, they are not intended in this verse, because they do not possess faith and righteous deeds that could counterbalance this, nor anything that could oppose it. Likewise is the case with any threat of punishment attached to a specific action: it is absolute, conditional upon the absence of repentance, or upon a righteous deed that equals it or outweighs it.

Then He, exalted is He, says: ﴿When you received it with your tongues﴾. Mujahid and Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: that is, some of you narrate it from others; one says, "I heard it from so-and-so," and "so-and-so said such-and-such," and some of them mentioned such-and-such.

Others recited it as "idh talaqunahu bi-alsinatikum" (when you receive it from one another with your tongues). In Sahih al-Bukhari, it is related from 'Aishah that she used to recite it in this way [Sahih al-Bukhari, nos. 4144, 4752], and she would say: "It is from waliq al-qawl" — meaning the lie in which its speaker persists. The Arabs say: "So-and-so persisted in the course (walaqa fulan fi al-sayr)" when he continued in it. The first reading is more well-known and is the one followed by the majority, but the second is transmitted from the Mother of the Believers 'Aishah.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj narrated to us, Abu Usamah narrated to us, from Nafi' ibn 'Umar, from Ibn Abi Mulaykah, that 'Aishah used to recite: "idh talaqunahu" and would say: "It is only waliq al-qawl," and al-walaq is the lie. Ibn Abi Mulaykah said: She knew it better than others.

* *

His saying: ﴿and you say with your mouths what you have no knowledge of﴾ means: you say what you do not know.

Then He, exalted is He, says: ﴿And you consider it trivial, while it is, in the sight of Allah, tremendous﴾. That is: you say what you say concerning the Mother of the Believers, and you consider that a light matter. Even if she were not the wife of the Prophet ﷺ, it would not be trivial; how much more so when she is the wife of the unlettered Prophet, the Seal of the Prophets and the Master of the Messengers. It is tremendous in the sight of Allah that such things be said about the wife of His Messenger! Allah is jealous for this, and He, glorified and exalted is He, does not permit such a thing for the wife of any of His prophets. Far, far be it! How then could this be said of the mistress of the women of the prophets, and the wife of the master of the children of Adam absolutely, in this world and the Hereafter? For this reason He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And you consider it trivial, while it is, in the sight of Allah, tremendous﴾. And in the two Sahihs: "Indeed a man may utter a word out of the displeasure of Allah, not realizing where it will lead, and it casts him into the Fire farther than the distance between the east and the west." In another narration: "He does not give it any thought" [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 6478; Sahih Muslim, no. 2988, from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him].

This is another discipline following the first: the command to think well (al-amr bil-zann khayran). That is, when something unbecoming is said about the chaste women (al-khiyarah), it is all the more fitting that one should think well of them, and that one should not allow oneself to entertain anything else. Then, if something of that kind takes hold of a person's self, whether as a whisper (waswasah) or an imagining (khayal), he should not speak of it. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah has overlooked for my Ummah what their souls whisper to them, so long as they do not speak it or act upon it." Both (al-Bukhari and Muslim) related it in their Sahihs. [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 5269, and Sahih Muslim, no. 127, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him.]

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And why, when you heard it, did you not say, "It is not for us to speak of this. Glory be to You; this is a great slander"?﴾ That is: it was not fitting for us to utter these words or to mention them to anyone. ﴿Glory be to You, this is a great slander﴾ That is: Glory be to Allah that such words should be said about the wife of His Prophet, His Messenger, and the beloved of His Friend.

Then He said, the Exalted: ﴿Allah admonishes you never to repeat the like of it again﴾ That is: Allah forbids you, warning that anything resembling this should never occur from you in the future. Therefore He said: ﴿if you are believers﴾ That is: if you believe in Allah and His law, and you venerate His Messenger (ﷺ). As for one who is characterized by disbelief, he has a different ruling.

Then He said: ﴿And Allah makes clear to you the verses﴾ That is: He clarifies for you the legal rulings of the Sharia and the wisdoms of divine decree. ﴿And Allah is Knowing and Wise﴾ That is: Knowing of what sets right His servants, Wise in His legislation and His decree.

Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And why, when you heard it, did you not say, "It is not for us to speak of this. Glory be to You; this is a great slander"?﴾ That is: it was not fitting for us to utter these words or to mention them to anyone. ﴿Glory be to You, this is a great slander﴾ That is: Glory be to Allah that such words should be said about the wife of His Prophet, His Messenger, and the beloved of His Friend.

Then He said, the Exalted: ﴿Allah admonishes you never to repeat the like of it again﴾ That is: Allah forbids you, warning that anything resembling this should never occur from you in the future. Therefore He said: ﴿if you are believers﴾ That is: if you believe in Allah and His law, and you venerate His Messenger (ﷺ). As for one who is characterized by disbelief, he has a different ruling.

Then He said: ﴿And Allah makes clear to you the verses﴾ That is: He clarifies for you the legal rulings of the Sharia and the wisdoms of divine decree. ﴿And Allah is Knowing and Wise﴾ That is: Knowing of what sets right His servants, Wise in His legislation and His decree.

This is another discipline following the first: the command to think well (al-amr bil-zann khayran). That is, when something unbecoming is said about the chaste women (al-khiyarah), it is all the more fitting that one should think well of them, and that one should not allow oneself to entertain anything else. Then, if something of that kind takes hold of a person's self, whether as a whisper (waswasah) or an imagining (khayal), he should not speak of it. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah has overlooked for my Ummah what their souls whisper to them, so long as they do not speak it or act upon it." Both (al-Bukhari and Muslim) related it in their Sahihs. [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 5269, and Sahih Muslim, no. 127, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him.]

Glory be to You; this is a great slander"?﴾ That is: it was not fitting for us to utter these words or to mention them to anyone. ﴿Glory be to You, this is a great slander﴾ That is: Glory be to Allah that such words should be said about the wife of His Prophet, His Messenger, and the beloved of His Friend.

Then He said, the Exalted: ﴿Allah admonishes you never to repeat the like of it again﴾ That is: Allah forbids you, warning that anything resembling this should never occur from you in the future. Therefore He said: ﴿if you are believers﴾ That is: if you believe in Allah and His law, and you venerate His Messenger (ﷺ). As for one who is characterized by disbelief, he has a different ruling.

Then He said: ﴿And Allah makes clear to you the verses﴾ That is: He clarifies for you the legal rulings of the Sharia and the wisdoms of divine decree. ﴿And Allah is Knowing and Wise﴾ That is: Knowing of what sets right His servants, Wise in His legislation and His decree.

This is a third act of discipline for one who hears some foul speech, something of it settles in his mind, and he speaks of it. He should not dwell on it much, nor spread it or broadcast it. Allah, the Exalted, has said: ﴿Indeed, those who like that immorality should be spread among those who believe﴾, i.e., they choose that foul talk about them should become widespread. ﴿For them is a painful punishment in this world﴾, i.e., through the prescribed legal penalty (hadd), and in the Hereafter through the punishment. ﴿And Allah knows, while you know not﴾, i.e., refer matters to Him and you will be guided.

Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Bakr narrated to us, Maymun ibn Abi Muhammad al-Mara'i narrated to us, Muhammad ibn 'Abbad al-Makhzumi narrated to us, from Thawban, from the Prophet (ﷺ) who said: "Do not harm the servants of Allah, do not reproach them, and do not seek out their faults. For whoever seeks out the faults of his Muslim brother, Allah will seek out his faults until He exposes him in his own house."

[Musnad (5/279).]

Allah, the Exalted, says: ﴿And were it not for Allah's grace upon you and His mercy, and that Allah is Most Kind, Most Merciful﴾. That is: were it not for this, another matter would have occurred. But He, the Exalted, is Kind to His servants and Merciful to them. So He turned in forgiveness to whoever among them repented from this matter [[Addition from manuscripts F and A.]] and purified whoever among them purified himself through the prescribed punishment (hadd) that was carried out upon him.

Then He said: ﴿O you who believe, do not follow the steps of Shaytan﴾. That is: his ways, his paths, and what he commands. ﴿And whoever follows the steps of Shaytan, indeed he enjoins what is shameful and wrong﴾. This is a warning and a caution against that, expressed in the most eloquent, concise, forceful and excellent wording.

ʿAli ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas: ﴿the steps of Shaytan﴾: his deeds. ʿIkrimah said: his incitements (nazaghat). Qatadah said: every act of disobedience is from the steps of Shaytan. Abu Mijlaz said: vows made in acts of disobedience are from the steps of Shaytan.

Masruq said: A man asked Ibn Masʿud, "I have made it unlawful for myself to eat food?" He said: "This is from the promptings (nazaʿat) of Shaytan. Atone for your oath and eat."

Al-Shaʿbi, regarding a man who vowed to slaughter his son, said: "This is from the incitements (nazaghat) of Shaytan," and he instructed him to slaughter a ram.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Hassan ibn ʿAbd Allah al-Misri narrated to us, al-Sarri ibn Yahya narrated to us, from Sulayman al-Taymi, from Abu Rafi who said: My wife became angry with me and said: "She is one day a Jewess and one day a Christian, and every slave she owns is free, if you do not divorce your wife." I came to ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUmar and he said: "This is only from the promptings (nazaghat) of Shaytan." Likewise Zaynab, the daughter of Umm Salamah, who was at that time the most learned woman in Madinah, said, and I came to ʿAsim ibn ʿUmar and he said the same.

Then Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And were it not for Allah's grace upon you and His mercy, not one of you would ever have been purified, ever﴾. That is: were it not for Him, who grants repentance and return to whom He wills, and who purifies souls from their polytheism, their wickedness, their corruption, and the bad characteristics within them, each according to his capacity, no one would have attained for himself purity or any good. ﴿But Allah purifies whom He wills﴾, that is, whom He wills of His creation, ﴿and Allah is All-Hearing, All-Knowing﴾ ... and He misguides whom He wills and casts him into the ruin of error and deviance.

* *

His saying: ﴿And Allah is All-Hearing﴾, that is, He hears the words of His servants, ﴿All-Knowing﴾ of them, of who among them deserves guidance and who deserves misguidance.

His saying: ﴿And Allah is All-Hearing﴾, that is, He hears the words of His servants, ﴿All-Knowing﴾ of them, of who among them deserves guidance and who deserves misguidance.

Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And let not those of virtue among you and wealth swear﴾, from al-iy'lah (the oath), [and it is: swearing an oath], meaning: let them not swear, ﴿those of virtue among you﴾, meaning: bounty, charity and benevolence, ﴿and wealth﴾, meaning: affluence, ﴿that they will not give to the near of kin and the needy and the emigrants for the cause of Allah﴾. That is, do not swear that you will not maintain your relatives, the needy and the emigrants. This is in the utmost gentleness and compassion in maintaining the ties of kinship. Therefore He said: ﴿and let them pardon and overlook﴾, meaning: for what has preceded from them of wrongdoing and harm. This is from Allah's forbearance, His generosity and His kindness to His creation, despite their wronging themselves.

This verse was revealed concerning al-Siddiq (the Truthful, Abu Bakr), when he swore that he would never benefit Mistah ibn Uthathah with any benefit after he had said what he said about Aishah, as has preceded in the hadith. When Allah revealed the innocence of the Mother of the Believers Aishah, the believing souls were content and settled, Allah accepted the repentance of those among the believers who had spoken about that, and the hadd (the prescribed punishment) was carried out on those upon whom it was carried out. Then the Blessed and Exalted, to whom belongs grace and favour, prescribed that al-Siddiq should show kindness to his relative and kinsman, Mistah ibn Uthathah, for he was the son of al-Siddiq's maternal aunt, and he was a needy man with no wealth except what Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, spent on him. He was also among the emigrants in the cause of Allah. He had slipped into a slip, from which Allah accepted his repentance, and the hadd was applied to him for it. Al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with him, was known for good conduct, and he had bounty and favours upon both relatives and strangers. When this verse was revealed up to His saying: ﴿Do you not like that Allah should forgive you? And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾, meaning: the recompense is of the same kind as the deed. Just as you forgive the one who wrongs you, Allah will forgive you, and just as you overlook, He will overlook for you. At that, al-Siddiq said: "Yes, by Allah, we love, O our Lord, that You forgive us." Then he returned to Mistah what he used to give him of expenditure, and said: "By Allah, I will never withdraw it from him, in exchange for what he said. By Allah, I will never benefit him with any benefit." Therefore al-Siddiq was indeed al-Siddiq [may Allah be pleased with him and with his daughter].

This is a warning from Allah, exalted is He, for those who accuse chaste, unwary, believing women. The description was given in the form of what is generally the case (kharraja makhraj al-ghalib).

The mothers of the believers are more deserving of inclusion in this than any other chaste woman, especially she who was the cause of the revelation, namely 'Aishah, daughter of al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with them both.

The scholars, may Allah have mercy on them, are unanimous that whoever reviles her after this and accuses her of what was alleged against her, after what has been mentioned in this verse, is a disbeliever, because he is opposing the Qur'an. Regarding the rest of the mothers of the believers there are two opinions, the more sound of which is that they are like her, and Allah knows best.

* *

Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿They are cursed in this world and the Hereafter, and theirs will be a great punishment﴾, like His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who annoy Allah and His Messenger – Allah has cursed them in this world and the Hereafter and prepared for them a humiliating punishment﴾ [al-Ahzab: 57] [In F: "and the Hereafter and theirs will be a humiliating punishment," which is an error.].

Some have held that it is specific to 'Aishah. Ibn Abi Hatim said:

We were told by Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj, who was told by Abdullah ibn Khirash, from al-'Awwam, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿Indeed, those who accuse chaste, unwary, believing women﴾ [He said:] It was revealed specifically concerning 'Aishah.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr [and] Muqatil ibn Hayyan also said likewise. Ibn Jarir reported it from 'Aishah, saying:

We were told by Ahmad ibn Abdah al-Dabbi, who was told by Abu 'Awanah, from Umar ibn Abi Salamah, from his father, who said: 'Aishah said: "I was accused of what I was accused of while I was unaware, and then it reached me afterwards. She said: While the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was sitting with me, [in F, A: "sitting with me"] there came a revelation [in F, A: "Allah the Exalted revealed to him"] to him. She said: When revelation came to him, he would be seized as if in a faint, and he received revelation while sitting with me; then he sat up wiping his face and said: 'O 'Aishah, rejoice.' She said: I said: 'By the praise of Allah, not by yours.' Then he recited: ﴿Indeed, those who accuse chaste, unwary, believing women﴾, until he recited [in F, A: "reached"] ﴿Those are cleared of what they say﴾ [an-Nur: 26]."

[Tafsir al-Tabari (18/82).]

This is how he related it, and it does not state that the ruling is specific to her; rather it states that she was the cause of the revelation to the exclusion of others, even though the ruling encompasses her and others alike. Perhaps this is what Ibn 'Abbas and those who said as he said intended, and Allah knows best.

Al-Dahhak, Abu al-Jawza' and Salamah ibn Nubayt said: what is meant by it is specifically the wives of the Prophet ﷺ, to the exclusion of other women.

Al-'Awfi reported from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who accuse chaste, unwary, believing women﴾, the verse: he meant the wives of the Prophet ﷺ, whom the hypocrites accused, so Allah made cursing and wrath obligatory upon them, and they returned with anger from Allah. So that was concerning the wives of the Prophet ﷺ. Then after that there was revealed: ﴿And those who accuse chaste women and then do not produce four witnesses﴾ to His saying: ﴿indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾, and Allah revealed the lashing and repentance; so repentance is accepted, and testimony is rejected.

Ibn Jarir said: We were told by al-Qasim, who was told by al-Husayn, who was told by Hushaym, who was informed by al-'Awwam ibn Hawshab, from a shaykh of the Banu Asad, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: He explained Surat an-Nur, and when he reached this verse: ﴿Indeed, those who accuse chaste, unwary, believing women are cursed﴾, to the end of the verse, he said: it concerns 'Aishah and the wives of the Prophet ﷺ, and it is unspecified [mubhamah], and there is no repentance for them. Then he recited: ﴿And those who accuse chaste women and then do not produce four witnesses﴾ to His saying: ﴿except those who repent after that and reform﴾ [an-Nur: 4, 5]. He said: So He made repentance possible for these, but did not make repentance possible for those who slandered those [women]. He said: Some of the people almost rose to kiss his head, because of the excellence of his explanation of Surat an-Nur.

[Tafsir al-Tabari (18/83).]

So his saying "wa hiya mubhamah" means: it is general in prohibiting the accusation of every chaste woman, and in cursing the one who does it in this world and the Hereafter.

Likewise 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: this concerns 'Aishah, and whoever does the like today regarding Muslim women, for him is what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has said; but 'Aishah was the leader in this matter.

Ibn Jarir chose its generality, and this is the correct view. What supports the generality is what Ibn Abi Hatim narrated:

We were told by Ahmad ibn Abd al-Rahman – the nephew of Ibn Wahb – who was told by my uncle, who was told by Sulayman ibn Bilal, from Thawr ibn Zayd, from Abu al-Ghayth [in A: "al-Mughayth"], from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Avoid the seven destructive sins." It was said: O Messenger of Allah, what are they? He said: "Associating partners with Allah, sorcery, killing a soul which Allah has forbidden except by right, consuming usury, consuming the property of an orphan, fleeing on the day of battle, and accusing chaste, unwary, believing women."

Al-Bukhari and Muslim both recorded it in their Sahihs, from the hadith of Sulayman ibn Bilal, with the same chain [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (2766) and Sahih Muslim no. (89)].

Al-Hafiz Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: We were told by Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Khalid al-Hadhdha' al-Harrani, who said: my father told me, (h) and we were told by Abu Shu'ayb al-Harrani, who said: my grandfather Ahmad ibn Abi Shu'ayb told us, who said: Musa ibn A'yan told us, from Layth, from Abu Ishaq, from Silah ibn Zufar, from Hudhayfah, from the Prophet ﷺ who said: "Slandering a chaste woman destroys the deeds of a hundred years." [al-Mu'jam al-Kabir of al-Tabarani (3/196); al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (6/279): "In it is Layth ibn Abi Sulaym, who is weak, though his narrations may be good, and the rest of its narrators are narrators of the Sahih."]

* *

His saying: ﴿On the day when their tongues, their hands and their feet will testify against them concerning what they used to do﴾. Ibn Abi Hatim said:

We were told by Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj, who was told by Abu Yahya al-Razi, from Amr ibn Abi Qays, from Mutarrif, from al-Minhal, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: They – meaning the polytheists – when they see that none will enter Paradise except the people of prayer, say: "Come, let us deny." So they deny, and Allah [seals] their mouths, and their hands and feet testify, and they cannot conceal from Allah any statement.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim also said: We were told by Yunus ibn Abd al-A'la, who was told by Ibn Wahb, who said: Amr ibn al-Harith informed me, from Darraj, from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Sa'id, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ who said: "On the Day of Resurrection the disbeliever will be made to recognise his deeds, so he denies and disputes. It will be said to him: 'These are your neighbours who testify against you.' He says: 'They lied.' It is said: 'Your family and your clan.' He says: 'They lied.' It is said: 'Swear!' So they swear. Then Allah seals their mouths, and their hands and tongues testify against them, then He admits them into the Fire." [Tafsir al-Tabari (18/105); Abu Ya'la recorded it in his Musnad no. (1392) by the route of Ibn Lahi'ah, from Darraj, from Abu al-Haytham; Darraj from Abu al-Haytham is weak.]

Ibn Abi Hatim also said: We were told by Abu Shaybah Ibrahim ibn Abd Allah ibn Abi Shaybah al-Kufi, who was told by Minjab ibn al-Harith al-Tamimi [in F: "al-Tayyimi"], who was told by Abu 'Amir al-Asadi, who was told by Sufyan, from Ubayd al-Muktib, from Fudayl ibn Amr al-Fuqaymi, from al-Sha'bi, from Anas ibn Malik who said: We were with the Prophet ﷺ when he laughed until his molar teeth showed, then said: "Do you know what I am laughing at?" We said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "At the dispute of the servant with his Lord on the Day of Resurrection. He says: 'O Lord, did You not protect me from injustice?' He says: 'Yes.' He says: 'I do not accept any witness against myself except from myself.' He says: 'Sufficient is your own self as a witness against you today, and the honourable scribes as witnesses.' Then his mouth is sealed, and his limbs are told: 'Speak!' and they speak of his deeds. Then he is left to speak, and he says: 'Away with you, and destruction! It was for your sake that I was contending.'"

Muslim and al-Nasa'i both narrated it from Abu Bakr ibn Abi al-Nadr, from his father, from Ubayd Allah al-Ash'ajji, from Sufyan al-Thawri, with it [Sahih Muslim no. (2969)]. Then al-Nasa'i said: I do not know of anyone who narrated this hadith from Sufyan al-Thawri except al-Ash'ajji, and it is a gharib hadith, and Allah knows best. Thus he said.

Qatadah said: O son of Adam, by Allah, against you there are witnesses from your own body who are not to be doubted, so be watchful of them and fear Allah in your secret and open conduct, for nothing is hidden from Him, darkness is light to Him, and secrecy is openness to Him. Whoever is able to die while thinking well of Allah, let him do so, and there is no power except with Allah.

* *

His saying: ﴿On that day Allah will pay them their full recompense, their true religion [dinahum al-haqq]﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: "dinahum" means their reckoning [hisabahum], and wherever "dinahum" occurs in the Qur'an it means their reckoning. Others said likewise.

The reading of the majority is with the accusative "al-haqq", as an adjective of "dinihim". Mujahid read it with the nominative, as an attribute of the Name of Majesty [Allah]. Some of the early generation read it in the codex of Ubayy ibn Ka'b: "Yawma'idhin yuwaffihimu Allahu al-haqqu dinahum."

Likewise 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: this concerns 'Aishah, and whoever does the like today regarding Muslim women, for him is what Allah, Mighty and Majestic, has said; but 'Aishah was the leader in this matter.

We were told by Ahmad ibn Abd al-Rahman – the nephew of Ibn Wahb – who was told by my uncle, who was told by Sulayman ibn Bilal, from Thawr ibn Zayd, from Abu al-Ghayth [in A: "al-Mughayth"], from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Avoid the seven destructive sins." It was said: O Messenger of Allah, what are they? He said: "Associating partners with Allah, sorcery, killing a soul which Allah has forbidden except by right, consuming usury, consuming the property of an orphan, fleeing on the day of battle, and accusing chaste, unwary, believing women."

Al-Hafiz Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: We were told by Muhammad ibn Amr ibn Khalid al-Hadhdha' al-Harrani, who said: my father told me, (h) and we were told by Abu Shu'ayb al-Harrani, who said: my grandfather Ahmad ibn Abi Shu'ayb told us, who said: Musa ibn A'yan told us, from Layth, from Abu Ishaq, from Silah ibn Zufar, from Hudhayfah, from the Prophet ﷺ who said: "Slandering a chaste woman destroys the deeds of a hundred years." [al-Mu'jam al-Kabir of al-Tabarani (3/196); al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (6/279): "In it is Layth ibn Abi Sulaym, who is weak, though his narrations may be good, and the rest of its narrators are narrators of the Sahih."]

* *

His saying: ﴿On the day when their tongues, their hands and their feet will testify against them concerning what they used to do﴾. Ibn Abi Hatim said:

We were told by Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj, who was told by Abu Yahya al-Razi, from Amr ibn Abi Qays, from Mutarrif, from al-Minhal, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: They – meaning the polytheists – when they see that none will enter Paradise except the people of prayer, say: "Come, let us deny." So they deny, and Allah [seals] their mouths, and their hands and feet testify, and they cannot conceal from Allah any statement.

Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim also said: We were told by Yunus ibn Abd al-A'la, who was told by Ibn Wahb, who said: Amr ibn al-Harith informed me, from Darraj, from Abu al-Haytham, from Abu Sa'id, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ who said: "On the Day of Resurrection the disbeliever will be made to recognise his deeds, so he denies and disputes. It will be said to him: 'These are your neighbours who testify against you.' He says: 'They lied.' It is said: 'Your family and your clan.' He says: 'They lied.' It is said: 'Swear!' So they swear. Then Allah seals their mouths, and their hands and tongues testify against them, then He admits them into the Fire." [Tafsir al-Tabari (18/105); Abu Ya'la recorded it in his Musnad no. (1392) by the route of Ibn Lahi'ah, from Darraj, from Abu al-Haytham; Darraj from Abu al-Haytham is weak.]

Ibn Abi Hatim also said: We were told by Abu Shaybah Ibrahim ibn Abd Allah ibn Abi Shaybah al-Kufi, who was told by Minjab ibn al-Harith al-Tamimi [in F: "al-Tayyimi"], who was told by Abu 'Amir al-Asadi, who was told by Sufyan, from Ubayd al-Muktib, from Fudayl ibn Amr al-Fuqaymi, from al-Sha'bi, from Anas ibn Malik who said: We were with the Prophet ﷺ when he laughed until his molar teeth showed, then said: "Do you know what I am laughing at?" We said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "At the dispute of the servant with his Lord on the Day of Resurrection. He says: 'O Lord, did You not protect me from injustice?' He says: 'Yes.' He says: 'I do not accept any witness against myself except from myself.' He says: 'Sufficient is your own self as a witness against you today, and the honourable scribes as witnesses.' Then his mouth is sealed, and his limbs are told: 'Speak!' and they speak of his deeds. Then he is left to speak, and he says: 'Away with you, and destruction! It was for your sake that I was contending.'"

Then al-Nasa'i said: I do not know of anyone who narrated this hadith from Sufyan al-Thawri except al-Ash'ajji, and it is a gharib hadith, and Allah knows best. Thus he said.

Whoever is able to die while thinking well of Allah, let him do so, and there is no power except with Allah.

His saying: ﴿On that day Allah will pay them their full recompense, their true religion [dinahum al-haqq]﴾. Ibn 'Abbas said: "dinahum" means their reckoning [hisabahum], and wherever "dinahum" occurs in the Qur'an it means their reckoning. Others said likewise.

The reading of the majority is with the accusative "al-haqq", as an adjective of "dinihim". Mujahid read it with the nominative, as an attribute of the Name of Majesty [Allah]. Some of the early generation read it in the codex of Ubayy ibn Ka'b: "Yawma'idhin yuwaffihimu Allahu al-haqqu dinahum."

His saying: ﴿And they will know that Allah is the Manifest Truth﴾, meaning: His promise, His warning and His reckoning are the justice in which there is no injustice.

This is a warning from Allah, exalted is He, for those who accuse chaste, unwary, believing women. The description was given in the form of what is generally the case (kharraja makhraj al-ghalib).

The mothers of the believers are more deserving of inclusion in this than any other chaste woman, especially she who was the cause of the revelation, namely 'Aishah, daughter of al-Siddiq, may Allah be pleased with them both.

The scholars, may Allah have mercy on them, are unanimous that whoever reviles her after this and accuses her of what was alleged against her, after what has been mentioned in this verse, is a disbeliever, because he is opposing the Qur'an. Regarding the rest of the mothers of the believers there are two opinions, the more sound of which is that they are like her, and Allah knows best.

* *

Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿They are cursed in this world and the Hereafter, and theirs will be a great punishment﴾, like His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who annoy Allah and His Messenger – Allah has cursed them in this world and the Hereafter and prepared for them a humiliating punishment﴾ [al-Ahzab: 57] [In F: "and the Hereafter and theirs will be a humiliating punishment," which is an error.].

Some have held that it is specific to 'Aishah. Ibn Abi Hatim said:

We were told by Abu Sa'id al-Ashajj, who was told by Abdullah ibn Khirash, from al-'Awwam, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas: ﴿Indeed, those who accuse chaste, unwary, believing women﴾ [He said:] It was revealed specifically concerning 'Aishah.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr [and] Muqatil ibn Hayyan also said likewise. Ibn Jarir reported it from 'Aishah, saying:

We were told by Ahmad ibn Abdah al-Dabbi, who was told by Abu 'Awanah, from Umar ibn Abi Salamah, from his father, who said: 'Aishah said: "I was accused of what I was accused of while I was unaware, and then it reached me afterwards. She said: While the Messenger of Allah ﷺ was sitting with me, [in F, A: "sitting with me"] there came a revelation [in F, A: "Allah the Exalted revealed to him"] to him. She said: When revelation came to him, he would be seized as if in a faint, and he received revelation while sitting with me; then he sat up wiping his face and said: 'O 'Aishah, rejoice.' She said: I said: 'By the praise of Allah, not by yours.' Then he recited: ﴿Indeed, those who accuse chaste, unwary, believing women﴾, until he recited [in F, A: "reached"] ﴿Those are cleared of what they say﴾ [an-Nur: 26]."

[Tafsir al-Tabari (18/82).]

This is how he related it, and it does not state that the ruling is specific to her; rather it states that she was the cause of the revelation to the exclusion of others, even though the ruling encompasses her and others alike. Perhaps this is what Ibn 'Abbas and those who said as he said intended, and Allah knows best.

Al-Dahhak, Abu al-Jawza' and Salamah ibn Nubayt said: what is meant by it is specifically the wives of the Prophet ﷺ, to the exclusion of other women.

Al-'Awfi reported from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His saying: ﴿Indeed, those who accuse chaste, unwary, believing women﴾, the verse: he meant the wives of the Prophet ﷺ, whom the hypocrites accused, so Allah made cursing and wrath obligatory upon them, and they returned with anger from Allah. So that was concerning the wives of the Prophet ﷺ. Then after that there was revealed: ﴿And those who accuse chaste women and then do not produce four witnesses﴾ to His saying: ﴿indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾, and Allah revealed the lashing and repentance; so repentance is accepted, and testimony is rejected.

Ibn Jarir said: We were told by al-Qasim, who was told by al-Husayn, who was told by Hushaym, who was informed by al-'Awwam ibn Hawshab, from a shaykh of the Banu Asad, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: He explained Surat an-Nur, and when he reached this verse: ﴿Indeed, those who accuse chaste, unwary, believing women are cursed﴾, to the end of the verse, he said: it concerns 'Aishah and the wives of the Prophet ﷺ, and it is unspecified [mubhamah], and there is no repentance for them. Then he recited: ﴿And those who accuse chaste women and then do not produce four witnesses﴾ to His saying: ﴿except those who repent after that and reform﴾ [an-Nur: 4, 5]. He said: So He made repentance possible for these, but did not make repentance possible for those who slandered those [women]. He said: Some of the people almost rose to kiss his head, because of the excellence of his explanation of Surat an-Nur.

[Tafsir al-Tabari (18/83).]
