Malik said, from Zayd ibn Aslam: It refers to houses of hair (tents).

This is a command from Allah the Exalted to His believing servants: that they lower their gaze from what He has forbidden them, so that they look only at what He has permitted them to look at. [[In Fa: "إليهم" (to them).]] They should also lower [[In F: "يغمصوا" (a variant reading).]] their gaze from the forbidden things. If it happens that the gaze falls upon something forbidden without intention, then one should quickly turn the gaze away from it, as Muslim reported in his Sahih, from the hadith of Yunus ibn Ubayd, from Amr ibn Sa'id, from Abu Zur'ah ibn Amr ibn Jarir, from his grandfather Jarir ibn Abdullah al-Bajali, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "I asked the Prophet ﷺ about a glance that comes unintended (nazrat al-fajah), and he commanded me to turn my gaze away."

Imam Ahmad also narrated it in the same way, from Hushaym, from Yunus ibn Ubayd, with the same chain. Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i narrated it too, from the same hadith. [[Sahih Muslim no. (2159), al-Musnad (4/361), Sunan Abi Dawud no. (2148), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (2776), and al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra no. (9233).]] Al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan sahih." In a narration of some of them, he said: "Lower your gaze" (atriq basaraka), meaning: look at the ground. And "sarf" (turning away) is more general, for it may be toward the ground or toward another direction. And Allah knows best.

Abu Dawud said: Ismail ibn Musa al-Fazari narrated to us, Sharik narrated to us, from Abu Rabi'ah al-Iyadi, from Abdullah ibn Buraydah, from his father, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to Ali: "O Ali, do not follow a glance with another glance, for the first is yours, but the second is not yours."

Al-Tirmidhi narrated it from the hadith of Sharik, and said: "Gharib (strange). We do not know it except from his narration." [[Sunan Abi Dawud no. (2149) and Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (2777).]]

In the Sahih, from Abu Sa'id, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Beware of sitting on the roadsides." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, we have no choice but to sit in our gatherings, where we talk." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "If you refuse, then give the road its right." They said: "And what is the right of the road, O Messenger of Allah?" He said: "Lowering the gaze, refraining from harm, returning the greeting, enjoining what is good, and forbidding what is evil." [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (2465) and Sahih Muslim no. (2121), from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him.]]

Abu al-Qasim al-Baghawi said: Talut ibn Abbad narrated to us, Fadl ibn Jubayr narrated to us: I heard Abu Umamah say: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "Guarantee for me six things and I will guarantee for you Paradise: when one of you speaks, let him not lie; when he is entrusted, let him not betray; when he promises, let him not break it; lower your gazes, restrain your hands, and guard your private parts." [[Narrated by al-Khatib al-Baghdadi in Tarikh Baghdad (7/392) through Abu al-Qasim al-Baghawi, with the same chain. Also narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (8/314) and Ibn Hibban in al-Majruhin (2/204) through Fadal ibn Jubayr, also called Ibn Zubayr. Ibn Hibban said: "Fadal ibn Jubayr, it is not permissible to argue with him."]]

In Sahih al-Bukhari: "Whoever guarantees for me what is between his jaws and what is between his legs, I guarantee for him Paradise." [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (6474), from the hadith of Sahl ibn Sa'd, may Allah be pleased with him.]]

Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar informed us, from Ayyub, from Ibn Sirin, from Ubaydah, who said: "Everything by which Allah is disobeyed is a major sin (kabirah)." He mentioned both parts and said: "Say to the believers that they lower their gaze from their sights" (Qur'an 24:30).

Since the gaze is a means that leads to corruption of the heart, as some of the early generations (salaf) said: "The gaze is a poisoned arrow toward the heart," Allah commanded the guarding of the private parts just as He commanded the guarding of the eyes, which are the motives that lead to it. He said: ﴿Say to the believing men that they lower their gaze and guard their private parts﴾ (24:30). Guarding the private parts is sometimes by preventing them from fornication, as He said: ﴿And those who guard their private parts, except from their wives or what their right hands possess, for they are not blameworthy﴾ (70:29-30). And sometimes it is by guarding them from being looked at, as came in the hadith in the Musnad and the Sunan: "Guard your nakedness, except from your wife or what your right hand possesses." [[Al-Musnad (5/3, 4), Sunan Abi Dawud no. (4017), and Sunan Ibn Majah no. (1920), from the hadith of Mu'awiyah ibn Haydah, may Allah be pleased with him.]]

﴿That is purer for them﴾, meaning: more purifying for their hearts and more pious for their religion, as it has been said: "Whoever guards his gaze, Allah will grant him light in his insight." And it is narrated: "in his heart."

Imam Ahmad said: Attab narrated to us, Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak narrated to us, Yahya ibn Ayyub informed us, from Ubayd Allah ibn Zahr, from Ali ibn Yazid, from al-Qasim, from Abu Umamah, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "No Muslim looks at the beauty of a woman [for the first time] [[Addition from F and A.]] and then lowers his gaze, except that Allah will give him a worship whose sweetness he will find." [[Al-Musnad (5/264). In its chain is Ubayd Allah ibn Zahr. Ibn Hibban said: "He narrates fabricated reports from reliable narrators, and when he narrates from Ali ibn Yazid, he brings forth absurdities. When in one chain Ubayd Allah ibn Zahr, Ali ibn Yazid and al-Qasim Abu Abd al-Rahman are gathered, that report is nothing but what their hands have produced."]]

This has also been narrated as a marfu' (traced to the Prophet ﷺ) report from Ibn Umar, Hudhayfah and A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with them. [[As for the hadith of Hudhayfah, al-Hakim narrated it in al-Mustadrak (4/314) through Ishaq al-Qurashi, from Hushaym, from Abd al-Rahman, from Ishaq, from Mihrab, from Salah ibn Zufar, from Hudhayfah, may Allah be pleased with him. Al-Hakim authenticated it, and al-Dhahabi criticized it. I say: Ishaq is weak, and Abd al-Rahman is al-Wasiti, whom they declared weak. As for the hadith of Ibn Umar, Abu Nu'aym narrated it in al-Hilyah (6/101) through Abu al-Yaman, from Abu al-Mahdi, from Abu al-Zahiriyyah, from Kathir ibn Murrah, from Ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, and its chain is very weak.]] However, there is weakness in its chain, but it is in the context of encouragement (al-targhib), and such reports are tolerated in that matter.

In al-Tabarani, through Ubayd Allah ibn Zahr, from Ali ibn Yazid, from al-Qasim, from Abu Umamah, marfu': "Lower your gazes, guard your private parts, and straighten your faces, or your faces will be darkened." [[Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (8/246). Ubayd Allah ibn Zahr, Ali ibn Yazid and al-Qasim are weak.]]

Al-Tabarani said: Ahmad ibn Zuhayr al-Tustari narrated to us, saying: We read to Muhammad ibn Hafs ibn Umar al-Darir al-Muqri', Yahya ibn Abi Bukayr narrated to us, Huraym ibn Sufyan narrated to us, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq, from al-Qasim ibn Abd al-Rahman, from his father, from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Indeed, the gaze is one of the poisoned arrows of Iblis. Whoever leaves it out of fear of Me, I will replace it with a faith whose sweetness he will find in his heart." [[Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (10/214). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (8/63): "In it is Abd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq al-Wasiti, who is weak."]]

* *

His statement: ﴿Indeed, Allah is Acquainted with what they do﴾, as He said: ﴿He knows the treachery of the eyes and what the hearts conceal﴾ (40:19).

In the Sahih, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "The son of Adam has been allotted his share of fornication, which he will inevitably encounter. The fornication of the eyes is the gaze; the fornication of the tongue is speech; the fornication of the ears is listening; the fornication of the hands is grasping; the fornication of the feet is walking; the soul desires and wishes, and the private part confirms that or denies it."

Al-Bukhari narrated it as a mu'allaq (without full chain), and Muslim narrated it with a full chain from another route, with similar wording to what has preceded. [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (6343) and Sahih Muslim no. (2657).]]

Many of the early generations (salaf) said that they used to forbid a man from fixing his gaze on a beardless youth (amrad). Many of the imams of the Sufis were very strict about this, and a group of the people of knowledge declared it forbidden, because of the temptation it contains, and others were extremely strict about it.

Ibn Abi al-Dunya said: Abu Sa'id al-Madani narrated to us, Umar ibn Sahl al-Mazini narrated to us, Umar ibn Muhammad ibn Suhban narrated to me, Safwan ibn Sulaym narrated to me, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Every eye will be weeping on the Day of Resurrection, except an eye that lowered itself from the prohibitions of Allah, an eye that stayed awake in the cause of Allah, and an eye from which a tear like the head of a fly comes out out of fear of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic." [[Al-Hilyah of Abu Nu'aym (3/163) also narrated it through Dawud ibn Ata, from Umar ibn Suhban, from Safwan, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, with the same wording. I do not know whether Abu Salamah has dropped out of the chain of Ibn Abi al-Dunya or not. Umar ibn Suhban is a munkar al-hadith (one whose narrations are rejected), and the imams agreed on his weakness.]]

This is a command from Allah, the Exalted, to the believing women, and a sign of His jealousy (ghayrah) for their husbands, His believing servants, and a distinction for them from the manner of the women of the Jahiliyyah (the age of ignorance) and the deeds of the polytheist women. The occasion of the revelation of this verse is what Muqatil ibn Hayyan related, saying: "It has reached us – and Allah knows best – that Jabir ibn 'Abdullah al-Ansari narrated that Asma' bint Murshida was in her dwelling among Banu Harithah, and women came in to her without wearing their waist-wrappers (izar), so that the anklet-bangles on their legs became visible, and their chests and the locks of their hair showed. Asma' said: 'How ugly this is!' So Allah revealed: ﴿And tell the believing women to lower their gaze and guard their private parts﴾, to the end of the verse."

His saying, the Exalted: ﴿And tell the believing women to lower their gaze﴾, means: from what Allah has forbidden them of looking at other than their husbands. For this reason, many of the scholars held that it is not permissible for a woman to look at non-mahram men, whether with desire or without desire at all. Many of them argued with what Abu Dawud and at-Tirmidhi narrated, from the hadith of az-Zuhri, from Nabhan, the freedman of Umm Salamah, that she related to him that Umm Salamah told him: that she was with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and Maymunah, and she said: "While we were with him, Ibn Umm Maktum came and entered upon him, and that was after we had been commanded to observe hijab. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'Veil yourselves from him.' I said: 'O Messenger of Allah, is he not blind, so he does not see us or recognize us?' The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'Are you two blind? Do you not see him?'" (Sunan Abi Dawud no. 4112, and Sunan at-Tirmidhi no. 2778).

At-Tirmidhi then said: "This is a hadith hasan sahih."

Others among the scholars held that it is permissible for women to look at non-mahram men without desire, as is established in the Sahih: that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ began looking at the Abyssinians while they played with their spears on the day of 'Eid in the mosque, and 'A'ishah, the Mother of the Believers, was looking at them from behind him, while he screened her from them until she grew weary and went back (Sahih al-Bukhari no. 454).

* *

His saying: ﴿and guard their private parts﴾. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: "from unlawful acts (al-fawahish)." Qatadah and Sufyan said: "from what is not lawful for them." Muqatil said: "from adultery (zina)." Abu al-'Aliyah said: "Every verse in the Qur'an in which guarding the private parts is mentioned means from zina, except this verse: ﴿and guard their private parts﴾, that no one sees them."

And His saying: ﴿and not reveal their adornment except what appears of it﴾ means: they should not display any of their adornment to non-mahram men, except what cannot be concealed.

Ibn Mas'ud said: "such as the outer garment and the clothes." He meant: according to what the women of the Arabs used to wear, of the head-covering (miqna'ah) that covers their clothing, and what appears of the lower garments, there is no blame upon her for that, because this cannot be concealed. The similar case in women's dress is what shows of her izar, which cannot be concealed. Al-Hasan, Ibn Sirin, Abu al-Jawza', Ibrahim al-Nakha'i and others said in agreement with the saying of Ibn Mas'ud.

Al-A'mash related from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding ﴿and not reveal their adornment except what appears of it﴾, that he said: "Her face, her palms, and the ring." It was also related from Ibn 'Umar, 'Ata', 'Ikrimah, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Abu al-Sha'tha', al-Dahhak, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i and others something similar. This may be an explanation of the adornment that they were forbidden to reveal, as Abu Ishaq al-Subay'i related from Abu al-Ahwas, from 'Abdullah, who said regarding His saying ﴿and not reveal their adornment﴾: "The adornment is the earring, the armlet, the anklet, and the necklace." In another narration from him by the same chain he said: "Adornment is of two kinds: an adornment that only the husband sees, which is the ring and the bracelet; and an adornment that non-mahram men see, which is the outer garment."

Az-Zuhri said: "What is displayed to those whom Allah has named, for whom it is lawful, is only the bracelets, the armlets and the earrings without uncovering; as for the general people, only the rings appear of it." Malik related from az-Zuhri: ﴿except what appears of it﴾ is the ring and the anklet.

It is possible that Ibn 'Abbas and those who followed him intended by "what appears of it" the face and the two palms, and this is the well-known view of the majority. It is supported by the hadith that Abu Dawud recorded in his Sunan:

Ya'qub ibn Ka'b al-Antaki and Mu'ammal ibn al-Fadl al-Harrani related to us, both saying: al-Walid related to us, from Sa'id ibn Bashir, from Qatadah, from Khalid ibn Durayk, from 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her: that Asma' bint Abi Bakr entered upon the Prophet ﷺ wearing thin garments, and he turned away from her and said: "O Asma', when a woman reaches menstruation, it is not proper that anything of her be seen except this," and he pointed to his face and his palms (Sunan Abi Dawud no. 4104).

But Abu Dawud and Abu Hatim al-Razi said: "This is mursal; Khalid ibn Durayk did not hear from 'A'ishah." And Allah knows best.

* *

His saying: ﴿and let them draw their head-coverings over their chests﴾, meaning: the miqna'ah, which is made with fringes (dawarib) hanging over the chests of women, to conceal what is beneath it of their chest and their breasts. This is to oppose the distinctive practice of the women of the Jahiliyyah, for they did not do that; rather, the woman would pass among the men with her chest uncovered, nothing concealing it, and perhaps she would show her neck, the locks of her hair, and the earrings of her ears. So Allah commanded the believing women to cover themselves in their appearance and their conditions, as Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿O Prophet, say to your wives and your daughters and the women of the believers that they should draw their outer garments over themselves. That is more suitable that they will be known and not be harmed﴾ [al-Ahzab: 59]. And in this noble verse He said: ﴿and let them draw their head-coverings over their chests﴾. Khumur is the plural of khimar, which is what one covers with, i.e., what the head is covered with, and it is what people call the miqna'ah.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: ﴿and let them draw﴾ means: let them tighten ﴿their head-coverings over their chests﴾, meaning: over the throat and the chest, so that nothing of it is seen.

Al-Bukhari said: Ahmad ibn Shabib related to us: my father related to us, from Yunus, from Ibn Shihab, from 'Urwah, from 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: "May Allah have mercy on the first emigrant women. When Allah revealed: ﴿and let them draw their head-coverings over their chests﴾, they split their woolen wraps and covered themselves with them" (Sahih al-Bukhari no. 4758).

He also said: Abu Nu'aym related to us, Ibrahim ibn Nafi' related to us, from al-Hasan ibn Muslim, from Safiyyah bint Shaybah: that 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, used to say: "When this verse was revealed: ﴿and let them draw their head-coverings over their chests﴾, they took their izars and split them from the edges, and covered themselves with them" (Sahih al-Bukhari no. 4759).

Ibn Abi Hatim said: my father related to us, Ahmad ibn 'Abdullah ibn Yunus related to us, al-Zinji ibn Khalid related to me, 'Abdullah ibn 'Uthman ibn Khuthaym related to us, from Safiyyah bint Shaybah, who said: "While we were with 'A'ishah, she said: we mentioned the women of Quraysh and their merit. 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, said: 'The women of Quraysh have merit, but by Allah, I have not seen anyone better than the women of the Ansar, more firm in their belief in the Book of Allah, nor in faith in the revelation. When Surat an-Nur was revealed: ﴿and let them draw their head-coverings over their chests﴾, their men returned to them reciting to them what Allah had revealed to them in it, and a man would recite it to his wife, his daughter, his sister, and to every relative. There was not a woman among them but she stood up to her striped woolen wrap and wrapped herself in it, out of belief and faith in what Allah had revealed in His Book. So they came in the morning behind the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for the dawn prayer, wrapped, as if there were crows upon their heads.'"

Abu Dawud related it through more than one route, from Safiyyah bint Shaybah, with the same wording (Sunan Abi Dawud nos. 4100, 4101).

Ibn Jarir said: Yunus related to us, Ibn Wahb informed us, that Qurrah ibn 'Abd al-Rahman informed him, from Ibn Shihab, from 'Urwah, from 'A'ishah, that she said: "May Allah have mercy on the first women emigrants. When Allah revealed: ﴿and let them draw their head-coverings over their chests﴾, they tore the thickest of their woolen wraps and covered themselves with them." Abu Dawud related it from the hadith of Ibn Wahb with the same wording (Tafsir al-Tabari 18/94; Sunan Abi Dawud no. 4102).

* *

His saying: ﴿and not reveal their adornment except to their husbands﴾, meaning: their husbands, ﴿or their fathers, or their husbands' fathers, or their sons, or their husbands' sons, or their brothers, or their brothers' sons, or their sisters' sons﴾. All these are the woman's mahram; it is permissible for her to appear before them with her adornment, but without excess and without flaunting (tabarruj).

Ibn al-Mundhir said: Musa (i.e., Ibn Harun) related to us, Abu Bakr (i.e., Ibn Abi Shaybah) related to us, 'Affan related to us, Hammad ibn Salamah related to us, Dawud informed us, from al-Sha'bi and 'Ikrimah regarding this verse: ﴿and not reveal their adornment except to their husbands or their fathers or their husbands' fathers﴾ – until he finished it – he said: "He did not mention the paternal uncle or the maternal uncle, because they are like parents to their children; and she should not take off her head-covering in the presence of the paternal or maternal uncle. As for the husband, all of that is for his sake, so she adorns herself for him in what is not to be seen in the presence of anyone else."

* *

His saying: ﴿or their women﴾, meaning: she may also display her adornment to Muslim women, but not to the women of the People of the Dhimmah; lest they describe them to their men. And although this is prohibited with all women, it is stronger with the women of the People of the Dhimmah, for nothing restrains them from it, whereas the Muslim woman knows that it is forbidden, so she refrains from it. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "A woman should not touch (mubashara) another woman and describe her to her husband, as if he were looking at her." Both (al-Bukhari and Muslim) narrated it in the Two Sahihs from Ibn Mas'ud (Sahih al-Bukhari no. 5241).

Sa'id ibn Mansur said in his Sunan: Isma'il ibn 'Ayyash related to us, from Hisham ibn al-Ghaz, from 'Ubadah ibn Nusayy, from his father, from al-Harith ibn Qays, who said: "The Commander of the Believers, 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, wrote to Abu 'Ubaydah: 'To proceed: it has reached me that some Muslim women enter the bathhouses with the women of the polytheists. So forbid those under your authority, for it is not lawful for a woman who believes in Allah and the Last Day to let anyone see her private part except the people of her religion.'" (Al-Bayhaqi also narrated it in al-Sunan al-Kubra 7/95 through Sa'id ibn Mansur.)

Mujahid said regarding His saying ﴿or their women﴾: "Their women are the Muslim women; the polytheist women are not among their women, and it is not permissible for a Muslim woman to uncover herself in the presence of a polytheist woman."

Ibn Kathir's commentary on Surah 24, verse 31 (part 2 of 2):

It is related by 'Abd in his *Tafsir*, from al-Kalbi, from Abu Salih, from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding ﴿or their women﴾, that he said: "They are Muslim women. She should not reveal them (her adornment) before a Jewish or Christian woman. This includes the necklace, the earrings and the broad necklace, and whatever it is not lawful for anyone to see except a mahram (a close relative whom one may never marry)."

Sa'id narrated to us from Jarir, from Layth, from Mujahid, who said: "A Muslim woman should not take off her khimar (headcover) in front of a polytheist woman, because Allah, the Exalted, says ﴿or their women﴾, and she is not one of their women."

It is also related from Makhul and 'Ubadah ibn Nusayy that they both disliked a Christian, Jewish or Magian woman kissing a Muslim woman.

As for what Ibn Abi Hatim related: "'Ali ibn al-Husayn narrated to us, Abu 'Umayr narrated to us, Damrah narrated to us, who said: Ibn 'Ata' said, from his father: 'When the Companions of the Prophet ﷺ came to Bayt al-Maqdis (Jerusalem), their midwives were Jewish and Christian women.' If this is authentic, it is to be understood as referring to a state of necessity, or that this was a matter of service (ibtihan). Furthermore, there is no uncovering of 's awrah (the parts of the body that must be covered) in it, in any case. And Allah knows best.

* *

As for His saying ﴿or those whom their right hands possess﴾, Ibn Juraij said: "That is, from the women of the polytheists. It is permissible for her to display her adornment before her (female slave), even if she is a polytheist, because she is her female slave. This is also the view of Sa'id ibn al-Musayyab. However, most scholars said: Rather, she may display (her adornment) before her male and female slaves (raqiq)." They cited the hadith which Abu Dawud related:

Muhammad ibn 'Isa narrated to us, Abu Jumay' Salim ibn Dinar narrated to us, from Thabit, from Anas, that the Prophet ﷺ came to Fatimah with a slave whom he had given to her. He said: "Fatimah had a garment which, when she covered her head with it, did not reach her feet, and when she covered her feet with it, did not reach her head. When the Prophet ﷺ saw what she was experiencing, he said: 'There is no harm for you, for he is only your father and your servant.'"[^1]

The Hafiz Ibn 'Asakir mentioned in his *Tarikh* (History), in the biography of Hudayj al-Khasi, the freedman of Mu'awiyah, that 'Abdullah ibn Mas'adah al-Fazari was very black and had very dark skin, and that the Prophet ﷺ had given him to his daughter Fatimah, and she raised him and then freed him. After all this, he was with Mu'awiyah during the days of Siffin, and he was among the fiercest people against 'Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him.[^2]

Imam Ahmad said: "Sufyan ibn 'Uyaynah narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, from Nabhan, from Umm Salamah, who mentioned that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'If one of you (women) has a mukatab (a slave who has contracted to buy his freedom), and he has the means to pay, then she should veil herself from him.'"

Abu Dawud related it from Musaddad, from Sufyan, with the same chain.[^3]

* *

As for His saying ﴿or male attendants having no physical desire﴾, that means such as hired workers and followers who are not of equal standing, and who, along with that, are lacking in their intellect and are without sexual desire for women, nor do they desire them.

Ibn 'Abbas said: "It is the dull-witted one who has no sexual desire."

Mujahid said: "It is the simpleton (ableh)."

'Ikrimah said: "It is the mukhannath (effeminate man) whose penis does not become erect." And other early scholars (salaf) said the same.

In the Sahih, from the hadith of al-Zuhri, from 'Urwah, from 'A'ishah, that a mukhannath used to enter upon the household of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, and they considered him among those without sexual desire. One day the Prophet ﷺ entered while he was describing a woman. He was saying: "When she comes forward, she comes forward with four (folds of flesh), and when she turns away, she turns away with eight." The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Do I not see that this one knows what is here? Let him not enter upon you (women) ever again." So he was banished, and he used to come to al-Bayda' every Friday to beg for food.[^4]

Imam Ahmad said: "Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, Hisham ibn 'Urwah narrated to us, from his father, from Zaynab bint Abi Salamah, from Umm Salamah, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered upon her while there was a mukhannath with her, and with her was her brother 'Abdullah ibn Abi Umayyah. The mukhannath was saying to 'Abdullah: 'O 'Abdullah ibn Abi Umayyah, if Allah grants you victory over al-Ta'if tomorrow, then (take) the daughter of Ghaylan, for she comes forward with four and turns away with eight.' She said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ heard him, and he said to Umm Salamah: 'Let this one never enter upon you.'"

Both of them (al-Bukhari and Muslim) related it in the two Sahihs, from the hadith of Hisham ibn 'Urwah, with the same chain.[^5]

Imam Ahmad said: "'Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Ma'mar narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, from 'Urwah ibn al-Zubayr, from 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: A man who was a mukhannath used to enter upon the wives of the Prophet ﷺ, and they considered him among those without sexual desire. One day the Prophet ﷺ entered while he was with some of his wives, and he was describing a woman. He said: 'When she comes forward, she comes forward with four, and when she turns away, she turns away with eight.' The Prophet ﷺ said: 'Do I not see that this one knows what is here? Let this one never enter upon you.' So they veiled him from them."

Muslim, Abu Dawud and al-Nasa'i related it through the chain of 'Abd al-Razzaq, with the same wording.[^6]

* *

As for His saying ﴿or children who have no knowledge of women's private parts﴾, that means that because of their youth they do not understand the conditions of women and their private parts from their soft speech, their graceful gait and their movements. So if the child is young and does not understand these things, there is no harm in his entering upon women. But if he is an adolescent or close to it, to the point that he knows these things and is aware of them, and distinguishes between the ugly and the beautiful, then he should not be allowed to enter upon women. It is established in the two Sahihs that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Beware of entering upon women." They said: "O Messenger of Allah, what about al-hamw (the husband's male relatives)?" He said: "Al-hamw is death."

* *

As for His saying ﴿And let them not stamp their feet so as to reveal what they hide of their adornment﴾: In the Jahiliyyah (Age of Ignorance), when a woman was walking in the street with a silent khalkhal (anklet, whose sound is not heard) on her foot, she would strike the ground with her foot, so that men would hear its jingling. So Allah forbade the believing women from doing the like of that. Similarly, if some of her adornment was concealed and she moved in a way that would reveal what was hidden, she falls under this prohibition, because of His saying, Exalted is He: ﴿And let them not stamp their feet so as to reveal what they hide of their adornment﴾. Among this also is that she is forbidden from wearing perfume and scent when she goes out of her house, so that men may smell her fragrance. Abu 'Isa al-Tirmidhi said: "Muhammad ibn Bashshar narrated to us, Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Qattan narrated to us, from Thabit ibn 'Umarah al-Hanafi, from Ghunaym ibn Qays, from Abu Musa, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: 'Every eye is adulterous, and a woman who applies perfume and then passes by a gathering is such-and-such' meaning an adulteress."

He said: "This is also narrated from Abu Hurayrah, and this hadith is hasan sahih (good and authentic)."

Abu Dawud and al-Nasa'i related it from the hadith of Thabit ibn 'Umarah, with the same chain.[^7]

Abu Dawud said: "Muhammad ibn Kathir narrated to us, Sufyan informed us, from 'Asim ibn 'Ubayd Allah, from 'Ubayd, the freedman of Abu Ruhm, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: A woman met him, and he perceived from her the scent of perfume, and her skirt was trailing behind her. He said to her: 'O maidservant of the Compeller (Jabbar), have you come from the mosque?' She said: 'Yes.' He said to her: 'Have you perfumed yourself?' She said: 'Yes.' He said: 'I heard my beloved Abu al-Qasim (the Messenger of Allah) ﷺ say: "Allah does not accept the prayer of a woman who has perfumed herself for this mosque until she returns and performs a ghusl (full washing) like her ghusl from janabah (major ritual impurity)."'"

Ibn Majah related it from Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, from Sufyan, that is Ibn 'Uyaynah, with the same chain.[^8]

Al-Tirmidhi also related from the hadith of Musa ibn 'Ubaydah, from Ayyub ibn Khalid, from Maymunah bint Sa'd, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "A woman who parades in adornment before those other than her own (family), is like the darkness of the Day of Resurrection, having no light."[^9]

Among this also is that they are forbidden to walk in the middle of the road, because of the display (tabarruj) it involves. Abu Dawud said: "al-Qa'nabi narrated to us, 'Abd al-'Aziz (that is, Ibn Muhammad) narrated to us, from Abu al-Yaman, from Shaddad ibn Abi 'Amr ibn Himas, from his father, from Hamzah ibn Abi Usayd al-Ansari, from his father, that he heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say while he was leaving the mosque, when men were mixing with women in the street: 'Hold back, for it is not for you (women) to take up the middle of the road; keep to the edges of the road.' So the woman would press herself against the wall, to the extent that her clothing would catch on the wall because of how close she pressed herself to it."[^10]

* *

As for His saying ﴿And turn to Allah in repentance, all of you, O believers, that you may succeed﴾: that is, do what I command you of these beautiful attributes and noble characteristics, and abandon what the people of the Jahiliyyah had of base characters and vile attributes. Indeed, true success lies entirely in doing what Allah and His Messenger command, and in abandoning what they forbid. And Allah, the Exalted, is the One whose help is sought, [and upon whom reliance is placed].

[^2]: Tarikh Dimashq (4/278, manuscript).
[^3]: Musnad (6/289) and Sunan Abi Dawud, hadith no. 3928.
[^4]: Sahih Muslim, hadith no. 2181, with an addition from Abu Dawud (no. 4109) through al-Zuhri, which is not in Sahih Muslim: "So he was banished, and he used to come to al-Bayda' every day of Friday..."
[^5]: Musnad (6/290), Sahih al-Bukhari no. 5887, and Sahih Muslim no. 2180.
[^6]: Musnad (6/152), Sahih Muslim no. 2181, Sunan Abi Dawud no. 4108, and al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra no. 9247.
[^7]: Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. 2786.
[^8]: Sunan Abi Dawud no. 4174 and Sunan Ibn Majah no. 4002.

[^10]: Sunan Abi Dawud no. 5272.

These noble verses contain a number of firm rulings and binding commands. His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And marry the single among you and the righteous among your male and female slaves﴾ is a command to marriage. A group of scholars held that it is obligatory upon everyone who is able to do so. They based this on the apparent meaning of the Prophet's (ﷺ) saying: "O young men, whoever among you is able to bear the expenses of marriage (al-ba'ah) should marry, for it lowers the gaze and guards the chastity. Whoever is not able should fast, for it is a shield for him." Both al-Bukhari and Muslim related it from the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (5066) and Sahih Muslim no. (1400).]].

It has come in the Sunan, through more than one route, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Marry, multiply, and propagate, for I will be proud of you before the nations on the Day of Resurrection." [[Sunan Abi Dawud no. (2050) and Sunan al-Nasa'i (6/65).]] In another narration: "Even by the miscarried fetus (al-siqt)."

Al-ayama is the plural of ayyim. It is used of a woman who has no husband and of a man who has no wife, whether he or she was previously married and then separated, or never married. Al-Jawhari related this from the lexicographers. It is said: "a man who is ayyim" and "a woman who is ayyim" as well.

* *

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿If they are poor, Allah will enrich them from His bounty, and Allah is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing﴾. Ali ibn Abi Talhah related from Ibn Abbas: Allah encouraged them to marry, commanded it for free people and slaves alike, and promised them richness through it, saying: ﴿If they are poor, Allah will enrich them from His bounty﴾.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father related to us, Mahmud ibn Khalid al-Azraq related to us, Umar ibn Abd al-Wahid related to us, from Sa'id (meaning Ibn Abd al-Aziz), who said: It reached me that Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "Obey Allah regarding what He has commanded you of marriage, and He will fulfil for you what He has promised of richness," and he recited: ﴿If they are poor, Allah will enrich them from His bounty﴾.

From Ibn Mas'ud: "Seek richness through marriage," for Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿If they are poor, Allah will enrich them from His bounty﴾. Ibn Jarir related it, and al-Baghawi mentioned a similar report from Umar.

From al-Layth, from Muhammad ibn Ajlan, from Sa'id al-Maqburi, from Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Three are a right upon Allah to help: the one who marries seeking chastity, the mukatab (slave under a contract of self-purchase) who seeks to pay, and the one who fights in the way of Allah." Related by Imam Ahmad, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah [[Musnad (2/251), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (1655), Sunan al-Nasa'i (6/61) and Sunan Ibn Majah no. (2518).]].

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) married that man who had found nothing but his waist-wrap and could not find even an iron ring; yet he married him to that woman and made his mahr (dower) that he should teach her what he had memorized of the Qur'an.

What is known of Allah's generosity and kindness is that He provides him and her with what is sufficient for them both. As for what many people cite as a hadith: "Marry the poor, Allah will enrich you," it has no basis. I have not found it in any sound or weak chain until now. The Qur'an is sufficient without it, and so is the hadith we have cited. And to Allah belongs all praise.

* *

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And let those who do not find a means of marriage keep themselves chaste until Allah enriches them from His bounty﴾. This is a command from Allah, exalted is He, to whoever cannot find the means to marry, to abstain from what is unlawful, as the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "O young men, whoever among you is able to bear the expenses of marriage should marry, for it lowers the gaze and guards the chastity. Whoever is not able should fast, for it is a shield for him."

This verse is general, while the one in Surah an-Nisa is more specific, namely His saying: ﴿And whoever among you lacks the means to marry free believing women, then let them marry from what your right hands possess of your believing young women﴾, up to: ﴿That is for whoever fears sin among you, but that you be patient is better for you﴾ [An-Nisa: 25]. That is, your patience in refraining from marrying slave women is better, because the child will be born a slave. ﴿And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾.

Ikrimah said regarding His saying: ﴿And let those who do not find a means of marriage keep themselves chaste﴾: It is the man who sees a woman and feels desire for her. If he has a wife, let him go to her and fulfil his need from her; and if he has no wife, let him contemplate the dominion of the heavens and the earth until Allah enriches him.

* *

His saying: ﴿And those who seek a contract of manumission from among those your right hands possess, write it for them if you know good in them﴾. This is a command from Allah, exalted is He, to masters: when their slaves request a contract of manumission (kitabah), they should grant it, on condition that the slave has a means and earnings by which he can pay the master the money he has stipulated. Many scholars held that this command is one of guidance and recommendation, not one of obligation and binding requirement; rather the master is free to choose: if his slave asks for a contract, he may grant it if he wishes, and if he wishes he need not grant it.

Al-Thawri related from Jabir, from al-Sha'bi: "If he wills, he may write the contract for him, and if he wills, he need not."

Ibn Wahb related from Isma'il ibn Ayyash, from a man, from Ata' ibn Abi Rabah: "If he wills, he writes it for him, and if he does not will, he does not write it." Muqatil ibn Hayyan and al-Hasan al-Basri also said the same.

Others held that when a slave asks this of his master, the master is obligated to grant what he asked, taking the apparent meaning of this command.

Al-Bukhari said: Rawh related from Ibn Jurayj: I said to Ata': "Is it obligatory upon me, if I know he has wealth, that I write a contract for him?" He said: "I do not see it as anything but obligatory." Amr ibn Dinar said: I said to Ata': "Do you report this from anyone?" He said: "No." Then he informed me that Musa ibn Anas told him that Sirin asked Anas for a contract of manumission, and he was a man of much wealth, but Anas refused.

So [Sirin] went to Umar ibn al-Khattab and said: "Write the contract for him." Anas refused, so Umar struck him with a whip, reciting: ﴿So write for them if you know good in them﴾, and so Anas wrote the contract [[Sahih al-Bukhari (5/184), Fath.]].

Al-Bukhari mentioned this in suspended form (ta'liq). Abd al-Razzaq related it: Ibn Jurayj informed us, saying: I said to Ata': "Is it obligatory upon me, if I know he has wealth, that I write a contract for him?" He said: "I do not see it as anything but obligatory." Amr ibn Dinar said: I said to Ata': "Do you report this from anyone?" He said: "No" [[Al-Tabari related it in his tafsir (18/98) through the chain of Abd al-Razzaq.]].

Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us, Muhammad ibn Bakr related to us, Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, from Anas ibn Malik: that Sirin wished to write a contract for him, but he hesitated, so Umar said to him: "You must write it for him." A sound chain [[Tafsir al-Tabari (18/98).]].

Sa'id ibn Mansur said: Hushaym ibn Juwayr related to us, from al-Dahhak, who said: "It is a firm command (azmah)."

This is the older of the two opinions of al-Shafi'i (may Allah have mercy on him). In his later opinion he held that it is not obligatory, based on the Prophet's (ﷺ) saying: "The property of a Muslim man is not lawful except with the good pleasure of his soul" [[Related by Ahmad in his Musnad (5/72) from the hadith of the paternal uncle of Abu Hurrah al-Raqqashi, and (5/425) from the hadith of Abu Humayd al-Sa'idi, and (3/423) from the hadith of Amr ibn Yathribi.]].

Ibn Wahb said: Malik said: "The matter according to us is that it is not incumbent upon the master of a slave to write a contract for him when he asks for it. I have never heard of any of the imams compelling anyone to write a contract for his slave." Malik said: "This is only a command from Allah and a permission from Him to people, not an obligation."

Al-Thawri, Abu Hanifah, Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, and others said likewise. Ibn Jarir chose the opinion of obligation, based on the apparent meaning of the verse.

* *

His saying: ﴿If you know good in them﴾. Some said: trustworthiness (amanah). Some said: truthfulness (sidq). [Some said: wealth (mal).] Some said: means of earning and gain (hilah wa kasb).

Abu Dawud related in his Kitab al-Marasil (hadith transmitted without a companion's link), from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said regarding: ﴿So write for them if you know good in them﴾: "If you know in them a craft, and do not leave them as a burden upon the people."

* *

His saying: ﴿And give them of the wealth of Allah which He has given you﴾. The commentators differed regarding it. Some said: it means remit to them part of the contract, then some said: a quarter; it was said: a third; it was said: a half; it was said: a portion of the contract without specifying.

Others said: rather, what is meant by His saying: ﴿And give them of the wealth of Allah which He has given you﴾ is the share which Allah has prescribed for them from the zakat wealth. This is the view of al-Hasan, Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam and his father, and Muqatil ibn Hayyan. Ibn Jarir chose it.

Ibrahim al-Nakha'i said regarding His saying: ﴿And give them of the wealth of Allah which He has given you﴾: "Their master and others urge the people to do so." Likewise Buraydah ibn al-Husayb al-Aslami and Qatadah said.

Ibn Abbas said: Allah commanded the believers to help with freeing the slaves (fi al-riqab). It has already been mentioned in the hadith from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Three are a right upon Allah to help," and he mentioned among them the mukatab who seeks to pay. The first opinion is more well-known.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn Isma'il related to us, Waki' related to us, from Ibn Shabib, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, from Umar: that he wrote a contract for a slave of his, named Abu Umayyah. When [the slave] brought his installment (najm) when it became due, Umar said: "O Abu Umayyah, go and use it for your contract." He said: "O Commander of the Faithful, if you left it until it is the last installment?" He said: "I fear I will not live to see that." Then he recited: ﴿So write for them if you know good in them, and give them of the wealth of Allah which He has given you﴾. Ikrimah said: That was the first installment paid in Islam.

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Humayd related to us, Harun ibn al-Mughirah related to us, from Anbasah, from Salim al-Aftas, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: "When Ibn Umar wrote a contract for his mukatab, he did not remit any part of the first installments, fearing that he might fail, and so his charity would return to him. But when [the contract] was in its last stage, he remitted whatever he wished" [[Tafsir al-Tabari (18/101).]].

Ali ibn Abi Talhah related from Ibn Abbas: ﴿And give them of the wealth of Allah which He has given you﴾: He said: that is, remit to them from their contract. Likewise Mujahid, Ata', al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazzah, Abd al-Karim ibn Malik al-Jazari, and al-Suddi said.

Muhammad ibn Sirin said regarding His saying: ﴿And give them of the wealth of Allah which He has given you﴾: "It used to please them that a man would leave a portion of his mukatab's contract to him."

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 24, verses 32–34 (part 2 of 2):

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan al-Muqri' informed us, Ibrahim ibn Musa informed us, Hisham ibn Yusuf informed us, from Ibn Juraij, who said: Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib informed me that Abdullah ibn Jundab informed him, from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "A quarter of the kitabah" [[Also narrated by Abd al-Razzaq in al-Musannaf, no. (15589), through Ibn Juraij, with the same chain. He said: "Ibn Juraij said: More than one person informed me, from Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, that he used to narrate this hadith without mentioning the Prophet (ﷺ) in it."]].

This is a gharib (rare) hadith, and its attribution to the Prophet (ﷺ) is munkar (rejected). The more likely view is that it is mawquf (ending with a Companion), reported from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, as Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, may Allah have mercy on him, transmitted it from him [[Also narrated by Abd al-Razzaq in his Musannaf, no. (15590), through Ma'mar, from Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, with the same wording.]].

* *

His saying: ﴿And do not compel your slave girls to prostitution, if they desire chastity, to seek the transient gain of worldly life﴾, and the rest of the verse. The people of the Jahiliyyah (pre-Islamic era) used to send their slave girl out to commit zina (fornication), and they would impose a tax on her which they took from her at every time. When Islam came, Allah forbade the Muslims [[In manuscripts F and A: "the believers".]] from this.

The occasion of revelation of this noble verse, as mentioned by more than one of the mufassirun (exegetes) from the al-Salaf (early generations) and al-Khalaf (later generations), concerned Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul [the hypocrite] [[Addition from F and A.]]. He had slave girls whom he compelled to prostitution, seeking their earnings, desiring their children, and seeking status thereby, as he claimed. [May Allah curse him and disgrace him.] [[Addition from F and A.]] [Mention of the reports (athar) related on this] [[Addition from F and A.]]

Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn Amr ibn Abd al-Khaliq al-Bazzar, may Allah have mercy on him, said in his Musnad: Ahmad ibn Dawud al-Wasiti narrated to us, Abu Amr al-Lakhmi, meaning Muhammad ibn al-Hajjaj, narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, who said: A slave girl belonging to Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, called Mu'adhah, used to be compelled by him to commit zina. When Islam came, this was revealed: ﴿And do not compel your slave girls to prostitution﴾ until His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah, after their compulsion, is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [[Musnad al-Bazzar, no. (2240), Kashf al-Astar. Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/83): "In it is Muhammad ibn al-Hajjaj al-Lakhmi, and he is a liar."]].

Al-A'mash said, from Abu Sufyan, from Jabir, regarding this verse: ﴿And do not compel your slave girls to prostitution﴾. He said: It was revealed concerning a slave girl of Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul called Musaykah, whom he compelled to fornication, while she was not bad [i.e., she was chaste], but she refused. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed this verse until His saying: ﴿And whoever compels them, then indeed Allah, after their compulsion, is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [[Narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (18/103), through al-A'mash, with the same chain.]].

Al-Nasa'i narrated, from the hadith of Ibn Juraij, from Abu al-Zubair, from Jabir, something similar [[Al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra, no. (11365), through Ibn Juraij, from Abu al-Zubair, with the same chain.]].

Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said: Amr ibn Ali narrated to us, Ali ibn Sa'id narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, Abu Sufyan narrated to me, from Jabir, who said: Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul had a slave girl called Musaykah, and he used to compel her to fornication. So Allah revealed: ﴿And do not compel your slave girls to prostitution﴾, until His saying: ﴿And whoever compels them, then indeed Allah, after their compulsion, is Forgiving and Merciful﴾.

Al-A'mash explicitly stated that he heard from Abu Sufyan, Talhah ibn Nafi', which refutes the view of the one who said: "He did not hear from him; it is only a written sheet (sahifah)," which al-Bazzar related.

Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said, from Sulayman ibn Mu'adh, from Simak, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas: that a slave girl of Abdullah ibn Ubayy used to commit zina in the Jahiliyyah, and she bore children from zina. He said to her: "Why do you not commit zina?" She said: "No, by Allah, I will not commit zina." So he beat her, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿And do not compel your slave girls to prostitution, if they desire chastity﴾ [[Also narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (11/284), through Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi, with the same chain.]].

Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri: that a man from Quraysh was taken captive on the day of Badr, and he was a captive with Abdullah ibn Ubayy. Abdullah ibn Ubayy had a slave girl called Mu'adhah, and the Qurashi captive wanted her for himself. She was a Muslim, and she refused him because of her Islam. Abdullah ibn Ubayy used to compel her to this and beat her, hoping that she would conceive for the Qurashi, so that he would demand a ransom for his child. So the Blessed and Exalted said: ﴿And do not compel your slave girls to prostitution, if they desire chastity﴾ [[Tafsir Abd al-Razzaq (2/50).]].

Al-Suddi said: This noble verse was revealed concerning Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, the head of the hypocrites. He had a slave girl called Mu'adhah, and whenever a guest arrived at his place, he would send her to him to have intercourse with him, desiring reward from him and honour for himself. The slave girl went to Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, and complained to him about this. Abu Bakr mentioned it to the Prophet (ﷺ), and he ordered that she be taken away from him. Abdullah ibn Ubayy shouted: "Who will excuse me from Muhammad, who overpowers us over our property?" So Allah revealed this concerning them.

Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: It has reached us, and Allah knows best, that this verse was revealed concerning two men who used to compel two of their slave girls. One of them was called Musaykah and belonged to an Ansari man, and Umaymah, the mother of Musaykah, belonged to Abdullah ibn Ubayy. Mu'adhah and Arwa were in that same position. Musaykah and her mother came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and mentioned this to him, so Allah revealed concerning that: ﴿And do not compel your slave girls to prostitution﴾, meaning: to zina.

* *

His saying: ﴿if they desire chastity﴾. This came out as the typical case (kharaja makhraj al-ghalib), so it has no implication (mafhum) that would restrict the ruling. His saying: ﴿to seek the transient gain [al-hayah] of worldly life﴾ [[Addition from F and A. It is the correct reading.]], meaning: from their earnings, their dowries, and their children.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) forbade the earnings of the cupper (hajjam), the payment of the prostitute (mahr al-baghi), and the bribe of the soothsayer (hulwan al-kahin) [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. (2237), and Muslim in his Sahih, no. (1567), from the hadith of Abu Mas'ud al-Ansari, may Allah be pleased with him: "That the Prophet (ﷺ) forbade the price of a dog, the payment of a prostitute, and the bribe of a soothsayer." As for the earnings of the cupper, Ibn Majah narrated in al-Sunan, no. (2165), from the hadith of Uqbah ibn Amr: "The Prophet (ﷺ) forbade the earnings of the cupper."]]. In another narration: "The payment of a prostitute is evil, the earnings of the cupper are evil, and the price of a dog is evil" [[Narrated by Ahmad in his Musnad (3/464), from the hadith of Rafi' ibn Khadij, may Allah be pleased with him.]].

* *

His saying: ﴿And whoever compels them, then indeed Allah, after their compulsion, is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [meaning: toward them, as has preceded in the hadith from Jabir.

Ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn Abbas: "If you do so, then indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful to them." [[Addition from F and A.]] And the sin is upon the one who compelled them. Likewise said Mujahid, Ata' al-Khurasani, al-A'mash, and Qatadah.

Abu Ubayd said: Ishaq al-Azraq narrated to me, from Awf, from al-Hasan regarding this verse: ﴿Indeed, Allah, after their compulsion, is Forgiving and Merciful﴾. He said: "To them, by Allah. To them, by Allah."

And from al-Zuhri, he said: "Forgiving to them for what they were compelled to."

And from Zayd ibn Aslam, he said: "Forgiving and Merciful to the compelled women."

Ibn al-Mundhir related these from them in his tafsir with their chains.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur'ah narrated to us, Yahya ibn Abd Allah narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to me, Ata' narrated to me, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: In the recitation of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud: "Indeed, Allah, after their compulsion, is Forgiving to them [[In F: "Forgiving to them."]] and Merciful," and their sin is upon the one who compelled them.

In the marfu' (traced to the Prophet) hadith from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), he said: "Allah has lifted from my ummah (community) error, forgetfulness, and what they are compelled to do." [[Narrated by Ibn Majah in al-Sunan, no. (2043), and its discussion has already preceded in surah al-A'raf.]]

When the Exalted had explained these rulings and clarified them, He said: ﴿And We have certainly sent down to you verses that are clear﴾, meaning: the Quran, containing clear, explanatory verses, ﴿and an example from those who passed away before you﴾, meaning: news of the past nations and what befell them due to their opposition to the commands of Allah, Exalted, as He said: ﴿So We made them a precedent and an example for later generations﴾ [Al-Zukhruf: 56].

﴿And an admonition﴾, meaning: a deterrent from committing sins and prohibited acts, ﴿for the righteous﴾, meaning: for those who fear Allah and are mindful of Him.

Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, said describing the Quran: "In it is the judgment of what is between you, the news of what came before you, and the information of what will come after you. It is the decisive word, not a jest. Whoever abandons it from a tyrant, Allah will break him, and whoever seeks guidance from other than it, Allah will lead him astray."

These noble verses contain a number of firm rulings and binding commands. His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And marry the single among you and the righteous among your male and female slaves﴾ is a command to marriage. A group of scholars held that it is obligatory upon everyone who is able to do so. They based this on the apparent meaning of the Prophet's (ﷺ) saying: "O young men, whoever among you is able to bear the expenses of marriage (al-ba'ah) should marry, for it lowers the gaze and guards the chastity. Whoever is not able should fast, for it is a shield for him." Both al-Bukhari and Muslim related it from the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (5066) and Sahih Muslim no. (1400).]].

It has come in the Sunan, through more than one route, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Marry, multiply, and propagate, for I will be proud of you before the nations on the Day of Resurrection." [[Sunan Abi Dawud no. (2050) and Sunan al-Nasa'i (6/65).]] In another narration: "Even by the miscarried fetus (al-siqt)."

Al-ayama is the plural of ayyim. It is used of a woman who has no husband and of a man who has no wife, whether he or she was previously married and then separated, or never married. Al-Jawhari related this from the lexicographers. It is said: "a man who is ayyim" and "a woman who is ayyim" as well.

* *

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿If they are poor, Allah will enrich them from His bounty, and Allah is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing﴾. Ali ibn Abi Talhah related from Ibn Abbas: Allah encouraged them to marry, commanded it for free people and slaves alike, and promised them richness through it, saying: ﴿If they are poor, Allah will enrich them from His bounty﴾.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father related to us, Mahmud ibn Khalid al-Azraq related to us, Umar ibn Abd al-Wahid related to us, from Sa'id (meaning Ibn Abd al-Aziz), who said: It reached me that Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "Obey Allah regarding what He has commanded you of marriage, and He will fulfil for you what He has promised of richness," and he recited: ﴿If they are poor, Allah will enrich them from His bounty﴾.

From Ibn Mas'ud: "Seek richness through marriage," for Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿If they are poor, Allah will enrich them from His bounty﴾. Ibn Jarir related it, and al-Baghawi mentioned a similar report from Umar.

From al-Layth, from Muhammad ibn Ajlan, from Sa'id al-Maqburi, from Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Three are a right upon Allah to help: the one who marries seeking chastity, the mukatab (slave under a contract of self-purchase) who seeks to pay, and the one who fights in the way of Allah." Related by Imam Ahmad, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah [[Musnad (2/251), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (1655), Sunan al-Nasa'i (6/61) and Sunan Ibn Majah no. (2518).]].

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) married that man who had found nothing but his waist-wrap and could not find even an iron ring; yet he married him to that woman and made his mahr (dower) that he should teach her what he had memorized of the Qur'an.

What is known of Allah's generosity and kindness is that He provides him and her with what is sufficient for them both. As for what many people cite as a hadith: "Marry the poor, Allah will enrich you," it has no basis. I have not found it in any sound or weak chain until now. The Qur'an is sufficient without it, and so is the hadith we have cited. And to Allah belongs all praise.

* *

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And let those who do not find a means of marriage keep themselves chaste until Allah enriches them from His bounty﴾. This is a command from Allah, exalted is He, to whoever cannot find the means to marry, to abstain from what is unlawful, as the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "O young men, whoever among you is able to bear the expenses of marriage should marry, for it lowers the gaze and guards the chastity. Whoever is not able should fast, for it is a shield for him."

This verse is general, while the one in Surah an-Nisa is more specific, namely His saying: ﴿And whoever among you lacks the means to marry free believing women, then let them marry from what your right hands possess of your believing young women﴾, up to: ﴿That is for whoever fears sin among you, but that you be patient is better for you﴾ [An-Nisa: 25]. That is, your patience in refraining from marrying slave women is better, because the child will be born a slave. ﴿And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾.

Ikrimah said regarding His saying: ﴿And let those who do not find a means of marriage keep themselves chaste﴾: It is the man who sees a woman and feels desire for her. If he has a wife, let him go to her and fulfil his need from her; and if he has no wife, let him contemplate the dominion of the heavens and the earth until Allah enriches him.

* *

His saying: ﴿And those who seek a contract of manumission from among those your right hands possess, write it for them if you know good in them﴾. This is a command from Allah, exalted is He, to masters: when their slaves request a contract of manumission (kitabah), they should grant it, on condition that the slave has a means and earnings by which he can pay the master the money he has stipulated. Many scholars held that this command is one of guidance and recommendation, not one of obligation and binding requirement; rather the master is free to choose: if his slave asks for a contract, he may grant it if he wishes, and if he wishes he need not grant it.

Al-Thawri related from Jabir, from al-Sha'bi: "If he wills, he may write the contract for him, and if he wills, he need not."

Ibn Wahb related from Isma'il ibn Ayyash, from a man, from Ata' ibn Abi Rabah: "If he wills, he writes it for him, and if he does not will, he does not write it." Muqatil ibn Hayyan and al-Hasan al-Basri also said the same.

Others held that when a slave asks this of his master, the master is obligated to grant what he asked, taking the apparent meaning of this command.

Al-Bukhari said: Rawh related from Ibn Jurayj: I said to Ata': "Is it obligatory upon me, if I know he has wealth, that I write a contract for him?" He said: "I do not see it as anything but obligatory." Amr ibn Dinar said: I said to Ata': "Do you report this from anyone?" He said: "No." Then he informed me that Musa ibn Anas told him that Sirin asked Anas for a contract of manumission, and he was a man of much wealth, but Anas refused.

So [Sirin] went to Umar ibn al-Khattab and said: "Write the contract for him." Anas refused, so Umar struck him with a whip, reciting: ﴿So write for them if you know good in them﴾, and so Anas wrote the contract [[Sahih al-Bukhari (5/184), Fath.]].

Al-Bukhari mentioned this in suspended form (ta'liq). Abd al-Razzaq related it: Ibn Jurayj informed us, saying: I said to Ata': "Is it obligatory upon me, if I know he has wealth, that I write a contract for him?" He said: "I do not see it as anything but obligatory." Amr ibn Dinar said: I said to Ata': "Do you report this from anyone?" He said: "No" [[Al-Tabari related it in his tafsir (18/98) through the chain of Abd al-Razzaq.]].

Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us, Muhammad ibn Bakr related to us, Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, from Anas ibn Malik: that Sirin wished to write a contract for him, but he hesitated, so Umar said to him: "You must write it for him." A sound chain [[Tafsir al-Tabari (18/98).]].

Sa'id ibn Mansur said: Hushaym ibn Juwayr related to us, from al-Dahhak, who said: "It is a firm command (azmah)."

This is the older of the two opinions of al-Shafi'i (may Allah have mercy on him). In his later opinion he held that it is not obligatory, based on the Prophet's (ﷺ) saying: "The property of a Muslim man is not lawful except with the good pleasure of his soul" [[Related by Ahmad in his Musnad (5/72) from the hadith of the paternal uncle of Abu Hurrah al-Raqqashi, and (5/425) from the hadith of Abu Humayd al-Sa'idi, and (3/423) from the hadith of Amr ibn Yathribi.]].

Ibn Wahb said: Malik said: "The matter according to us is that it is not incumbent upon the master of a slave to write a contract for him when he asks for it. I have never heard of any of the imams compelling anyone to write a contract for his slave." Malik said: "This is only a command from Allah and a permission from Him to people, not an obligation."

Al-Thawri, Abu Hanifah, Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, and others said likewise. Ibn Jarir chose the opinion of obligation, based on the apparent meaning of the verse.

* *

His saying: ﴿If you know good in them﴾. Some said: trustworthiness (amanah). Some said: truthfulness (sidq). [Some said: wealth (mal).] Some said: means of earning and gain (hilah wa kasb).

Abu Dawud related in his Kitab al-Marasil (hadith transmitted without a companion's link), from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said regarding: ﴿So write for them if you know good in them﴾: "If you know in them a craft, and do not leave them as a burden upon the people."

* *

His saying: ﴿And give them of the wealth of Allah which He has given you﴾. The commentators differed regarding it. Some said: it means remit to them part of the contract, then some said: a quarter; it was said: a third; it was said: a half; it was said: a portion of the contract without specifying.

Others said: rather, what is meant by His saying: ﴿And give them of the wealth of Allah which He has given you﴾ is the share which Allah has prescribed for them from the zakat wealth. This is the view of al-Hasan, Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam and his father, and Muqatil ibn Hayyan. Ibn Jarir chose it.

Ibrahim al-Nakha'i said regarding His saying: ﴿And give them of the wealth of Allah which He has given you﴾: "Their master and others urge the people to do so." Likewise Buraydah ibn al-Husayb al-Aslami and Qatadah said.

Ibn Abbas said: Allah commanded the believers to help with freeing the slaves (fi al-riqab). It has already been mentioned in the hadith from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Three are a right upon Allah to help," and he mentioned among them the mukatab who seeks to pay. The first opinion is more well-known.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn Isma'il related to us, Waki' related to us, from Ibn Shabib, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, from Umar: that he wrote a contract for a slave of his, named Abu Umayyah. When [the slave] brought his installment (najm) when it became due, Umar said: "O Abu Umayyah, go and use it for your contract." He said: "O Commander of the Faithful, if you left it until it is the last installment?" He said: "I fear I will not live to see that." Then he recited: ﴿So write for them if you know good in them, and give them of the wealth of Allah which He has given you﴾. Ikrimah said: That was the first installment paid in Islam.

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Humayd related to us, Harun ibn al-Mughirah related to us, from Anbasah, from Salim al-Aftas, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: "When Ibn Umar wrote a contract for his mukatab, he did not remit any part of the first installments, fearing that he might fail, and so his charity would return to him. But when [the contract] was in its last stage, he remitted whatever he wished" [[Tafsir al-Tabari (18/101).]].

Ali ibn Abi Talhah related from Ibn Abbas: ﴿And give them of the wealth of Allah which He has given you﴾: He said: that is, remit to them from their contract. Likewise Mujahid, Ata', al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazzah, Abd al-Karim ibn Malik al-Jazari, and al-Suddi said.

Muhammad ibn Sirin said regarding His saying: ﴿And give them of the wealth of Allah which He has given you﴾: "It used to please them that a man would leave a portion of his mukatab's contract to him."

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 24, verses 32–34 (part 2 of 2):

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan al-Muqri' informed us, Ibrahim ibn Musa informed us, Hisham ibn Yusuf informed us, from Ibn Juraij, who said: Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib informed me that Abdullah ibn Jundab informed him, from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "A quarter of the kitabah" [[Also narrated by Abd al-Razzaq in al-Musannaf, no. (15589), through Ibn Juraij, with the same chain. He said: "Ibn Juraij said: More than one person informed me, from Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, that he used to narrate this hadith without mentioning the Prophet (ﷺ) in it."]].

This is a gharib (rare) hadith, and its attribution to the Prophet (ﷺ) is munkar (rejected). The more likely view is that it is mawquf (ending with a Companion), reported from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, as Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, may Allah have mercy on him, transmitted it from him [[Also narrated by Abd al-Razzaq in his Musannaf, no. (15590), through Ma'mar, from Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, with the same wording.]].

* *

His saying: ﴿And do not compel your slave girls to prostitution, if they desire chastity, to seek the transient gain of worldly life﴾, and the rest of the verse. The people of the Jahiliyyah (pre-Islamic era) used to send their slave girl out to commit zina (fornication), and they would impose a tax on her which they took from her at every time. When Islam came, Allah forbade the Muslims [[In manuscripts F and A: "the believers".]] from this.

The occasion of revelation of this noble verse, as mentioned by more than one of the mufassirun (exegetes) from the al-Salaf (early generations) and al-Khalaf (later generations), concerned Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul [the hypocrite] [[Addition from F and A.]]. He had slave girls whom he compelled to prostitution, seeking their earnings, desiring their children, and seeking status thereby, as he claimed. [May Allah curse him and disgrace him.] [[Addition from F and A.]] [Mention of the reports (athar) related on this] [[Addition from F and A.]]

Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn Amr ibn Abd al-Khaliq al-Bazzar, may Allah have mercy on him, said in his Musnad: Ahmad ibn Dawud al-Wasiti narrated to us, Abu Amr al-Lakhmi, meaning Muhammad ibn al-Hajjaj, narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, who said: A slave girl belonging to Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, called Mu'adhah, used to be compelled by him to commit zina. When Islam came, this was revealed: ﴿And do not compel your slave girls to prostitution﴾ until His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah, after their compulsion, is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [[Musnad al-Bazzar, no. (2240), Kashf al-Astar. Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/83): "In it is Muhammad ibn al-Hajjaj al-Lakhmi, and he is a liar."]].

Al-A'mash said, from Abu Sufyan, from Jabir, regarding this verse: ﴿And do not compel your slave girls to prostitution﴾. He said: It was revealed concerning a slave girl of Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul called Musaykah, whom he compelled to fornication, while she was not bad [i.e., she was chaste], but she refused. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed this verse until His saying: ﴿And whoever compels them, then indeed Allah, after their compulsion, is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [[Narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (18/103), through al-A'mash, with the same chain.]].

Al-Nasa'i narrated, from the hadith of Ibn Juraij, from Abu al-Zubair, from Jabir, something similar [[Al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra, no. (11365), through Ibn Juraij, from Abu al-Zubair, with the same chain.]].

Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said: Amr ibn Ali narrated to us, Ali ibn Sa'id narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, Abu Sufyan narrated to me, from Jabir, who said: Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul had a slave girl called Musaykah, and he used to compel her to fornication. So Allah revealed: ﴿And do not compel your slave girls to prostitution﴾, until His saying: ﴿And whoever compels them, then indeed Allah, after their compulsion, is Forgiving and Merciful﴾.

Al-A'mash explicitly stated that he heard from Abu Sufyan, Talhah ibn Nafi', which refutes the view of the one who said: "He did not hear from him; it is only a written sheet (sahifah)," which al-Bazzar related.

Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said, from Sulayman ibn Mu'adh, from Simak, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas: that a slave girl of Abdullah ibn Ubayy used to commit zina in the Jahiliyyah, and she bore children from zina. He said to her: "Why do you not commit zina?" She said: "No, by Allah, I will not commit zina." So he beat her, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿And do not compel your slave girls to prostitution, if they desire chastity﴾ [[Also narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (11/284), through Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi, with the same chain.]].

Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri: that a man from Quraysh was taken captive on the day of Badr, and he was a captive with Abdullah ibn Ubayy. Abdullah ibn Ubayy had a slave girl called Mu'adhah, and the Qurashi captive wanted her for himself. She was a Muslim, and she refused him because of her Islam. Abdullah ibn Ubayy used to compel her to this and beat her, hoping that she would conceive for the Qurashi, so that he would demand a ransom for his child. So the Blessed and Exalted said: ﴿And do not compel your slave girls to prostitution, if they desire chastity﴾ [[Tafsir Abd al-Razzaq (2/50).]].

Al-Suddi said: This noble verse was revealed concerning Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, the head of the hypocrites. He had a slave girl called Mu'adhah, and whenever a guest arrived at his place, he would send her to him to have intercourse with him, desiring reward from him and honour for himself. The slave girl went to Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, and complained to him about this. Abu Bakr mentioned it to the Prophet (ﷺ), and he ordered that she be taken away from him. Abdullah ibn Ubayy shouted: "Who will excuse me from Muhammad, who overpowers us over our property?" So Allah revealed this concerning them.

Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: It has reached us, and Allah knows best, that this verse was revealed concerning two men who used to compel two of their slave girls. One of them was called Musaykah and belonged to an Ansari man, and Umaymah, the mother of Musaykah, belonged to Abdullah ibn Ubayy. Mu'adhah and Arwa were in that same position. Musaykah and her mother came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and mentioned this to him, so Allah revealed concerning that: ﴿And do not compel your slave girls to prostitution﴾, meaning: to zina.

* *

His saying: ﴿if they desire chastity﴾. This came out as the typical case (kharaja makhraj al-ghalib), so it has no implication (mafhum) that would restrict the ruling. His saying: ﴿to seek the transient gain [al-hayah] of worldly life﴾ [[Addition from F and A. It is the correct reading.]], meaning: from their earnings, their dowries, and their children.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) forbade the earnings of the cupper (hajjam), the payment of the prostitute (mahr al-baghi), and the bribe of the soothsayer (hulwan al-kahin) [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. (2237), and Muslim in his Sahih, no. (1567), from the hadith of Abu Mas'ud al-Ansari, may Allah be pleased with him: "That the Prophet (ﷺ) forbade the price of a dog, the payment of a prostitute, and the bribe of a soothsayer." As for the earnings of the cupper, Ibn Majah narrated in al-Sunan, no. (2165), from the hadith of Uqbah ibn Amr: "The Prophet (ﷺ) forbade the earnings of the cupper."]]. In another narration: "The payment of a prostitute is evil, the earnings of the cupper are evil, and the price of a dog is evil" [[Narrated by Ahmad in his Musnad (3/464), from the hadith of Rafi' ibn Khadij, may Allah be pleased with him.]].

* *

His saying: ﴿And whoever compels them, then indeed Allah, after their compulsion, is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [meaning: toward them, as has preceded in the hadith from Jabir.

Ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn Abbas: "If you do so, then indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful to them." [[Addition from F and A.]] And the sin is upon the one who compelled them. Likewise said Mujahid, Ata' al-Khurasani, al-A'mash, and Qatadah.

Abu Ubayd said: Ishaq al-Azraq narrated to me, from Awf, from al-Hasan regarding this verse: ﴿Indeed, Allah, after their compulsion, is Forgiving and Merciful﴾. He said: "To them, by Allah. To them, by Allah."

And from al-Zuhri, he said: "Forgiving to them for what they were compelled to."

And from Zayd ibn Aslam, he said: "Forgiving and Merciful to the compelled women."

Ibn al-Mundhir related these from them in his tafsir with their chains.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur'ah narrated to us, Yahya ibn Abd Allah narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to me, Ata' narrated to me, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: In the recitation of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud: "Indeed, Allah, after their compulsion, is Forgiving to them [[In F: "Forgiving to them."]] and Merciful," and their sin is upon the one who compelled them.

In the marfu' (traced to the Prophet) hadith from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), he said: "Allah has lifted from my ummah (community) error, forgetfulness, and what they are compelled to do." [[Narrated by Ibn Majah in al-Sunan, no. (2043), and its discussion has already preceded in surah al-A'raf.]]

﴿And an admonition﴾, meaning: a deterrent from committing sins and prohibited acts, ﴿for the righteous﴾, meaning: for those who fear Allah and are mindful of Him.

It is the decisive word, not a jest. Whoever abandons it from a tyrant, Allah will break him, and whoever seeks guidance from other than it, Allah will lead him astray."

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And marry the single among you and the righteous among your male and female slaves﴾ is a command to marriage. A group of scholars held that it is obligatory upon everyone who is able to do so. They based this on the apparent meaning of the Prophet's (ﷺ) saying: "O young men, whoever among you is able to bear the expenses of marriage (al-ba'ah) should marry, for it lowers the gaze and guards the chastity. Whoever is not able should fast, for it is a shield for him." Both al-Bukhari and Muslim related it from the hadith of Ibn Mas'ud [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (5066) and Sahih Muslim no. (1400).]].

It has come in the Sunan, through more than one route, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Marry, multiply, and propagate, for I will be proud of you before the nations on the Day of Resurrection." [[Sunan Abi Dawud no. (2050) and Sunan al-Nasa'i (6/65).]] In another narration: "Even by the miscarried fetus (al-siqt)."

* *

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿If they are poor, Allah will enrich them from His bounty, and Allah is All-Encompassing, All-Knowing﴾. Ali ibn Abi Talhah related from Ibn Abbas: Allah encouraged them to marry, commanded it for free people and slaves alike, and promised them richness through it, saying: ﴿If they are poor, Allah will enrich them from His bounty﴾.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father related to us, Mahmud ibn Khalid al-Azraq related to us, Umar ibn Abd al-Wahid related to us, from Sa'id (meaning Ibn Abd al-Aziz), who said: It reached me that Abu Bakr al-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him) said: "Obey Allah regarding what He has commanded you of marriage, and He will fulfil for you what He has promised of richness," and he recited: ﴿If they are poor, Allah will enrich them from His bounty﴾.

From Ibn Mas'ud: "Seek richness through marriage," for Allah, exalted is He, says: ﴿If they are poor, Allah will enrich them from His bounty﴾. Ibn Jarir related it, and al-Baghawi mentioned a similar report from Umar.

From al-Layth, from Muhammad ibn Ajlan, from Sa'id al-Maqburi, from Abu Hurayrah (may Allah be pleased with him), who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Three are a right upon Allah to help: the one who marries seeking chastity, the mukatab (slave under a contract of self-purchase) who seeks to pay, and the one who fights in the way of Allah." Related by Imam Ahmad, al-Tirmidhi, al-Nasa'i and Ibn Majah [[Musnad (2/251), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (1655), Sunan al-Nasa'i (6/61) and Sunan Ibn Majah no. (2518).]].

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) married that man who had found nothing but his waist-wrap and could not find even an iron ring; yet he married him to that woman and made his mahr (dower) that he should teach her what he had memorized of the Qur'an.

What is known of Allah's generosity and kindness is that He provides him and her with what is sufficient for them both. As for what many people cite as a hadith: "Marry the poor, Allah will enrich you," it has no basis. I have not found it in any sound or weak chain until now. The Qur'an is sufficient without it, and so is the hadith we have cited. And to Allah belongs all praise.

* *

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And let those who do not find a means of marriage keep themselves chaste until Allah enriches them from His bounty﴾.
