This is a command from Allah, exalted is He, to whoever cannot find the means to marry, to abstain from what is unlawful, as the Prophet (ﷺ) said: "O young men, whoever among you is able to bear the expenses of marriage should marry, for it lowers the gaze and guards the chastity. Whoever is not able should fast, for it is a shield for him."

This verse is general, while the one in Surah an-Nisa is more specific, namely His saying: ﴿And whoever among you lacks the means to marry free believing women, then let them marry from what your right hands possess of your believing young women﴾, up to: ﴿That is for whoever fears sin among you, but that you be patient is better for you﴾ [An-Nisa: 25]. That is, your patience in refraining from marrying slave women is better, because the child will be born a slave. ﴿And Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾.

Ikrimah said regarding His saying: ﴿And let those who do not find a means of marriage keep themselves chaste﴾: It is the man who sees a woman and feels desire for her. If he has a wife, let him go to her and fulfil his need from her; and if he has no wife, let him contemplate the dominion of the heavens and the earth until Allah enriches him.

* *

His saying: ﴿And those who seek a contract of manumission from among those your right hands possess, write it for them if you know good in them﴾. This is a command from Allah, exalted is He, to masters: when their slaves request a contract of manumission (kitabah), they should grant it, on condition that the slave has a means and earnings by which he can pay the master the money he has stipulated. Many scholars held that this command is one of guidance and recommendation, not one of obligation and binding requirement; rather the master is free to choose: if his slave asks for a contract, he may grant it if he wishes, and if he wishes he need not grant it.

Al-Thawri related from Jabir, from al-Sha'bi: "If he wills, he may write the contract for him, and if he wills, he need not."

Ibn Wahb related from Isma'il ibn Ayyash, from a man, from Ata' ibn Abi Rabah: "If he wills, he writes it for him, and if he does not will, he does not write it." Muqatil ibn Hayyan and al-Hasan al-Basri also said the same.

Others held that when a slave asks this of his master, the master is obligated to grant what he asked, taking the apparent meaning of this command.

Al-Bukhari said: Rawh related from Ibn Jurayj: I said to Ata': "Is it obligatory upon me, if I know he has wealth, that I write a contract for him?" He said: "I do not see it as anything but obligatory." Amr ibn Dinar said: I said to Ata': "Do you report this from anyone?" He said: "No." Then he informed me that Musa ibn Anas told him that Sirin asked Anas for a contract of manumission, and he was a man of much wealth, but Anas refused.

So [Sirin] went to Umar ibn al-Khattab and said: "Write the contract for him." Anas refused, so Umar struck him with a whip, reciting: ﴿So write for them if you know good in them﴾, and so Anas wrote the contract [[Sahih al-Bukhari (5/184), Fath.]].

Al-Bukhari mentioned this in suspended form (ta'liq). Abd al-Razzaq related it: Ibn Jurayj informed us, saying: I said to Ata': "Is it obligatory upon me, if I know he has wealth, that I write a contract for him?" He said: "I do not see it as anything but obligatory." Amr ibn Dinar said: I said to Ata': "Do you report this from anyone?" He said: "No" [[Al-Tabari related it in his tafsir (18/98) through the chain of Abd al-Razzaq.]].

Ibn Jarir said: Muhammad ibn Bashshar related to us, Muhammad ibn Bakr related to us, Sa'id related to us, from Qatadah, from Anas ibn Malik: that Sirin wished to write a contract for him, but he hesitated, so Umar said to him: "You must write it for him." A sound chain [[Tafsir al-Tabari (18/98).]].

Sa'id ibn Mansur said: Hushaym ibn Juwayr related to us, from al-Dahhak, who said: "It is a firm command (azmah)."

This is the older of the two opinions of al-Shafi'i (may Allah have mercy on him). In his later opinion he held that it is not obligatory, based on the Prophet's (ﷺ) saying: "The property of a Muslim man is not lawful except with the good pleasure of his soul" [[Related by Ahmad in his Musnad (5/72) from the hadith of the paternal uncle of Abu Hurrah al-Raqqashi, and (5/425) from the hadith of Abu Humayd al-Sa'idi, and (3/423) from the hadith of Amr ibn Yathribi.]].

Ibn Wahb said: Malik said: "The matter according to us is that it is not incumbent upon the master of a slave to write a contract for him when he asks for it. I have never heard of any of the imams compelling anyone to write a contract for his slave." Malik said: "This is only a command from Allah and a permission from Him to people, not an obligation."

Al-Thawri, Abu Hanifah, Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam, and others said likewise. Ibn Jarir chose the opinion of obligation, based on the apparent meaning of the verse.

* *

His saying: ﴿If you know good in them﴾. Some said: trustworthiness (amanah). Some said: truthfulness (sidq). [Some said: wealth (mal).] Some said: means of earning and gain (hilah wa kasb).

Abu Dawud related in his Kitab al-Marasil (hadith transmitted without a companion's link), from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said regarding: ﴿So write for them if you know good in them﴾: "If you know in them a craft, and do not leave them as a burden upon the people."

* *

His saying: ﴿And give them of the wealth of Allah which He has given you﴾. The commentators differed regarding it. Some said: it means remit to them part of the contract, then some said: a quarter; it was said: a third; it was said: a half; it was said: a portion of the contract without specifying.

Others said: rather, what is meant by His saying: ﴿And give them of the wealth of Allah which He has given you﴾ is the share which Allah has prescribed for them from the zakat wealth. This is the view of al-Hasan, Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam and his father, and Muqatil ibn Hayyan. Ibn Jarir chose it.

Ibrahim al-Nakha'i said regarding His saying: ﴿And give them of the wealth of Allah which He has given you﴾: "Their master and others urge the people to do so." Likewise Buraydah ibn al-Husayb al-Aslami and Qatadah said.

Ibn Abbas said: Allah commanded the believers to help with freeing the slaves (fi al-riqab). It has already been mentioned in the hadith from the Prophet (ﷺ) that he said: "Three are a right upon Allah to help," and he mentioned among them the mukatab who seeks to pay. The first opinion is more well-known.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn Isma'il related to us, Waki' related to us, from Ibn Shabib, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas, from Umar: that he wrote a contract for a slave of his, named Abu Umayyah. When [the slave] brought his installment (najm) when it became due, Umar said: "O Abu Umayyah, go and use it for your contract." He said: "O Commander of the Faithful, if you left it until it is the last installment?" He said: "I fear I will not live to see that." Then he recited: ﴿So write for them if you know good in them, and give them of the wealth of Allah which He has given you﴾. Ikrimah said: That was the first installment paid in Islam.

Ibn Jarir said: Ibn Humayd related to us, Harun ibn al-Mughirah related to us, from Anbasah, from Salim al-Aftas, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: "When Ibn Umar wrote a contract for his mukatab, he did not remit any part of the first installments, fearing that he might fail, and so his charity would return to him. But when [the contract] was in its last stage, he remitted whatever he wished" [[Tafsir al-Tabari (18/101).]].

Ali ibn Abi Talhah related from Ibn Abbas: ﴿And give them of the wealth of Allah which He has given you﴾: He said: that is, remit to them from their contract. Likewise Mujahid, Ata', al-Qasim ibn Abi Bazzah, Abd al-Karim ibn Malik al-Jazari, and al-Suddi said.

Muhammad ibn Sirin said regarding His saying: ﴿And give them of the wealth of Allah which He has given you﴾: "It used to please them that a man would leave a portion of his mukatab's contract to him."

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 24, verses 32–34 (part 2 of 2):

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Al-Fadl ibn Shadhan al-Muqri' informed us, Ibrahim ibn Musa informed us, Hisham ibn Yusuf informed us, from Ibn Juraij, who said: Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib informed me that Abdullah ibn Jundab informed him, from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "A quarter of the kitabah" [[Also narrated by Abd al-Razzaq in al-Musannaf, no. (15589), through Ibn Juraij, with the same chain. He said: "Ibn Juraij said: More than one person informed me, from Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, that he used to narrate this hadith without mentioning the Prophet (ﷺ) in it."]].

This is a gharib (rare) hadith, and its attribution to the Prophet (ﷺ) is munkar (rejected). The more likely view is that it is mawquf (ending with a Companion), reported from Ali, may Allah be pleased with him, as Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, may Allah have mercy on him, transmitted it from him [[Also narrated by Abd al-Razzaq in his Musannaf, no. (15590), through Ma'mar, from Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Sulami, with the same wording.]].

* *

His saying: ﴿And do not compel your slave girls to prostitution, if they desire chastity, to seek the transient gain of worldly life﴾, and the rest of the verse. The people of the Jahiliyyah (pre-Islamic era) used to send their slave girl out to commit zina (fornication), and they would impose a tax on her which they took from her at every time. When Islam came, Allah forbade the Muslims [[In manuscripts F and A: "the believers".]] from this.

The occasion of revelation of this noble verse, as mentioned by more than one of the mufassirun (exegetes) from the al-Salaf (early generations) and al-Khalaf (later generations), concerned Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul [the hypocrite] [[Addition from F and A.]]. He had slave girls whom he compelled to prostitution, seeking their earnings, desiring their children, and seeking status thereby, as he claimed. [May Allah curse him and disgrace him.] [[Addition from F and A.]] [Mention of the reports (athar) related on this] [[Addition from F and A.]]

Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr Ahmad ibn Amr ibn Abd al-Khaliq al-Bazzar, may Allah have mercy on him, said in his Musnad: Ahmad ibn Dawud al-Wasiti narrated to us, Abu Amr al-Lakhmi, meaning Muhammad ibn al-Hajjaj, narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated to us, from al-Zuhri, who said: A slave girl belonging to Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, called Mu'adhah, used to be compelled by him to commit zina. When Islam came, this was revealed: ﴿And do not compel your slave girls to prostitution﴾ until His saying: ﴿Indeed, Allah, after their compulsion, is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [[Musnad al-Bazzar, no. (2240), Kashf al-Astar. Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (7/83): "In it is Muhammad ibn al-Hajjaj al-Lakhmi, and he is a liar."]].

Al-A'mash said, from Abu Sufyan, from Jabir, regarding this verse: ﴿And do not compel your slave girls to prostitution﴾. He said: It was revealed concerning a slave girl of Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul called Musaykah, whom he compelled to fornication, while she was not bad [i.e., she was chaste], but she refused. So Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed this verse until His saying: ﴿And whoever compels them, then indeed Allah, after their compulsion, is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [[Narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (18/103), through al-A'mash, with the same chain.]].

Al-Nasa'i narrated, from the hadith of Ibn Juraij, from Abu al-Zubair, from Jabir, something similar [[Al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra, no. (11365), through Ibn Juraij, from Abu al-Zubair, with the same chain.]].

Al-Hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said: Amr ibn Ali narrated to us, Ali ibn Sa'id narrated to us, al-A'mash narrated to us, Abu Sufyan narrated to me, from Jabir, who said: Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul had a slave girl called Musaykah, and he used to compel her to fornication. So Allah revealed: ﴿And do not compel your slave girls to prostitution﴾, until His saying: ﴿And whoever compels them, then indeed Allah, after their compulsion, is Forgiving and Merciful﴾.

Al-A'mash explicitly stated that he heard from Abu Sufyan, Talhah ibn Nafi', which refutes the view of the one who said: "He did not hear from him; it is only a written sheet (sahifah)," which al-Bazzar related.

Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi said, from Sulayman ibn Mu'adh, from Simak, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas: that a slave girl of Abdullah ibn Ubayy used to commit zina in the Jahiliyyah, and she bore children from zina. He said to her: "Why do you not commit zina?" She said: "No, by Allah, I will not commit zina." So he beat her, and Allah, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿And do not compel your slave girls to prostitution, if they desire chastity﴾ [[Also narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (11/284), through Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi, with the same chain.]].

Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar informed us, from al-Zuhri: that a man from Quraysh was taken captive on the day of Badr, and he was a captive with Abdullah ibn Ubayy. Abdullah ibn Ubayy had a slave girl called Mu'adhah, and the Qurashi captive wanted her for himself. She was a Muslim, and she refused him because of her Islam. Abdullah ibn Ubayy used to compel her to this and beat her, hoping that she would conceive for the Qurashi, so that he would demand a ransom for his child. So the Blessed and Exalted said: ﴿And do not compel your slave girls to prostitution, if they desire chastity﴾ [[Tafsir Abd al-Razzaq (2/50).]].

Al-Suddi said: This noble verse was revealed concerning Abdullah ibn Ubayy ibn Salul, the head of the hypocrites. He had a slave girl called Mu'adhah, and whenever a guest arrived at his place, he would send her to him to have intercourse with him, desiring reward from him and honour for himself. The slave girl went to Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, and complained to him about this. Abu Bakr mentioned it to the Prophet (ﷺ), and he ordered that she be taken away from him. Abdullah ibn Ubayy shouted: "Who will excuse me from Muhammad, who overpowers us over our property?" So Allah revealed this concerning them.

Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: It has reached us, and Allah knows best, that this verse was revealed concerning two men who used to compel two of their slave girls. One of them was called Musaykah and belonged to an Ansari man, and Umaymah, the mother of Musaykah, belonged to Abdullah ibn Ubayy. Mu'adhah and Arwa were in that same position. Musaykah and her mother came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and mentioned this to him, so Allah revealed concerning that: ﴿And do not compel your slave girls to prostitution﴾, meaning: to zina.

* *

His saying: ﴿if they desire chastity﴾. This came out as the typical case (kharaja makhraj al-ghalib), so it has no implication (mafhum) that would restrict the ruling. His saying: ﴿to seek the transient gain [al-hayah] of worldly life﴾ [[Addition from F and A. It is the correct reading.]], meaning: from their earnings, their dowries, and their children.

The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) forbade the earnings of the cupper (hajjam), the payment of the prostitute (mahr al-baghi), and the bribe of the soothsayer (hulwan al-kahin) [[Narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. (2237), and Muslim in his Sahih, no. (1567), from the hadith of Abu Mas'ud al-Ansari, may Allah be pleased with him: "That the Prophet (ﷺ) forbade the price of a dog, the payment of a prostitute, and the bribe of a soothsayer." As for the earnings of the cupper, Ibn Majah narrated in al-Sunan, no. (2165), from the hadith of Uqbah ibn Amr: "The Prophet (ﷺ) forbade the earnings of the cupper."]]. In another narration: "The payment of a prostitute is evil, the earnings of the cupper are evil, and the price of a dog is evil" [[Narrated by Ahmad in his Musnad (3/464), from the hadith of Rafi' ibn Khadij, may Allah be pleased with him.]].

* *

His saying: ﴿And whoever compels them, then indeed Allah, after their compulsion, is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ [meaning: toward them, as has preceded in the hadith from Jabir.

Ibn Abi Talhah narrated from Ibn Abbas: "If you do so, then indeed Allah is Forgiving and Merciful to them." [[Addition from F and A.]] And the sin is upon the one who compelled them. Likewise said Mujahid, Ata' al-Khurasani, al-A'mash, and Qatadah.

Abu Ubayd said: Ishaq al-Azraq narrated to me, from Awf, from al-Hasan regarding this verse: ﴿Indeed, Allah, after their compulsion, is Forgiving and Merciful﴾. He said: "To them, by Allah. To them, by Allah."

And from al-Zuhri, he said: "Forgiving to them for what they were compelled to."

And from Zayd ibn Aslam, he said: "Forgiving and Merciful to the compelled women."

Ibn al-Mundhir related these from them in his tafsir with their chains.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Abu Zur'ah narrated to us, Yahya ibn Abd Allah narrated to us, Ibn Lahi'ah narrated to me, Ata' narrated to me, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: In the recitation of Abdullah ibn Mas'ud: "Indeed, Allah, after their compulsion, is Forgiving to them [[In F: "Forgiving to them."]] and Merciful," and their sin is upon the one who compelled them.

In the marfu' (traced to the Prophet) hadith from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), he said: "Allah has lifted from my ummah (community) error, forgetfulness, and what they are compelled to do." [[Narrated by Ibn Majah in al-Sunan, no. (2043), and its discussion has already preceded in surah al-A'raf.]]

When the Exalted had explained these rulings and clarified them, He said: ﴿And We have certainly sent down to you verses that are clear﴾, meaning: the Quran, containing clear, explanatory verses, ﴿and an example from those who passed away before you﴾, meaning: news of the past nations and what befell them due to their opposition to the commands of Allah, Exalted, as He said: ﴿So We made them a precedent and an example for later generations﴾ [Al-Zukhruf: 56].

﴿And an admonition﴾, meaning: a deterrent from committing sins and prohibited acts, ﴿for the righteous﴾, meaning: for those who fear Allah and are mindful of Him.

Ali ibn Abi Talib, may Allah be pleased with him, said describing the Quran: "In it is the judgment of what is between you, the news of what came before you, and the information of what will come after you. It is the decisive word, not a jest. Whoever abandons it from a tyrant, Allah will break him, and whoever seeks guidance from other than it, Allah will lead him astray."

Ali ibn Abi Talhah reported from Ibn Abbas regarding ﴿Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth﴾ that it means: the Guide of the people of the heavens and the earth.

Ibn Jurayj said: Mujahid and Ibn Abbas said concerning His words ﴿Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth﴾: He manages the affair within them, their stars, their sun and their moon.

Ibn Jarir said: Sulayman ibn Umar ibn Khalid al-Raqqi related to us, from Wahb ibn Rashid, from Farqad, from Anas ibn Malik, who said: "Indeed My God says: My light is My guidance."

Ibn Jarir chose this view, may Allah have mercy on him.

Abu Ja'far al-Razi said, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, from Abu al-'Aliyah, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, concerning the saying of Allah the Exalted ﴿Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth﴾: He said: It is the believer in whose breast Allah placed [Allah] faith and the Qur'an. Allah then struck a parable for him, saying: ﴿Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth﴾, beginning with His own light, then He mentioned the light of the believer, saying: "the likeness of the light of one who believes in Him." He said: Ubayy ibn Ka'b used to recite it: "the likeness of the light of one who believes in Allah, and he is the believer in whose breast faith and the Qur'an have been placed."

In the same way, Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Qays ibn Sa'd related from Ibn Abbas that he recited it thus: "the light of one who believes in Allah."

Some of them recited: "Allah has illuminated the heavens and the earth."

And from al-Dahhak: "Allah has illuminated the heavens and the earth."

Al-Suddi said concerning His words ﴿Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth﴾: By His light the heavens and the earth were illuminated.

In the hadith which Muhammad ibn Ishaq narrated in the Sirah, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that he said in his supplication on the day the people of al-Ta'if harmed him: "I seek refuge in the light of Your Face, by which the darknesses are illuminated and by which the affairs of this world and the Hereafter are set right, that Your anger should descend upon me or Your wrath should alight upon me. To You belongs the reproach until You are pleased, and there is no power and no strength except by You." [Ibn Hisham related it in al-Sirah al-Nabawiyyah (1/420), from Ibn Ishaq.]

In the Two Sahihs, from Ibn Abbas: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), when he rose at night, would say: "O Allah, to You be praise. You are the Sustainer of the heavens and the earth and whatever is in them. To You be praise. You are the Light of the heavens and the earth and whatever is in them." The hadith... [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (1120) and Sahih Muslim no. (769).]

And from Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: Indeed your Lord has no night or day; the light of the Throne is from the light of His Face.

* *

As for His words ﴿the likeness of His light﴾, there are two views regarding this pronoun:

The first: it refers back to Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, meaning: the likeness of His guidance in the heart of the believer, as said by Ibn Abbas, ﴿as a niche﴾.

The second: the pronoun refers back to the believer, which the context of the speech indicates. Its implied meaning is: the likeness of the light of the believer that is in his heart, as a niche. He likened the heart of the believer and what it is innately disposed to of guidance, and what it receives of the Qur'an that corresponds to what it is innately disposed to, as the Exalted said: ﴿Is one who has clear proof from his Lord and is followed by a witness from Him?﴾ [Hud: 17]. He likened the heart of the [believer] in its purity within itself to a lamp of transparent, gem-like glass, and what it draws guidance from in the Qur'an and the Shari'ah to pure, good, bright, balanced oil, which has no turbidity and no deviation.

As for His words ﴿as a niche﴾: Ibn Abbas, Mujahid, Muhammad ibn Ka'b and others said: it is the place of the wick in the lamp. This is the well-known view; therefore He said after it: ﴿in it is a lamp﴾, which is the wick that gives light.

Al-Awfi related from Ibn Abbas concerning His words ﴿Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth. The likeness of His light is as a niche in which is a lamp﴾: The Jews said to Muhammad (ﷺ): "How can the light of Allah be reached beyond the sky?" So Allah struck this parable for His light, saying: ﴿Allah is the Light of the heavens and the earth. The likeness of His light...﴾. And the mishkah is a recess in the house. He said: It is a parable which Allah struck for His obedience; He named His obedience light, then named it various kinds.

Ibn Abi Najih related from Mujahid: the kuwwah (recess) is in the language of Abyssinia. Another added: the mishkah is a recess with no opening. And from Mujahid: the mishkah is the iron rods on which the lamp is hung.

The first view is more preferable, namely that the mishkah is the place of the wick in the lamp; therefore He said: ﴿in it is a lamp﴾, which is the light in the wick.

Ubayy ibn Ka'b said: the lamp is the light, which is the Qur'an and the faith in his breast.

Al-Suddi said: it is the lamp (siraj).

﴿The lamp is in a glass﴾, meaning: this light shines within clear glass.

Ubayy ibn Ka'b and others said: it is the likeness of the believer's heart. ﴿The glass is as if it were a star of brilliance﴾: some read it with a damma on the dal without a hamza, from durr (pearl), meaning: as if it were a star of pearl.

Others read "dirri'" and "durri'" with a kasra or damma on the dal and with a hamza, from al-dar' which is pushing away; this is because a star when it is hurled is brighter than in all other states, and the Arabs call stars that are not recognized "darari."

Ubayy ibn Ka'b said: a shining star. Qatadah said: shining, clear, large. ﴿Lit from a blessed tree﴾, meaning: it draws its fuel from the oil of a blessed olive tree, ﴿an olive tree﴾, in apposition or as explanatory addition, ﴿neither of the east nor of the west﴾, meaning: it is not on the eastern side of its plot, so the sun does not reach it from the beginning of the day, nor on its western side, so the shade withdraws from it before sunset; rather it is in a middle place, which the sun touches from the beginning of the day to its end, so its oil comes out balanced, pure and bright.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn Ammar related to us, saying: Abd al-Rahman ibn Abd Allah ibn Sa'd related to us, Amr ibn Abi Qays informed us, from Simak ibn Harb, from Ikrimah, from Ibn Abbas concerning His words ﴿an olive tree neither of the east nor of the west﴾: He said: it is a tree in the desert, not shaded by a mountain, nor a tree, nor a cave, and nothing conceals it, and that is the best for its oil.

Yahya ibn Sa'id al-Qattan said, from Imran ibn Hudayr, from Ikrimah, concerning His words ﴿neither of the east nor of the west﴾: He said: it is in a desert, and that is purest for its adornment.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: my father related to us, Abu Nu'aym related to us, Umar ibn Farrukh related to us, from Habib ibn al-Zubayr, from Ikrimah, who was asked by a man about ﴿an olive tree neither of the east nor of the west﴾; he said: That is an olive tree in a barren land; when the sun rises it shines upon it, and when it sets it sets upon it, and that is the purest oil there can be.

Mujahid said concerning His words ﴿an olive tree neither of the east nor of the west﴾: He said: it is not eastern, the sun does not strike it when it sets, nor western, the sun does not strike it when it rises; rather it is both eastern and western, the sun strikes it when it rises and when it sets.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said concerning His words ﴿an olive tree neither of the east nor of the west, whose oil would almost glow﴾: He said: It is the best oil. He said: When the sun rises it strikes it from the direction of the east, and when it begins to set the sun strikes it, so the sun strikes it in the morning and the evening, and such a tree is not counted as eastern or western.

Al-Suddi said concerning His words ﴿an olive tree neither of the east nor of the west﴾: He means: it is not eastern, such that the east claims it, nor western, such that the west claims it to the exclusion of the east; rather it is on the top of a mountain or in a desert, and the sun strikes it all day.

It has also been said that the meaning of His words ﴿an olive tree neither of the east nor of the west﴾ is that it is in the middle of the trees, and it is not exposed to the east or to the west.

Abu Ja'far al-Razi said, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, from Abu al-'Aliyah, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, concerning the saying of Allah the Exalted ﴿an olive tree neither of the east nor of the west﴾: He said: it is green and lush; the sun does not strike it in any condition, neither when it rises nor when it sets. He said: Likewise this believer has been protected from being struck by any of the trials, though he is tested by them, and Allah keeps him steadfast in them; he is between four qualities: if he speaks he is truthful, if he judges he is just, if he is tested he is patient, and if he is given he is thankful. Among other people he is like a living man walking among the graves of the dead.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ali ibn al-Husayn related to us, Musaddad related to us, saying: Abu Awanah related to us, from Abu Bishr, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr concerning His words ﴿an olive tree neither of the east nor of the west﴾: He said: it is in the middle of the trees; the sun does not strike it from east or west.

Atiyyah al-Awfi said: ﴿neither of the east nor of the west﴾: He said: it is a tree in a place among the trees, whose fruit's shadow is seen in its leaves, and this is among the trees that the sun neither rises upon nor sets upon.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn Ammar related to us, Abd al-Rahman al-Dashtaki related to us, Amr ibn Abi Qays related to us, from Ata', from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, concerning His words the Exalted ﴿neither of the east nor of the west﴾: It is not eastern, in that there is no west to it, nor western, in that there is no east to it; rather it is both eastern and western.

Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi said: ﴿neither of the east nor of the west﴾: He said: it is the qiblah.

Zayd ibn Aslam said: ﴿neither of the east nor of the west﴾: He said: it is Syria.

Al-Hasan al-Basri said: Had this tree been in the earth, it would have been either eastern or western; but it is a parable which Allah struck for His light.

Al-Dahhak said, from Ibn Abbas: ﴿lit from a blessed tree﴾: He said: a righteous man. ﴿an olive tree neither of the east nor of the west﴾: He said: neither Jewish nor Christian.

The most preferable of these views is the first, namely that it is on a level part of the earth, in a wide, open, exposed place, bright to the sun, which the sun touches from the beginning of the day to its end, so that its oil is purest and most refined for its adornment, as said by more than one of those who preceded; therefore He said: ﴿whose oil would almost glow even if no fire touched it﴾. Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: that is, by the radiance of the oil's brightness.

* *

As for His words ﴿light upon light﴾: Al-Awfi said, from Ibn Abbas: it means by that the faith of the servant and his deed.

Mujahid and al-Suddi said: it means the light of the fire and the light of the oil.

Ubayy ibn Ka'b said: ﴿light upon light﴾: he moves within five lights: his speech is light, his deed is light, his entrance is light, his exit is light, and his destination is toward light on the Day of Resurrection, toward Paradise.

Shimr ibn Atiyyah said: Ibn Abbas came to Ka'b al-Ahbar and said: "Tell me about the saying of Allah: ﴿whose oil would almost glow even if no fire touched it﴾." He said: Muhammad almost makes clear to the people, even if he does not speak, that he is a prophet, just as that oil almost glows.

Al-Suddi said concerning His words ﴿light upon light﴾: the light of the fire and the light of the oil; when they came together they shone, and neither shines without its companion; likewise the light of the Qur'an and the light of faith, when they come together, neither of them exists except with its companion.

* *

Part 2 of 2 is translated below, as requested.

His saying: ﴿Allah guides to His light whom He wills﴾ means: Allah directs to His guidance whoever He chooses. As came in the hadith narrated by the Imam Ahmad:

Mu'awiyah ibn 'Amr narrated to us: Ibrahim ibn Muhammad al-Fazari narrated to us: al-Awza'i narrated to us: Rabi'ah ibn Yazid narrated to me, from Abdullah [ibn] [[Addition from F, A, and al-Musnad.]] al-Daylami, from Abdullah ibn 'Amr, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Allah created His creation in darkness, then cast upon them of His light on that day. Whoever is struck by some of His light that day is guided, and whoever misses it goes astray. Therefore I say: the pen has dried over the knowledge of Allah, Mighty and Majestic." [[al-Musnad (2/176).]]

Another route from him: al-Bazzar said: Shihab ibn 'Uthman narrated to us: Ayyub [[In F, A: "al-Bazzar said: Shihab ibn 'Uthman narrated to us: Ayyub".]] ibn Suwayd narrated to us, from Yahya ibn Abi 'Amr al-Shaybani, from his father, from Abdullah ibn 'Umar, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Allah created His creation in darkness, then cast upon them a light from His light. Whoever is struck by that light is guided, and whoever misses it [[In F, A: "akhta'a" (missed).]] goes astray." [Al-Bazzar also narrated it from Abdullah ibn 'Amr by another route, with the same wording and letters.] [[Addition from F, A.]] [[Musnad al-Bazzar no. (2145), Kashf al-Astar; and Ahmad narrated it in his Musnad (2/197) by way of Muhammad ibn Muhajir, from Urwah ibn Ruwaym, from Ibn al-Daylami, from Abdullah ibn 'Amr, with the same.]].

* *

His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿And Allah sets forth parables for the people, and Allah is Knowing of all things﴾. When He mentioned this as a parable of the light of His guidance in the heart of the believer, He concluded the verse with His saying: ﴿And Allah sets forth parables for the people, and Allah is Knowing of all things﴾, meaning: He is most knowing of who deserves guidance and who deserves being led astray.

Imam Ahmad said: Abu al-Nadr narrated to us: Abu Mu'awiyah narrated to us, namely Shayban, from Layth, from 'Amr ibn Murrah, from Abu al-Bakhtari, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The hearts are four: a bare heart in which there is like a lamp that shines; a wrapped heart bound over its covering; an inverted heart; and a sheathed heart. As for the bare heart, it is the heart of the believer, whose lamp is his light within it. As for the wrapped heart, it is the heart of the disbeliever. As for the inverted heart, it is the heart of the hypocrite, who knows then denies. As for the sheathed heart, it is a heart in which there is both faith and hypocrisy; the likeness of faith in it is that of a plant which good water nourishes, and the likeness of hypocrisy in it is that of a sore which pus and blood feed. Whichever of the two increases overcomes the other, and it is overcome by it." Its chain is good [[al-Musnad (3/17).]], but they did not record it.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 24, verses 36–38 (part 1 of 3):

When Allah, the Exalted, struck the [parable [[addition from manuscripts F and A]]] of the believer's heart, and what it contains of guidance and knowledge, by the lamp in the clear glass, which is kindled with good oil, and that is like a lamp-stand, He mentioned its place, which is the mosques, which are the most beloved places on earth to Allah, the Exalted. They are His houses in which He is worshipped and in which He is made One. So He said: ﴿in houses which Allah has permitted to be raised﴾. That is, Allah, the Exalted, commanded that they be raised, meaning that they be purified from filth, idle talk, and deeds and words that are not fitting in them. As 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah reported from Ibn 'Abbas concerning this noble verse, ﴿in houses which Allah has permitted to be raised﴾, he said: Allah, glorified is He, forbade idle talk in them. Likewise said 'Ikrimah, Abu Salih, al-Dahhak, Nafi' ibn Jubayr, Abu Bakr ibn Sulayman ibn Abi Hathmah [in F and A: "Khaythamah"], Sufyan ibn Husayn, and others among the scholars of tafsir [in F and A: "tafsir"].

Qatadah said: They are these mosques. Allah, glorified is He, commanded that they be built and raised, and commanded that they be maintained and purified. It has been mentioned to us that Ka'b [al-Ahbar] used to say: "Indeed, it is written in the Tawrah (Torah): 'Verily, My houses on earth are the mosques, and whoever performs ablution and does it well, then visits Me in My house, I will honour him, and it is due upon the one visited to honour the visitor.'" Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it in his Tafsir.

Many hadiths have come concerning the building of mosques, respecting and venerating them, and perfuming and fumigating them. This has a separate place where it is mentioned, and I have written a separate booklet on that, and to Allah belongs all praise and grace. With the help of Allah, the Exalted, we will mention here a portion of that, if Allah wills, and in Him is trust and upon Him is reliance:

From the Commander of the Faithful, 'Uthman ibn 'Affan, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Whoever builds a mosque seeking thereby the Face of Allah, Allah will build for him a like of it in Paradise." It is recorded by both [al-Bukhari and Muslim] in their Sahihs. [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (450) and Sahih Muslim no. (533).]

Ibn Majah narrated from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever builds a mosque in which the name of Allah is mentioned, Allah will build for him a house in Paradise." [Sunan Ibn Majah no. (735), through al-Walid ibn Abi al-Walid from 'Uthman ibn 'Abdullah from 'Umar. Al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id (1/260): "This isnad is mursal; 'Uthman ibn 'Abdullah ibn Suraqah narrated from 'Umar, and he is his maternal grandfather, but he did not hear from him, as stated by al-Mizzi."]

And for al-Nasa'i, from 'Amr ibn 'Abasah, the like of it. [In A: "'Anbasah".] [Sunan al-Nasa'i (2/31).] The hadiths on this are very numerous.

From 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) commanded that mosques be built in the neighbourhoods, and that they be cleaned and perfumed. [al-Musnad (6/279), Sunan Abi Dawud no. (455), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (594), and Sunan Ibn Majah no. (759).] It was narrated by Ahmad and the authors of the Sunan except al-Nasa'i. And for Ahmad and Abu Dawud, from Samurah ibn Jundub, a similar report. [al-Musnad (5/17) and Sunan Abi Dawud no. (456).]

Al-Bukhari said: 'Umar said: "Build for the people a shelter that protects them, and beware of reddening or yellowing [the mosque], lest you tempt the people." [Sahih al-Bukhari (1/539), Fath.]

Ibn Majah narrated from him (i.e., 'Umar) who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The deeds of no people have ever been evil except that they adorned their mosques." [Sunan Ibn Majah no. (741), through Jabbarah ibn al-Mughallas from 'Abd al-Karim ibn 'Abd al-Rahman from 'Amr ibn Maymun from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, with the same. Al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id (1/262): "In this isnad is Jabbarah ibn al-Mughallas, who has been accused (of lying)."] In its isnad there is weakness.

Abu Dawud narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I have not been commanded to decorate the mosques." Ibn 'Abbas said: "You will surely adorn them as the Jews and Christians adorned them." [Sunan Abi Dawud no. (448).]

From Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The Hour will not come until the people boast about mosques." It was narrated by Imam Ahmad and the authors of the Sunan except al-Tirmidhi. [al-Musnad (3/134), Sunan Abi Dawud no. (449), Sunan al-Nasa'i (2/32), and Sunan Ibn Majah no. (739).]

From Buraydah, that a man recited poetry in the mosque, and he said: "Who calls to the red camel?" The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "May you not find it! The mosques were only built for what they were built for." Narrated by Muslim. [Sahih Muslim no. (569).]

From 'Amr ibn Shu'ayb, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) forbade buying and selling in the mosques, and reciting poetry in them. Narrated by Ahmad and the authors of the Sunan. [al-Musnad (2/179), Sunan Abi Dawud no. (1079), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (322), Sunan al-Nasa'i (2/47), and Sunan Ibn Majah no. (749).] Al-Tirmidhi said: Hasan.

From Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When you see someone buying or selling in the mosque, say: 'May Allah not make your trade profitable.' And when you see someone searching for a lost item in the mosque, say: 'May Allah not return it to you.'" Narrated by al-Tirmidhi, who said: Hasan gharib. [Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3121).]

Ibn Majah and others narrated, from the hadith of Ibn 'Umar, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "There are matters that are not befitting in the mosque: it should not be used as a path, weapons should not be displayed in it, a bow should not be strung in it, arrows should not be scattered in it, raw meat should not be carried through it, a prescribed punishment should not be carried out in it, retaliation should not be exacted in it, and it should not be made a marketplace." [Sunan Ibn Majah no. (748). Al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id (1/264): "In this isnad is Zayd ibn Jubayrah. Ibn 'Abd al-Barr said: They are agreed that he is weak."]

From Wathilah ibn al-Asqa', from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "Keep your children and your insane away from the mosques, and your buying and selling, and your disputes, and the raising of your voices, and the carrying out of your prescribed punishments, and the drawing of your swords, and make for their doors places of purification, and perfume them on Fridays." [In A and F: "its isnad".]

Ibn Majah also narrated it, and in its isnad there is weakness. [Sunan Ibn Majah no. (750). Al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id (1/265): "This isnad is weak; Abu Sa'id is Muhammad ibn Sa'id al-Masallub. Ahmad said: he used to deliberately fabricate hadith. Then he said: al-Harith ibn Nabhan is weak."]

As for "it should not be made a path," some scholars disliked passing through it except out of need when one finds an alternative to it. In a report: "Indeed the angels marvel at a man who passes by the mosque and does not pray in it."

As for "weapons should not be displayed in it, a bow should not be strung in it, and arrows should not be scattered in it," this is due to fear that some people may be hit by them, because of the large number of worshippers in it. For this reason, when someone passed by with arrows, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) commanded him to hold their points, so as not to harm anyone, as is established in the Sahih. [Narrated by Muslim in his Sahih no. (2615) from the hadith of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari.]

As for the prohibition of passing through it with raw meat, it is due to fear of blood dripping from it, just as a menstruating woman is forbidden from passing through it if she fears staining it.

As for "a prescribed punishment should not be carried out in it, nor retaliation," it is due to fear of impurity arising in it from the one being punished or the one whose limb is cut off.

As for "it should not be made a marketplace," it is due to what preceded of the prohibition of buying and selling in it, for it was only built for the remembrance of Allah and for prayer, as the Prophet (ﷺ), upon whom be prayers and peace, said to that Bedouin who urinated in a corner of the mosque: "Indeed the mosques were not built for this; they were only built for the remembrance of Allah and for prayer in them." Then he commanded a bucket of water, which was poured over his urine. [Narrated by Muslim in his Sahih no. (284) from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him.]

In the second hadith: "Keep your children away from your mosques," this is because they play in them and it is not suitable for them. 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, when he saw children playing in the mosque, would strike them with the mikhfaqah, which is the whip (durrah). He used to inspect (yafattish) the mosque after 'Isha', and would not leave anyone in it.

"And your insane": meaning, because of the weakness of their minds, and people mocking them, which leads to playing in it, and due to fear of their soiling the mosque, and similar things.

"And your buying and your selling": as previously mentioned.

"And your disputes": meaning, litigation and judging in it. For this reason many scholars stated that a judge should not set himself up to settle cases in the mosque, but should be in another place, because of the abundance of arguments, quarrels, and loud clamour that is not suitable for it. For this reason he (ﷺ) said after it: "and the raising of your voices."

Al-Bukhari said: Ali ibn 'Abd Allah narrated to us, Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, al-Ju'ayd ibn 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, who said: Yazid ibn Khusayfah narrated to me, from al-Sa'ib ibn Yazid al-Kindi, who said: I was standing in the mosque when a man threw pebbles at me, so I looked and saw that it was 'Umar ibn al-Khattab. He said: "Go and bring me these two." I brought them to him, and he said: "Who are you two?" or "Where are you from?" They said: "From the people of al-Ta'if." He said: "If you were from the people of this town, I would have punished you both. You raise your voices in the mosque of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)!" [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (470).]

Al-Nasa'i said: Suwayd ibn Nasr narrated to us, from Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak, from Shu'bah, from Sa'd ibn Ibrahim, from his father Ibrahim ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf, who said: 'Umar heard the voice of a man in the mosque and said: "Do you know where you are?" And this is also authentic. [Al-Mizzi mentioned it in Tuhfat al-Ashraf (8/4) and attributed it to al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra, in al-Mawa'iz.]

* *

As for his saying: "and the raising of your voices," and "the drawing of your swords," these have preceded.

* *

As for his saying: "and make for their doors places of purification," meaning the latrines, which are used for ablution and relieving oneself. Near the mosque of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) there were wells from which they drew water, and they would drink from them, purify themselves, perform ablution, and other things.

* *

As for his saying: "and perfume them on Fridays," meaning: fumigate them on the days of Friday, because of the large gathering of people on that day.

Al-Hafiz Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili said: 'Ubayd Allah narrated to us, 'Abd al-Rahman [in A: "'Abdullah"] ibn Mahdi narrated to us, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, that 'Umar used to perfume the mosque of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) every Friday. Its isnad is hasan, there is no harm in it. [Musnad Abi Ya'la (1/170).] And Allah knows best.

It is established in the two Sahihs from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he said: "A man's prayer in congregation is multiplied twenty-five times over his prayer in his house or in his market. That is because when he performs ablution and does it well [in F and A: "the ablution"], then goes out to the mosque, with nothing bringing him out but prayer, he does not take a step except that a degree is raised for him thereby and a sin is removed from him thereby. When he prays, the angels will not cease to send blessings upon him as long as he remains in his place of prayer, saying: 'O Allah, bless him; O Allah, have mercy upon him.' And he remains in prayer as long as he is waiting for the prayer." [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (647) and Sahih Muslim no. (649), from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him.]

Al-Daraqutni also transmits it as a marfu' (traced back to the Prophet ﷺ) report: "There is no prayer for the neighbour of the mosque except in the mosque." [[Sunan al-Daraqutni (1/420), through the chain of Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Yamami, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, as a marfu' report, with the same wording. It was also transmitted by al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak (1/246) and al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan al-Kubra (3/57), through Sulayman ibn Dawud, with the same wording. Sulayman ibn Dawud is agreed upon as weak. From the hadith of Jabir: al-Daraqutni also transmitted it in his Sunan (1/420), through Muhammad ibn Miskin, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Muhammad ibn Suqah, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Jabir, as a marfu' report, with the same wording. Abu al-Tayyib said in his commentary: "It contains Muhammad ibn Miskin. Al-Dhahabi said: he is not known, and his report is munkar (rejected). Al-Bukhari said: there is a problem (nazar) in the chain of his hadith."]].

In the Sunan (collections) it is also reported: "Give glad tidings to those who walk to the mosques in the darkness with complete light on the Day of Resurrection." [[Abu Dawud in his Sunan, no. (561), and al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan, no. (223), from the hadith of Buraydah ibn al-Husayb, may Allah be pleased with him. Al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a gharib (singular) hadith from this route, marfu'. It is sahih as a musnad (with a continuous chain) and as a mawquf (ending with the Companions) report, and it is not traced back (musnad) to the Prophet ﷺ."]].

It is recommended for one who enters the mosque to begin with his right foot, and to say what is established in Sahih al-Bukhari (Sahih al-Bukhari, the collection of al-Bukhari) from Abdullah ibn Amr [[In A: "Umar."]], may Allah be pleased with him [[In F and A: "with both of them."]], that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to say when he entered the mosque: "I seek refuge in Allah the Mighty, and in His Noble Face, and in His Ancient Authority, from the accursed Shaytan." [He said: "Ever?" He said: "Yes."] [[Addition from A.]] He said: "When he says that, Shaytan says: 'He has been protected from me for the rest of the day.'" [[I have not found it in Sahih al-Bukhari. Al-Mizzi mentioned it in Tuhfat al-Ashraf and Ibn al-Athir in Jami' al-Usul, and they attributed it only to Abu Dawud in his Sunan, no. (466).]]

Muslim transmitted with his chain, from Abu Humayd, or Abu Usayd, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "When one of you enters the mosque, let him say: 'O Allah, open for me the doors of Your mercy.' And when he leaves, let him say: 'O Allah, I ask You of Your bounty.'"

Al-Nasa'i transmitted it from both of them, from the Prophet ﷺ, the like of it. [[Sahih Muslim no. (713) and Sunan al-Nasa'i (2/53).]]

From Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "When one of you enters the mosque, let him greet the Prophet ﷺ and say: 'O Allah, open for me the doors of Your mercy.' And when he leaves, let him greet the Prophet ﷺ and say: 'O Allah, protect me from the accursed Shaytan.'"

Ibn Majah, Ibn Khuzaymah and Ibn Hibban transmitted it in their Sahihs. [[Sunan Ibn Majah no. (773), Sahih Ibn Khuzaymah no. (452), and Sahih Ibn Hibban no. (2048), al-Ihsan, all through Abu Bakr al-Hanafi, from al-Dahhak ibn Uthman, from al-Maqburi, from Abu Hurayrah, with the same wording. Al-Busayri said in al-Zawa'id (1/97): "This chain is sahih and its narrators are trustworthy."]]

Imam Ahmad said: Ismail ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Layth ibn Abi Sulaym narrated to us, from Abdullah ibn Hasan [[In A: "Husayn."]], from his mother Fatimah bint Husayn, from her grandmother Fatimah bint the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered the mosque, he would send blessings upon Muhammad and greet him with peace, then say: "O Allah, forgive me my sins, and open for me the doors of Your mercy." And when he left, he would send blessings upon Muhammad and greet him with peace, then say: "O Allah, forgive me my sins, and open for me the doors of Your bounty."

It was also transmitted by al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah. [[Al-Musnad (6/282), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (314), and Sunan Ibn Majah no. (771).]] Al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a hasan hadith, but its chain is not continuous (muttasil), because Fatimah bint al-Husayn al-Sughra did not meet Fatimah al-Kubra."

All of this which we have mentioned, along with what we have left out of the hadiths reported on this subject for the sake of brevity, is all included in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿in houses which Allah has permitted to be raised﴾.

* *

His saying: ﴿and His name is mentioned therein﴾, meaning: the name of Allah, as in His saying: ﴿O Children of Adam, take your adornment at every mosque﴾ [al-A'raf: 31], and His saying ﴿and set your faces upright at every mosque, and call upon Him, being sincere to Him in religion﴾ [al-A'raf: 29], and His saying ﴿And the mosques are for Allah, so do not invoke anyone with Allah﴾ [al-Jinn: 18].

Ibn Abbas said: ﴿and His name is mentioned therein﴾ means: His Book is recited therein.

* *

His saying: ﴿He is glorified therein in the mornings and the evenings﴾, meaning: in the early mornings and the late afternoons. Al-Asal is the plural of asil, which is the end of the day.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said, from Ibn Abbas: Every tasbih (glorification) in the Qur'an is salat (prayer).

Ali ibn Abi Talhah said, from Ibn Abbas: By al-ghuduww (the mornings) he means the Dawn Prayer (salat al-ghadah), and by al-asal he means the Afternoon Prayer (salat al-'asr). These are the first prayers which Allah made obligatory, so He wished to mention them and to remind His servants of them.

Al-Hasan and al-Dahhak said likewise: ﴿He is glorified therein in the mornings and the evenings﴾ means: the prayer.

As for the one of the reciters (qurra', the transmitters of the recognized readings) who read "yusabbihu lahu fiha bil-ghuduwwi wal-asal" with a fatha on the ba' of "yusabbu" [meaning it is in the passive voice, the subject not named], he stops at His saying ﴿wal-asal﴾ with a complete pause, and begins with His saying ﴿men (rijal) whom neither trade nor sale distracts from the remembrance of Allah﴾, and it is as if it explains the omitted subject, as the poet said:

"Let Yazid weep, one who is weak in disputes,
and one bewildered by what the calamities cast down..."

As if it were said: Who weeps for him? He said: This one weeps for him. And as if it were said: Who is glorified for Him therein? He said: Men.

But according to the reading of the one who reads "yusabbihu" with a kasra on the ba' [meaning it is active], making it a verb with ﴿rijal﴾ as its subject, then stopping is only good at the subject, since it completes the sentence.

His saying ﴿rijal (men)﴾ indicates their lofty aspirations, their high resolve and their elevated determination, through which they became the builders of the mosques, which are the houses of Allah on His earth, and the places of His worship, His thanks, His Oneness and His glorification, as He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿Among the believers are men who have been true to what they covenanted with Allah﴾ [al-Ahzab: 23].

As for women, their prayer in their houses is better for them, because of what Abu Dawud transmitted from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "The prayer of a woman in her house is better than her prayer in her chamber (hujrah), and her prayer in her inner room (makhda') is better than her prayer in her house." [[Sunan Abi Dawud no. (580).]]

Imam Ahmad said: Yahya ibn Ghaylan narrated to us, Rishdin narrated to us, Amr narrated to me, from Abu al-Samh, from al-Sa'ib, the freedman of Umm Salamah, from Umm Salamah, may Allah be pleased with her, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that he said: "The best of the mosques of women is the innermost part of their houses." [[Al-Musnad (6/297).]]

Imam Ahmad also said: Harun narrated to us, Abdullah ibn Wahb informed me, Dawud ibn Qays narrated to us, from Abdullah ibn Suwayd al-Ansari, from his paternal aunt Umm Humayd, the wife of Abu Humayd al-Sa'idi, that she came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I love to pray with you." He said: "I know that you love to pray with me, but your prayer in your house is better than your prayer in your chamber, and your prayer in your chamber is better than your prayer in your courtyard, and your prayer in your courtyard is better than your prayer in the mosque of your people, and your prayer in the mosque of your people is better than your prayer in my mosque." She said: So she ordered that a mosque be built for her in the furthest and darkest part of her house, and she used to pray in it until she met Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. [[Al-Musnad (6/371). They did not transmit it.]]

This is so. It is permissible for her, however, to attend the congregation of men, on condition that she does not harm any man by displaying adornment or wearing perfume, as is established in the two Sahihs (al-Bukhari and Muslim) from Abdullah ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Do not prevent the female servants of Allah from the mosques of Allah." [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (900) and Sahih Muslim no. (442).]]

Al-Bukhari and Muslim transmitted it, and Ahmad and Abu Dawud have: "And their houses are better for them." [[Al-Musnad (2/76) and Sunan Abi Dawud no. (567), from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both.]] And in another narration: "And let them go out while they are unscented (tafilat)," meaning: they have no fragrance.

It is established in Sahih Muslim, from Zaynab, the wife of Ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to us: "When one of you women attends the mosque, let her not touch perfume." [[Sahih Muslim no. (443).]]

And in the two Sahihs from Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, that she said: The women of the believers used to attend the Dawn Prayer with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, then they would return wrapped in their mantles (murut), so that they could not be recognized because of the darkness (ghalas). [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (578) and Sahih Muslim no. (645).]]

And in the two Sahihs also, from her, that she said: If the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had seen what the women have newly introduced, he would have prevented them from the mosques, just as the women of the Children of Israel were prevented. [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (869) and Sahih Muslim no. (445).]]

* *

His saying: ﴿men whom neither trade nor sale distracts from the remembrance of Allah﴾, like His saying: ﴿O you who believe, let not your wealth or your children distract you from the remembrance of Allah. And whoever does that, those are the losers﴾ [al-Munafiqun: 9], and He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿O you who believe, when the call is made for prayer on the day of Jumu'ah, hasten to the remembrance of Allah and leave off trade. That is better for you, if you only knew﴾ [al-Jumu'ah: 9].

He, may He be exalted, says: The world, its adornment, its finery and the pleasures of its trade and its profits do not distract them from the remembrance of their Lord, who is their Creator and their Provider. And those who know that what is with Him is better for them and more beneficial than what is in their hands, because what they have will perish and what is with Allah remains. For this reason He said: ﴿Trade and sale do not distract them from the remembrance of Allah, and the establishment of prayer, and the giving of zakah﴾, meaning: they give precedence to His obedience, His will and His love over their own will and love.

Hushaym said, from Sayyar: I was told, from Ibn Mas'ud, that he saw some people of the market, when the call to prayer was made, leaving their trading and rising to prayer, and Abdullah said: These are among those whom Allah mentioned in His Book: ﴿men whom neither trade nor sale distracts from the remembrance of Allah﴾. [[Narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (18/113).]]

Likewise Amr ibn Dinar al-Qahramani narrated, from Salim, from Abdullah ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, that he was in the market when the prayer was established, so they closed their shops and entered the mosque. Ibn Umar said: It was concerning them that this was revealed: ﴿men whom neither trade nor sale distracts from the remembrance of Allah﴾. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Jarir. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (18/113).]]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Bakr al-San'ani narrated to us, Abu Sa'id, client of the Banu Hashim, narrated to us, Abdullah ibn Bujayr narrated to us, Abu Abd Rabb narrated to us, who said: Abu al-Darda', may Allah be pleased with him, said: I used to stand on these steps and trade on them, making three hundred dinars every day, and I attend the prayer in the mosque every day. Indeed, I do not say that this is not lawful, but I love to be among those about whom Allah said: ﴿men whom neither trade nor sale distracts from the remembrance of Allah﴾.

Amr ibn Dinar al-A'war said: I was with Salim ibn Abdullah, and we were heading to the mosque. We passed by the market of Madinah, where the people had stood up for prayer and covered their goods. Salim looked at their goods, with no one near them, and then recited this verse: ﴿Men whom neither trade nor sale distracts from the remembrance of Allah﴾. Then he said: "They are these people."

Sa'id ibn Abi al-Hasan and al-Dahhak said likewise: "Trade and sale do not distract them from coming to the prayer at its time."

Mutar al-Warraq said: "They used to buy and sell, but whenever one of them heard the call to prayer while the scales were in his hand, he lowered them and went to the prayer."

Ali ibn Abi Talhah reported from Ibn Abbas regarding ﴿neither trade nor sale distracts them from the remembrance of Allah﴾: "It means the obligatory prayer (al-salat al-maktubah)." Al-Rabi' ibn Anas and Muqatil ibn Hayyan said the same.

Al-Suddi said: "It means the prayer in congregation."

Also from Muqatil ibn Hayyan: "Such things do not distract them from attending the prayer, and from establishing it as Allah commanded them, and from observing its appointed times and what Allah entrusted them to guard in it."

* *

His saying: ﴿They fear a Day in which hearts and eyes will be turned about﴾ means the Day of Resurrection, the day in which hearts and eyes will be turned about, that is, from the severity of terror and the magnitude of its horrors. As Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And warn them of the Approaching Day, when hearts will rise up to the throats, choked with grief﴾ [Ghafir: 18]. And Allah the Exalted said: ﴿He only delays them until a Day when eyes will stare fixedly﴾ [Ibrahim: 42]. And Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And they give food, despite their love for it, to the needy, the orphan, and the captive, saying: "We feed you only for the sake of Allah. We desire no reward from you, nor thanks. Indeed, we fear from our Lord a Day austere and distressing." So Allah will protect them from the evil of that Day and will give them radiance and happiness, and will reward them for their patience with a garden and silk﴾ [Al-Insan: 8–12].

Here Allah says: ﴿that Allah may reward them for the best of what they did﴾, meaning: these are among those whose best deeds are accepted from them, and whose evil deeds He overlooks.

* *

His saying: ﴿and increase them from His bounty﴾ means He accepts the good from them and multiplies it for them, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not wrong even the weight of an atom; and if it is a good deed, He doubles it and gives from Himself a great reward﴾ [An-Nisa: 40]. And Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Whoever comes with a good deed will have ten times its like﴾ [Al-An'am: 160]. And He said: ﴿Who is it that would lend to Allah a goodly loan so that He may multiply it for him many times over?﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 245]. And He said: ﴿And Allah multiplies for whom He wills﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 261], just as He said here: ﴿And Allah provides for whom He wills without account﴾.

It is reported from Ibn Mas'ud that milk was brought to him, and he offered it to his companions one by one, and none of them drank it because they were fasting. Ibn Mas'ud, who was not fasting, took it and drank it. Then he recited the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿They fear a Day in which hearts and eyes will be turned about﴾. Related by al-Nasa'i and Ibn Abi Hatim, from the hadith of al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, from Alqamah, from him [[Mentioned by al-Mizzi in Tuhfat al-Ashraf under no. (9435), and attributed it to al-Nasa'i in al-Mawa'iz.]].

Ibn Abi Hatim also said: My father related to us, Suwayd ibn Sa'id related to us, Ali ibn Mushir related to us, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Asma' bint Yazid, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "When Allah gathers the first and the last on the Day of Resurrection, a caller will come and call out with a voice that the creatures will hear: 'Let the people of the gathering know who is most worthy of honour. Let those stand up whom neither trade nor sale distracts from the remembrance of Allah.' They will stand up, and they will be few. Then all the rest of creation will be called to account." [[Also related by Hannad in al-Zuhd under no. (176), through Abu Mu'awiyah, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq, with the same chain. Abd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq is weak.]]

Al-Tabarani related, from the hadith of Baqiyyah, from Isma'il ibn Abd Allah al-Kindi, from al-A'mash, from Abu Wa'il, from Ibn Mas'ud, from the Prophet ﷺ regarding His saying: ﴿that He may pay them their wages and increase them from His bounty﴾ [Fatir: 30]: "﴿Their wages﴾ means He will admit them into Paradise, ﴿and increase them from His bounty﴾ means intercession for whoever is owed intercession, for those who did good to them in the world." [[Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir of al-Tabarani (10/248). The hafiz Ibn Kathir said when commenting on verse 173 of Surat al-Nisa': "This chain does not hold up; but when it is reported from Ibn Mas'ud as a mawquf (companion's saying), it is good."]]

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 24, verses 36–38 (part 1 of 3):

When Allah, the Exalted, struck the [parable [[addition from manuscripts F and A]]] of the believer's heart, and what it contains of guidance and knowledge, by the lamp in the clear glass, which is kindled with good oil, and that is like a lamp-stand, He mentioned its place, which is the mosques, which are the most beloved places on earth to Allah, the Exalted. They are His houses in which He is worshipped and in which He is made One. So He said: ﴿in houses which Allah has permitted to be raised﴾. That is, Allah, the Exalted, commanded that they be raised, meaning that they be purified from filth, idle talk, and deeds and words that are not fitting in them. As 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah reported from Ibn 'Abbas concerning this noble verse, ﴿in houses which Allah has permitted to be raised﴾, he said: Allah, glorified is He, forbade idle talk in them. Likewise said 'Ikrimah, Abu Salih, al-Dahhak, Nafi' ibn Jubayr, Abu Bakr ibn Sulayman ibn Abi Hathmah [in F and A: "Khaythamah"], Sufyan ibn Husayn, and others among the scholars of tafsir [in F and A: "tafsir"].

Qatadah said: They are these mosques. Allah, glorified is He, commanded that they be built and raised, and commanded that they be maintained and purified. It has been mentioned to us that Ka'b [al-Ahbar] used to say: "Indeed, it is written in the Tawrah (Torah): 'Verily, My houses on earth are the mosques, and whoever performs ablution and does it well, then visits Me in My house, I will honour him, and it is due upon the one visited to honour the visitor.'" Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it in his Tafsir.

Many hadiths have come concerning the building of mosques, respecting and venerating them, and perfuming and fumigating them. This has a separate place where it is mentioned, and I have written a separate booklet on that, and to Allah belongs all praise and grace. With the help of Allah, the Exalted, we will mention here a portion of that, if Allah wills, and in Him is trust and upon Him is reliance:

From the Commander of the Faithful, 'Uthman ibn 'Affan, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Whoever builds a mosque seeking thereby the Face of Allah, Allah will build for him a like of it in Paradise." It is recorded by both [al-Bukhari and Muslim] in their Sahihs. [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (450) and Sahih Muslim no. (533).]

Ibn Majah narrated from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever builds a mosque in which the name of Allah is mentioned, Allah will build for him a house in Paradise." [Sunan Ibn Majah no. (735), through al-Walid ibn Abi al-Walid from 'Uthman ibn 'Abdullah from 'Umar. Al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id (1/260): "This isnad is mursal; 'Uthman ibn 'Abdullah ibn Suraqah narrated from 'Umar, and he is his maternal grandfather, but he did not hear from him, as stated by al-Mizzi."]

And for al-Nasa'i, from 'Amr ibn 'Abasah, the like of it. [In A: "'Anbasah".] [Sunan al-Nasa'i (2/31).] The hadiths on this are very numerous.

From 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) commanded that mosques be built in the neighbourhoods, and that they be cleaned and perfumed. [al-Musnad (6/279), Sunan Abi Dawud no. (455), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (594), and Sunan Ibn Majah no. (759).] It was narrated by Ahmad and the authors of the Sunan except al-Nasa'i. And for Ahmad and Abu Dawud, from Samurah ibn Jundub, a similar report. [al-Musnad (5/17) and Sunan Abi Dawud no. (456).]

Al-Bukhari said: 'Umar said: "Build for the people a shelter that protects them, and beware of reddening or yellowing [the mosque], lest you tempt the people." [Sahih al-Bukhari (1/539), Fath.]

Ibn Majah narrated from him (i.e., 'Umar) who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The deeds of no people have ever been evil except that they adorned their mosques." [Sunan Ibn Majah no. (741), through Jabbarah ibn al-Mughallas from 'Abd al-Karim ibn 'Abd al-Rahman from 'Amr ibn Maymun from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, with the same. Al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id (1/262): "In this isnad is Jabbarah ibn al-Mughallas, who has been accused (of lying)."] In its isnad there is weakness.

Abu Dawud narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I have not been commanded to decorate the mosques." Ibn 'Abbas said: "You will surely adorn them as the Jews and Christians adorned them." [Sunan Abi Dawud no. (448).]

From Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The Hour will not come until the people boast about mosques." It was narrated by Imam Ahmad and the authors of the Sunan except al-Tirmidhi. [al-Musnad (3/134), Sunan Abi Dawud no. (449), Sunan al-Nasa'i (2/32), and Sunan Ibn Majah no. (739).]

From Buraydah, that a man recited poetry in the mosque, and he said: "Who calls to the red camel?" The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "May you not find it! The mosques were only built for what they were built for." Narrated by Muslim. [Sahih Muslim no. (569).]

From 'Amr ibn Shu'ayb, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) forbade buying and selling in the mosques, and reciting poetry in them. Narrated by Ahmad and the authors of the Sunan. [al-Musnad (2/179), Sunan Abi Dawud no. (1079), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (322), Sunan al-Nasa'i (2/47), and Sunan Ibn Majah no. (749).] Al-Tirmidhi said: Hasan.

From Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When you see someone buying or selling in the mosque, say: 'May Allah not make your trade profitable.' And when you see someone searching for a lost item in the mosque, say: 'May Allah not return it to you.'" Narrated by al-Tirmidhi, who said: Hasan gharib. [Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3121).]

Ibn Majah and others narrated, from the hadith of Ibn 'Umar, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "There are matters that are not befitting in the mosque: it should not be used as a path, weapons should not be displayed in it, a bow should not be strung in it, arrows should not be scattered in it, raw meat should not be carried through it, a prescribed punishment should not be carried out in it, retaliation should not be exacted in it, and it should not be made a marketplace." [Sunan Ibn Majah no. (748). Al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id (1/264): "In this isnad is Zayd ibn Jubayrah. Ibn 'Abd al-Barr said: They are agreed that he is weak."]

From Wathilah ibn al-Asqa', from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "Keep your children and your insane away from the mosques, and your buying and selling, and your disputes, and the raising of your voices, and the carrying out of your prescribed punishments, and the drawing of your swords, and make for their doors places of purification, and perfume them on Fridays." [In A and F: "its isnad".]

Ibn Majah also narrated it, and in its isnad there is weakness. [Sunan Ibn Majah no. (750). Al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id (1/265): "This isnad is weak; Abu Sa'id is Muhammad ibn Sa'id al-Masallub. Ahmad said: he used to deliberately fabricate hadith. Then he said: al-Harith ibn Nabhan is weak."]

As for "it should not be made a path," some scholars disliked passing through it except out of need when one finds an alternative to it. In a report: "Indeed the angels marvel at a man who passes by the mosque and does not pray in it."

As for "weapons should not be displayed in it, a bow should not be strung in it, and arrows should not be scattered in it," this is due to fear that some people may be hit by them, because of the large number of worshippers in it. For this reason, when someone passed by with arrows, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) commanded him to hold their points, so as not to harm anyone, as is established in the Sahih. [Narrated by Muslim in his Sahih no. (2615) from the hadith of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari.]

As for the prohibition of passing through it with raw meat, it is due to fear of blood dripping from it, just as a menstruating woman is forbidden from passing through it if she fears staining it.

As for "a prescribed punishment should not be carried out in it, nor retaliation," it is due to fear of impurity arising in it from the one being punished or the one whose limb is cut off.

As for "it should not be made a marketplace," it is due to what preceded of the prohibition of buying and selling in it, for it was only built for the remembrance of Allah and for prayer, as the Prophet (ﷺ), upon whom be prayers and peace, said to that Bedouin who urinated in a corner of the mosque: "Indeed the mosques were not built for this; they were only built for the remembrance of Allah and for prayer in them." Then he commanded a bucket of water, which was poured over his urine. [Narrated by Muslim in his Sahih no. (284) from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him.]

In the second hadith: "Keep your children away from your mosques," this is because they play in them and it is not suitable for them. 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, when he saw children playing in the mosque, would strike them with the mikhfaqah, which is the whip (durrah). He used to inspect (yafattish) the mosque after 'Isha', and would not leave anyone in it.

"And your insane": meaning, because of the weakness of their minds, and people mocking them, which leads to playing in it, and due to fear of their soiling the mosque, and similar things.

"And your buying and your selling": as previously mentioned.

"And your disputes": meaning, litigation and judging in it. For this reason many scholars stated that a judge should not set himself up to settle cases in the mosque, but should be in another place, because of the abundance of arguments, quarrels, and loud clamour that is not suitable for it. For this reason he (ﷺ) said after it: "and the raising of your voices."

Al-Bukhari said: Ali ibn 'Abd Allah narrated to us, Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, al-Ju'ayd ibn 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, who said: Yazid ibn Khusayfah narrated to me, from al-Sa'ib ibn Yazid al-Kindi, who said: I was standing in the mosque when a man threw pebbles at me, so I looked and saw that it was 'Umar ibn al-Khattab. He said: "Go and bring me these two." I brought them to him, and he said: "Who are you two?" or "Where are you from?" They said: "From the people of al-Ta'if." He said: "If you were from the people of this town, I would have punished you both. You raise your voices in the mosque of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)!" [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (470).]

Al-Nasa'i said: Suwayd ibn Nasr narrated to us, from Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak, from Shu'bah, from Sa'd ibn Ibrahim, from his father Ibrahim ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf, who said: 'Umar heard the voice of a man in the mosque and said: "Do you know where you are?" And this is also authentic. [Al-Mizzi mentioned it in Tuhfat al-Ashraf (8/4) and attributed it to al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra, in al-Mawa'iz.]

* *

As for his saying: "and the raising of your voices," and "the drawing of your swords," these have preceded.

* *

As for his saying: "and make for their doors places of purification," meaning the latrines, which are used for ablution and relieving oneself. Near the mosque of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) there were wells from which they drew water, and they would drink from them, purify themselves, perform ablution, and other things.

* *

As for his saying: "and perfume them on Fridays," meaning: fumigate them on the days of Friday, because of the large gathering of people on that day.

Al-Hafiz Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili said: 'Ubayd Allah narrated to us, 'Abd al-Rahman [in A: "'Abdullah"] ibn Mahdi narrated to us, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, that 'Umar used to perfume the mosque of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) every Friday. Its isnad is hasan, there is no harm in it. [Musnad Abi Ya'la (1/170).] And Allah knows best.

It is established in the two Sahihs from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he said: "A man's prayer in congregation is multiplied twenty-five times over his prayer in his house or in his market. That is because when he performs ablution and does it well [in F and A: "the ablution"], then goes out to the mosque, with nothing bringing him out but prayer, he does not take a step except that a degree is raised for him thereby and a sin is removed from him thereby. When he prays, the angels will not cease to send blessings upon him as long as he remains in his place of prayer, saying: 'O Allah, bless him; O Allah, have mercy upon him.' And he remains in prayer as long as he is waiting for the prayer." [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (647) and Sahih Muslim no. (649), from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him.]

Al-Daraqutni also transmits it as a marfu' (traced back to the Prophet ﷺ) report: "There is no prayer for the neighbour of the mosque except in the mosque." [[Sunan al-Daraqutni (1/420), through the chain of Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Yamami, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, as a marfu' report, with the same wording. It was also transmitted by al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak (1/246) and al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan al-Kubra (3/57), through Sulayman ibn Dawud, with the same wording. Sulayman ibn Dawud is agreed upon as weak. From the hadith of Jabir: al-Daraqutni also transmitted it in his Sunan (1/420), through Muhammad ibn Miskin, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Muhammad ibn Suqah, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Jabir, as a marfu' report, with the same wording. Abu al-Tayyib said in his commentary: "It contains Muhammad ibn Miskin. Al-Dhahabi said: he is not known, and his report is munkar (rejected). Al-Bukhari said: there is a problem (nazar) in the chain of his hadith."]].

In the Sunan (collections) it is also reported: "Give glad tidings to those who walk to the mosques in the darkness with complete light on the Day of Resurrection." [[Abu Dawud in his Sunan, no. (561), and al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan, no. (223), from the hadith of Buraydah ibn al-Husayb, may Allah be pleased with him. Al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a gharib (singular) hadith from this route, marfu'. It is sahih as a musnad (with a continuous chain) and as a mawquf (ending with the Companions) report, and it is not traced back (musnad) to the Prophet ﷺ."]].

It is recommended for one who enters the mosque to begin with his right foot, and to say what is established in Sahih al-Bukhari (Sahih al-Bukhari, the collection of al-Bukhari) from Abdullah ibn Amr [[In A: "Umar."]], may Allah be pleased with him [[In F and A: "with both of them."]], that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to say when he entered the mosque: "I seek refuge in Allah the Mighty, and in His Noble Face, and in His Ancient Authority, from the accursed Shaytan." [He said: "Ever?" He said: "Yes."] [[Addition from A.]] He said: "When he says that, Shaytan says: 'He has been protected from me for the rest of the day.'" [[I have not found it in Sahih al-Bukhari.
