Al-Mizzi mentioned it in Tuhfat al-Ashraf and Ibn al-Athir in Jami' al-Usul, and they attributed it only to Abu Dawud in his Sunan, no. (466).]]

Muslim transmitted with his chain, from Abu Humayd, or Abu Usayd, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "When one of you enters the mosque, let him say: 'O Allah, open for me the doors of Your mercy.' And when he leaves, let him say: 'O Allah, I ask You of Your bounty.'"

Al-Nasa'i transmitted it from both of them, from the Prophet ﷺ, the like of it. [[Sahih Muslim no. (713) and Sunan al-Nasa'i (2/53).]]

From Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "When one of you enters the mosque, let him greet the Prophet ﷺ and say: 'O Allah, open for me the doors of Your mercy.' And when he leaves, let him greet the Prophet ﷺ and say: 'O Allah, protect me from the accursed Shaytan.'"

Ibn Majah, Ibn Khuzaymah and Ibn Hibban transmitted it in their Sahihs. [[Sunan Ibn Majah no. (773), Sahih Ibn Khuzaymah no. (452), and Sahih Ibn Hibban no. (2048), al-Ihsan, all through Abu Bakr al-Hanafi, from al-Dahhak ibn Uthman, from al-Maqburi, from Abu Hurayrah, with the same wording. Al-Busayri said in al-Zawa'id (1/97): "This chain is sahih and its narrators are trustworthy."]]

Imam Ahmad said: Ismail ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Layth ibn Abi Sulaym narrated to us, from Abdullah ibn Hasan [[In A: "Husayn."]], from his mother Fatimah bint Husayn, from her grandmother Fatimah bint the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered the mosque, he would send blessings upon Muhammad and greet him with peace, then say: "O Allah, forgive me my sins, and open for me the doors of Your mercy." And when he left, he would send blessings upon Muhammad and greet him with peace, then say: "O Allah, forgive me my sins, and open for me the doors of Your bounty."

It was also transmitted by al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah. [[Al-Musnad (6/282), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (314), and Sunan Ibn Majah no. (771).]] Al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a hasan hadith, but its chain is not continuous (muttasil), because Fatimah bint al-Husayn al-Sughra did not meet Fatimah al-Kubra."

All of this which we have mentioned, along with what we have left out of the hadiths reported on this subject for the sake of brevity, is all included in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿in houses which Allah has permitted to be raised﴾.

* *

His saying: ﴿and His name is mentioned therein﴾, meaning: the name of Allah, as in His saying: ﴿O Children of Adam, take your adornment at every mosque﴾ [al-A'raf: 31], and His saying ﴿and set your faces upright at every mosque, and call upon Him, being sincere to Him in religion﴾ [al-A'raf: 29], and His saying ﴿And the mosques are for Allah, so do not invoke anyone with Allah﴾ [al-Jinn: 18].

Ibn Abbas said: ﴿and His name is mentioned therein﴾ means: His Book is recited therein.

* *

His saying: ﴿He is glorified therein in the mornings and the evenings﴾, meaning: in the early mornings and the late afternoons. Al-Asal is the plural of asil, which is the end of the day.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said, from Ibn Abbas: Every tasbih (glorification) in the Qur'an is salat (prayer).

Ali ibn Abi Talhah said, from Ibn Abbas: By al-ghuduww (the mornings) he means the Dawn Prayer (salat al-ghadah), and by al-asal he means the Afternoon Prayer (salat al-'asr). These are the first prayers which Allah made obligatory, so He wished to mention them and to remind His servants of them.

Al-Hasan and al-Dahhak said likewise: ﴿He is glorified therein in the mornings and the evenings﴾ means: the prayer.

As for the one of the reciters (qurra', the transmitters of the recognized readings) who read "yusabbihu lahu fiha bil-ghuduwwi wal-asal" with a fatha on the ba' of "yusabbu" [meaning it is in the passive voice, the subject not named], he stops at His saying ﴿wal-asal﴾ with a complete pause, and begins with His saying ﴿men (rijal) whom neither trade nor sale distracts from the remembrance of Allah﴾, and it is as if it explains the omitted subject, as the poet said:

"Let Yazid weep, one who is weak in disputes,
and one bewildered by what the calamities cast down..."

As if it were said: Who weeps for him? He said: This one weeps for him. And as if it were said: Who is glorified for Him therein? He said: Men.

But according to the reading of the one who reads "yusabbihu" with a kasra on the ba' [meaning it is active], making it a verb with ﴿rijal﴾ as its subject, then stopping is only good at the subject, since it completes the sentence.

His saying ﴿rijal (men)﴾ indicates their lofty aspirations, their high resolve and their elevated determination, through which they became the builders of the mosques, which are the houses of Allah on His earth, and the places of His worship, His thanks, His Oneness and His glorification, as He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿Among the believers are men who have been true to what they covenanted with Allah﴾ [al-Ahzab: 23].

As for women, their prayer in their houses is better for them, because of what Abu Dawud transmitted from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "The prayer of a woman in her house is better than her prayer in her chamber (hujrah), and her prayer in her inner room (makhda') is better than her prayer in her house." [[Sunan Abi Dawud no. (580).]]

Imam Ahmad said: Yahya ibn Ghaylan narrated to us, Rishdin narrated to us, Amr narrated to me, from Abu al-Samh, from al-Sa'ib, the freedman of Umm Salamah, from Umm Salamah, may Allah be pleased with her, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that he said: "The best of the mosques of women is the innermost part of their houses." [[Al-Musnad (6/297).]]

Imam Ahmad also said: Harun narrated to us, Abdullah ibn Wahb informed me, Dawud ibn Qays narrated to us, from Abdullah ibn Suwayd al-Ansari, from his paternal aunt Umm Humayd, the wife of Abu Humayd al-Sa'idi, that she came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I love to pray with you." He said: "I know that you love to pray with me, but your prayer in your house is better than your prayer in your chamber, and your prayer in your chamber is better than your prayer in your courtyard, and your prayer in your courtyard is better than your prayer in the mosque of your people, and your prayer in the mosque of your people is better than your prayer in my mosque." She said: So she ordered that a mosque be built for her in the furthest and darkest part of her house, and she used to pray in it until she met Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. [[Al-Musnad (6/371). They did not transmit it.]]

This is so. It is permissible for her, however, to attend the congregation of men, on condition that she does not harm any man by displaying adornment or wearing perfume, as is established in the two Sahihs (al-Bukhari and Muslim) from Abdullah ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Do not prevent the female servants of Allah from the mosques of Allah." [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (900) and Sahih Muslim no. (442).]]

Al-Bukhari and Muslim transmitted it, and Ahmad and Abu Dawud have: "And their houses are better for them." [[Al-Musnad (2/76) and Sunan Abi Dawud no. (567), from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both.]] And in another narration: "And let them go out while they are unscented (tafilat)," meaning: they have no fragrance.

It is established in Sahih Muslim, from Zaynab, the wife of Ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to us: "When one of you women attends the mosque, let her not touch perfume." [[Sahih Muslim no. (443).]]

And in the two Sahihs from Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, that she said: The women of the believers used to attend the Dawn Prayer with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, then they would return wrapped in their mantles (murut), so that they could not be recognized because of the darkness (ghalas). [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (578) and Sahih Muslim no. (645).]]

And in the two Sahihs also, from her, that she said: If the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had seen what the women have newly introduced, he would have prevented them from the mosques, just as the women of the Children of Israel were prevented. [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (869) and Sahih Muslim no. (445).]]

* *

His saying: ﴿men whom neither trade nor sale distracts from the remembrance of Allah﴾, like His saying: ﴿O you who believe, let not your wealth or your children distract you from the remembrance of Allah. And whoever does that, those are the losers﴾ [al-Munafiqun: 9], and He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿O you who believe, when the call is made for prayer on the day of Jumu'ah, hasten to the remembrance of Allah and leave off trade. That is better for you, if you only knew﴾ [al-Jumu'ah: 9].

He, may He be exalted, says: The world, its adornment, its finery and the pleasures of its trade and its profits do not distract them from the remembrance of their Lord, who is their Creator and their Provider. And those who know that what is with Him is better for them and more beneficial than what is in their hands, because what they have will perish and what is with Allah remains. For this reason He said: ﴿Trade and sale do not distract them from the remembrance of Allah, and the establishment of prayer, and the giving of zakah﴾, meaning: they give precedence to His obedience, His will and His love over their own will and love.

Hushaym said, from Sayyar: I was told, from Ibn Mas'ud, that he saw some people of the market, when the call to prayer was made, leaving their trading and rising to prayer, and Abdullah said: These are among those whom Allah mentioned in His Book: ﴿men whom neither trade nor sale distracts from the remembrance of Allah﴾. [[Narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (18/113).]]

Likewise Amr ibn Dinar al-Qahramani narrated, from Salim, from Abdullah ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, that he was in the market when the prayer was established, so they closed their shops and entered the mosque. Ibn Umar said: It was concerning them that this was revealed: ﴿men whom neither trade nor sale distracts from the remembrance of Allah﴾. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Jarir. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (18/113).]]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Bakr al-San'ani narrated to us, Abu Sa'id, client of the Banu Hashim, narrated to us, Abdullah ibn Bujayr narrated to us, Abu Abd Rabb narrated to us, who said: Abu al-Darda', may Allah be pleased with him, said: I used to stand on these steps and trade on them, making three hundred dinars every day, and I attend the prayer in the mosque every day. Indeed, I do not say that this is not lawful, but I love to be among those about whom Allah said: ﴿men whom neither trade nor sale distracts from the remembrance of Allah﴾.

Amr ibn Dinar al-A'war said: I was with Salim ibn Abdullah, and we were heading to the mosque. We passed by the market of Madinah, where the people had stood up for prayer and covered their goods. Salim looked at their goods, with no one near them, and then recited this verse: ﴿Men whom neither trade nor sale distracts from the remembrance of Allah﴾. Then he said: "They are these people."

Sa'id ibn Abi al-Hasan and al-Dahhak said likewise: "Trade and sale do not distract them from coming to the prayer at its time."

Mutar al-Warraq said: "They used to buy and sell, but whenever one of them heard the call to prayer while the scales were in his hand, he lowered them and went to the prayer."

Ali ibn Abi Talhah reported from Ibn Abbas regarding ﴿neither trade nor sale distracts them from the remembrance of Allah﴾: "It means the obligatory prayer (al-salat al-maktubah)." Al-Rabi' ibn Anas and Muqatil ibn Hayyan said the same.

Al-Suddi said: "It means the prayer in congregation."

Also from Muqatil ibn Hayyan: "Such things do not distract them from attending the prayer, and from establishing it as Allah commanded them, and from observing its appointed times and what Allah entrusted them to guard in it."

* *

His saying: ﴿They fear a Day in which hearts and eyes will be turned about﴾ means the Day of Resurrection, the day in which hearts and eyes will be turned about, that is, from the severity of terror and the magnitude of its horrors. As Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And warn them of the Approaching Day, when hearts will rise up to the throats, choked with grief﴾ [Ghafir: 18]. And Allah the Exalted said: ﴿He only delays them until a Day when eyes will stare fixedly﴾ [Ibrahim: 42]. And Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And they give food, despite their love for it, to the needy, the orphan, and the captive, saying: "We feed you only for the sake of Allah. We desire no reward from you, nor thanks. Indeed, we fear from our Lord a Day austere and distressing." So Allah will protect them from the evil of that Day and will give them radiance and happiness, and will reward them for their patience with a garden and silk﴾ [Al-Insan: 8–12].

Here Allah says: ﴿that Allah may reward them for the best of what they did﴾, meaning: these are among those whose best deeds are accepted from them, and whose evil deeds He overlooks.

* *

His saying: ﴿and increase them from His bounty﴾ means He accepts the good from them and multiplies it for them, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not wrong even the weight of an atom; and if it is a good deed, He doubles it and gives from Himself a great reward﴾ [An-Nisa: 40]. And Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Whoever comes with a good deed will have ten times its like﴾ [Al-An'am: 160]. And He said: ﴿Who is it that would lend to Allah a goodly loan so that He may multiply it for him many times over?﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 245]. And He said: ﴿And Allah multiplies for whom He wills﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 261], just as He said here: ﴿And Allah provides for whom He wills without account﴾.

It is reported from Ibn Mas'ud that milk was brought to him, and he offered it to his companions one by one, and none of them drank it because they were fasting. Ibn Mas'ud, who was not fasting, took it and drank it. Then he recited the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿They fear a Day in which hearts and eyes will be turned about﴾. Related by al-Nasa'i and Ibn Abi Hatim, from the hadith of al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, from Alqamah, from him [[Mentioned by al-Mizzi in Tuhfat al-Ashraf under no. (9435), and attributed it to al-Nasa'i in al-Mawa'iz.]].

Ibn Abi Hatim also said: My father related to us, Suwayd ibn Sa'id related to us, Ali ibn Mushir related to us, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Asma' bint Yazid, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "When Allah gathers the first and the last on the Day of Resurrection, a caller will come and call out with a voice that the creatures will hear: 'Let the people of the gathering know who is most worthy of honour. Let those stand up whom neither trade nor sale distracts from the remembrance of Allah.' They will stand up, and they will be few. Then all the rest of creation will be called to account." [[Also related by Hannad in al-Zuhd under no. (176), through Abu Mu'awiyah, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq, with the same chain. Abd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq is weak.]]

Al-Tabarani related, from the hadith of Baqiyyah, from Isma'il ibn Abd Allah al-Kindi, from al-A'mash, from Abu Wa'il, from Ibn Mas'ud, from the Prophet ﷺ regarding His saying: ﴿that He may pay them their wages and increase them from His bounty﴾ [Fatir: 30]: "﴿Their wages﴾ means He will admit them into Paradise, ﴿and increase them from His bounty﴾ means intercession for whoever is owed intercession, for those who did good to them in the world." [[Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir of al-Tabarani (10/248). The hafiz Ibn Kathir said when commenting on verse 173 of Surat al-Nisa': "This chain does not hold up; but when it is reported from Ibn Mas'ud as a mawquf (companion's saying), it is good."]]

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 24, verses 36–38 (part 1 of 3):

When Allah, the Exalted, struck the [parable [[addition from manuscripts F and A]]] of the believer's heart, and what it contains of guidance and knowledge, by the lamp in the clear glass, which is kindled with good oil, and that is like a lamp-stand, He mentioned its place, which is the mosques, which are the most beloved places on earth to Allah, the Exalted. They are His houses in which He is worshipped and in which He is made One. So He said: ﴿in houses which Allah has permitted to be raised﴾. That is, Allah, the Exalted, commanded that they be raised, meaning that they be purified from filth, idle talk, and deeds and words that are not fitting in them. As 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah reported from Ibn 'Abbas concerning this noble verse, ﴿in houses which Allah has permitted to be raised﴾, he said: Allah, glorified is He, forbade idle talk in them. Likewise said 'Ikrimah, Abu Salih, al-Dahhak, Nafi' ibn Jubayr, Abu Bakr ibn Sulayman ibn Abi Hathmah [in F and A: "Khaythamah"], Sufyan ibn Husayn, and others among the scholars of tafsir [in F and A: "tafsir"].

Qatadah said: They are these mosques. Allah, glorified is He, commanded that they be built and raised, and commanded that they be maintained and purified. It has been mentioned to us that Ka'b [al-Ahbar] used to say: "Indeed, it is written in the Tawrah (Torah): 'Verily, My houses on earth are the mosques, and whoever performs ablution and does it well, then visits Me in My house, I will honour him, and it is due upon the one visited to honour the visitor.'" Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it in his Tafsir.

Many hadiths have come concerning the building of mosques, respecting and venerating them, and perfuming and fumigating them. This has a separate place where it is mentioned, and I have written a separate booklet on that, and to Allah belongs all praise and grace. With the help of Allah, the Exalted, we will mention here a portion of that, if Allah wills, and in Him is trust and upon Him is reliance:

From the Commander of the Faithful, 'Uthman ibn 'Affan, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "Whoever builds a mosque seeking thereby the Face of Allah, Allah will build for him a like of it in Paradise." It is recorded by both [al-Bukhari and Muslim] in their Sahihs. [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (450) and Sahih Muslim no. (533).]

Ibn Majah narrated from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever builds a mosque in which the name of Allah is mentioned, Allah will build for him a house in Paradise." [Sunan Ibn Majah no. (735), through al-Walid ibn Abi al-Walid from 'Uthman ibn 'Abdullah from 'Umar. Al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id (1/260): "This isnad is mursal; 'Uthman ibn 'Abdullah ibn Suraqah narrated from 'Umar, and he is his maternal grandfather, but he did not hear from him, as stated by al-Mizzi."]

And for al-Nasa'i, from 'Amr ibn 'Abasah, the like of it. [In A: "'Anbasah".] [Sunan al-Nasa'i (2/31).] The hadiths on this are very numerous.

From 'A'ishah, may Allah be pleased with her, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) commanded that mosques be built in the neighbourhoods, and that they be cleaned and perfumed. [al-Musnad (6/279), Sunan Abi Dawud no. (455), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (594), and Sunan Ibn Majah no. (759).] It was narrated by Ahmad and the authors of the Sunan except al-Nasa'i. And for Ahmad and Abu Dawud, from Samurah ibn Jundub, a similar report. [al-Musnad (5/17) and Sunan Abi Dawud no. (456).]

Al-Bukhari said: 'Umar said: "Build for the people a shelter that protects them, and beware of reddening or yellowing [the mosque], lest you tempt the people." [Sahih al-Bukhari (1/539), Fath.]

Ibn Majah narrated from him (i.e., 'Umar) who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The deeds of no people have ever been evil except that they adorned their mosques." [Sunan Ibn Majah no. (741), through Jabbarah ibn al-Mughallas from 'Abd al-Karim ibn 'Abd al-Rahman from 'Amr ibn Maymun from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, with the same. Al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id (1/262): "In this isnad is Jabbarah ibn al-Mughallas, who has been accused (of lying)."] In its isnad there is weakness.

Abu Dawud narrated from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with them both, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I have not been commanded to decorate the mosques." Ibn 'Abbas said: "You will surely adorn them as the Jews and Christians adorned them." [Sunan Abi Dawud no. (448).]

From Anas, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The Hour will not come until the people boast about mosques." It was narrated by Imam Ahmad and the authors of the Sunan except al-Tirmidhi. [al-Musnad (3/134), Sunan Abi Dawud no. (449), Sunan al-Nasa'i (2/32), and Sunan Ibn Majah no. (739).]

From Buraydah, that a man recited poetry in the mosque, and he said: "Who calls to the red camel?" The Prophet (ﷺ) said: "May you not find it! The mosques were only built for what they were built for." Narrated by Muslim. [Sahih Muslim no. (569).]

From 'Amr ibn Shu'ayb, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) forbade buying and selling in the mosques, and reciting poetry in them. Narrated by Ahmad and the authors of the Sunan. [al-Musnad (2/179), Sunan Abi Dawud no. (1079), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (322), Sunan al-Nasa'i (2/47), and Sunan Ibn Majah no. (749).] Al-Tirmidhi said: Hasan.

From Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "When you see someone buying or selling in the mosque, say: 'May Allah not make your trade profitable.' And when you see someone searching for a lost item in the mosque, say: 'May Allah not return it to you.'" Narrated by al-Tirmidhi, who said: Hasan gharib. [Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3121).]

Ibn Majah and others narrated, from the hadith of Ibn 'Umar, traced to the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "There are matters that are not befitting in the mosque: it should not be used as a path, weapons should not be displayed in it, a bow should not be strung in it, arrows should not be scattered in it, raw meat should not be carried through it, a prescribed punishment should not be carried out in it, retaliation should not be exacted in it, and it should not be made a marketplace." [Sunan Ibn Majah no. (748). Al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id (1/264): "In this isnad is Zayd ibn Jubayrah. Ibn 'Abd al-Barr said: They are agreed that he is weak."]

From Wathilah ibn al-Asqa', from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: "Keep your children and your insane away from the mosques, and your buying and selling, and your disputes, and the raising of your voices, and the carrying out of your prescribed punishments, and the drawing of your swords, and make for their doors places of purification, and perfume them on Fridays." [In A and F: "its isnad".]

Ibn Majah also narrated it, and in its isnad there is weakness. [Sunan Ibn Majah no. (750). Al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id (1/265): "This isnad is weak; Abu Sa'id is Muhammad ibn Sa'id al-Masallub. Ahmad said: he used to deliberately fabricate hadith. Then he said: al-Harith ibn Nabhan is weak."]

As for "it should not be made a path," some scholars disliked passing through it except out of need when one finds an alternative to it. In a report: "Indeed the angels marvel at a man who passes by the mosque and does not pray in it."

As for "weapons should not be displayed in it, a bow should not be strung in it, and arrows should not be scattered in it," this is due to fear that some people may be hit by them, because of the large number of worshippers in it. For this reason, when someone passed by with arrows, the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) commanded him to hold their points, so as not to harm anyone, as is established in the Sahih. [Narrated by Muslim in his Sahih no. (2615) from the hadith of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari.]

As for the prohibition of passing through it with raw meat, it is due to fear of blood dripping from it, just as a menstruating woman is forbidden from passing through it if she fears staining it.

As for "a prescribed punishment should not be carried out in it, nor retaliation," it is due to fear of impurity arising in it from the one being punished or the one whose limb is cut off.

As for "it should not be made a marketplace," it is due to what preceded of the prohibition of buying and selling in it, for it was only built for the remembrance of Allah and for prayer, as the Prophet (ﷺ), upon whom be prayers and peace, said to that Bedouin who urinated in a corner of the mosque: "Indeed the mosques were not built for this; they were only built for the remembrance of Allah and for prayer in them." Then he commanded a bucket of water, which was poured over his urine. [Narrated by Muslim in his Sahih no. (284) from the hadith of Anas ibn Malik, may Allah be pleased with him.]

In the second hadith: "Keep your children away from your mosques," this is because they play in them and it is not suitable for them. 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, may Allah be pleased with him, when he saw children playing in the mosque, would strike them with the mikhfaqah, which is the whip (durrah). He used to inspect (yafattish) the mosque after 'Isha', and would not leave anyone in it.

"And your insane": meaning, because of the weakness of their minds, and people mocking them, which leads to playing in it, and due to fear of their soiling the mosque, and similar things.

"And your buying and your selling": as previously mentioned.

"And your disputes": meaning, litigation and judging in it. For this reason many scholars stated that a judge should not set himself up to settle cases in the mosque, but should be in another place, because of the abundance of arguments, quarrels, and loud clamour that is not suitable for it. For this reason he (ﷺ) said after it: "and the raising of your voices."

Al-Bukhari said: Ali ibn 'Abd Allah narrated to us, Yahya ibn Sa'id narrated to us, al-Ju'ayd ibn 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, who said: Yazid ibn Khusayfah narrated to me, from al-Sa'ib ibn Yazid al-Kindi, who said: I was standing in the mosque when a man threw pebbles at me, so I looked and saw that it was 'Umar ibn al-Khattab. He said: "Go and bring me these two." I brought them to him, and he said: "Who are you two?" or "Where are you from?" They said: "From the people of al-Ta'if." He said: "If you were from the people of this town, I would have punished you both. You raise your voices in the mosque of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ)!" [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (470).]

Al-Nasa'i said: Suwayd ibn Nasr narrated to us, from Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak, from Shu'bah, from Sa'd ibn Ibrahim, from his father Ibrahim ibn 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf, who said: 'Umar heard the voice of a man in the mosque and said: "Do you know where you are?" And this is also authentic. [Al-Mizzi mentioned it in Tuhfat al-Ashraf (8/4) and attributed it to al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra, in al-Mawa'iz.]

* *

As for his saying: "and the raising of your voices," and "the drawing of your swords," these have preceded.

* *

As for his saying: "and make for their doors places of purification," meaning the latrines, which are used for ablution and relieving oneself. Near the mosque of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) there were wells from which they drew water, and they would drink from them, purify themselves, perform ablution, and other things.

* *

As for his saying: "and perfume them on Fridays," meaning: fumigate them on the days of Friday, because of the large gathering of people on that day.

Al-Hafiz Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili said: 'Ubayd Allah narrated to us, 'Abd al-Rahman [in A: "'Abdullah"] ibn Mahdi narrated to us, from 'Abdullah ibn 'Umar, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, that 'Umar used to perfume the mosque of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) every Friday. Its isnad is hasan, there is no harm in it. [Musnad Abi Ya'la (1/170).] And Allah knows best.

It is established in the two Sahihs from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he said: "A man's prayer in congregation is multiplied twenty-five times over his prayer in his house or in his market. That is because when he performs ablution and does it well [in F and A: "the ablution"], then goes out to the mosque, with nothing bringing him out but prayer, he does not take a step except that a degree is raised for him thereby and a sin is removed from him thereby. When he prays, the angels will not cease to send blessings upon him as long as he remains in his place of prayer, saying: 'O Allah, bless him; O Allah, have mercy upon him.' And he remains in prayer as long as he is waiting for the prayer." [Sahih al-Bukhari no. (647) and Sahih Muslim no. (649), from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him.]

Al-Daraqutni also transmits it as a marfu' (traced back to the Prophet ﷺ) report: "There is no prayer for the neighbour of the mosque except in the mosque." [[Sunan al-Daraqutni (1/420), through the chain of Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Yamami, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, as a marfu' report, with the same wording. It was also transmitted by al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak (1/246) and al-Bayhaqi in al-Sunan al-Kubra (3/57), through Sulayman ibn Dawud, with the same wording. Sulayman ibn Dawud is agreed upon as weak. From the hadith of Jabir: al-Daraqutni also transmitted it in his Sunan (1/420), through Muhammad ibn Miskin, from Abdullah ibn Bukayr, from Muhammad ibn Suqah, from Muhammad ibn al-Munkadir, from Jabir, as a marfu' report, with the same wording. Abu al-Tayyib said in his commentary: "It contains Muhammad ibn Miskin. Al-Dhahabi said: he is not known, and his report is munkar (rejected). Al-Bukhari said: there is a problem (nazar) in the chain of his hadith."]].

In the Sunan (collections) it is also reported: "Give glad tidings to those who walk to the mosques in the darkness with complete light on the Day of Resurrection." [[Abu Dawud in his Sunan, no. (561), and al-Tirmidhi in his Sunan, no. (223), from the hadith of Buraydah ibn al-Husayb, may Allah be pleased with him. Al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a gharib (singular) hadith from this route, marfu'. It is sahih as a musnad (with a continuous chain) and as a mawquf (ending with the Companions) report, and it is not traced back (musnad) to the Prophet ﷺ."]].

It is recommended for one who enters the mosque to begin with his right foot, and to say what is established in Sahih al-Bukhari (Sahih al-Bukhari, the collection of al-Bukhari) from Abdullah ibn Amr [[In A: "Umar."]], may Allah be pleased with him [[In F and A: "with both of them."]], that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ used to say when he entered the mosque: "I seek refuge in Allah the Mighty, and in His Noble Face, and in His Ancient Authority, from the accursed Shaytan." [He said: "Ever?" He said: "Yes."] [[Addition from A.]] He said: "When he says that, Shaytan says: 'He has been protected from me for the rest of the day.'" [[I have not found it in Sahih al-Bukhari. Al-Mizzi mentioned it in Tuhfat al-Ashraf and Ibn al-Athir in Jami' al-Usul, and they attributed it only to Abu Dawud in his Sunan, no. (466).]]

Muslim transmitted with his chain, from Abu Humayd, or Abu Usayd, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "When one of you enters the mosque, let him say: 'O Allah, open for me the doors of Your mercy.' And when he leaves, let him say: 'O Allah, I ask You of Your bounty.'"

Al-Nasa'i transmitted it from both of them, from the Prophet ﷺ, the like of it. [[Sahih Muslim no. (713) and Sunan al-Nasa'i (2/53).]]

From Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "When one of you enters the mosque, let him greet the Prophet ﷺ and say: 'O Allah, open for me the doors of Your mercy.' And when he leaves, let him greet the Prophet ﷺ and say: 'O Allah, protect me from the accursed Shaytan.'"

Ibn Majah, Ibn Khuzaymah and Ibn Hibban transmitted it in their Sahihs. [[Sunan Ibn Majah no. (773), Sahih Ibn Khuzaymah no. (452), and Sahih Ibn Hibban no. (2048), al-Ihsan, all through Abu Bakr al-Hanafi, from al-Dahhak ibn Uthman, from al-Maqburi, from Abu Hurayrah, with the same wording. Al-Busayri said in al-Zawa'id (1/97): "This chain is sahih and its narrators are trustworthy."]]

Imam Ahmad said: Ismail ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, Layth ibn Abi Sulaym narrated to us, from Abdullah ibn Hasan [[In A: "Husayn."]], from his mother Fatimah bint Husayn, from her grandmother Fatimah bint the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, who said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ entered the mosque, he would send blessings upon Muhammad and greet him with peace, then say: "O Allah, forgive me my sins, and open for me the doors of Your mercy." And when he left, he would send blessings upon Muhammad and greet him with peace, then say: "O Allah, forgive me my sins, and open for me the doors of Your bounty."

It was also transmitted by al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah. [[Al-Musnad (6/282), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (314), and Sunan Ibn Majah no. (771).]] Al-Tirmidhi said: "This is a hasan hadith, but its chain is not continuous (muttasil), because Fatimah bint al-Husayn al-Sughra did not meet Fatimah al-Kubra."

All of this which we have mentioned, along with what we have left out of the hadiths reported on this subject for the sake of brevity, is all included in His saying, may He be exalted: ﴿in houses which Allah has permitted to be raised﴾.

* *

His saying: ﴿and His name is mentioned therein﴾, meaning: the name of Allah, as in His saying: ﴿O Children of Adam, take your adornment at every mosque﴾ [al-A'raf: 31], and His saying ﴿and set your faces upright at every mosque, and call upon Him, being sincere to Him in religion﴾ [al-A'raf: 29], and His saying ﴿And the mosques are for Allah, so do not invoke anyone with Allah﴾ [al-Jinn: 18].

Ibn Abbas said: ﴿and His name is mentioned therein﴾ means: His Book is recited therein.

* *

His saying: ﴿He is glorified therein in the mornings and the evenings﴾, meaning: in the early mornings and the late afternoons. Al-Asal is the plural of asil, which is the end of the day.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said, from Ibn Abbas: Every tasbih (glorification) in the Qur'an is salat (prayer).

Ali ibn Abi Talhah said, from Ibn Abbas: By al-ghuduww (the mornings) he means the Dawn Prayer (salat al-ghadah), and by al-asal he means the Afternoon Prayer (salat al-'asr). These are the first prayers which Allah made obligatory, so He wished to mention them and to remind His servants of them.

Al-Hasan and al-Dahhak said likewise: ﴿He is glorified therein in the mornings and the evenings﴾ means: the prayer.

As for the one of the reciters (qurra', the transmitters of the recognized readings) who read "yusabbihu lahu fiha bil-ghuduwwi wal-asal" with a fatha on the ba' of "yusabbu" [meaning it is in the passive voice, the subject not named], he stops at His saying ﴿wal-asal﴾ with a complete pause, and begins with His saying ﴿men (rijal) whom neither trade nor sale distracts from the remembrance of Allah﴾, and it is as if it explains the omitted subject, as the poet said:

"Let Yazid weep, one who is weak in disputes,
and one bewildered by what the calamities cast down..."

As if it were said: Who weeps for him? He said: This one weeps for him. And as if it were said: Who is glorified for Him therein? He said: Men.

But according to the reading of the one who reads "yusabbihu" with a kasra on the ba' [meaning it is active], making it a verb with ﴿rijal﴾ as its subject, then stopping is only good at the subject, since it completes the sentence.

His saying ﴿rijal (men)﴾ indicates their lofty aspirations, their high resolve and their elevated determination, through which they became the builders of the mosques, which are the houses of Allah on His earth, and the places of His worship, His thanks, His Oneness and His glorification, as He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿Among the believers are men who have been true to what they covenanted with Allah﴾ [al-Ahzab: 23].

As for women, their prayer in their houses is better for them, because of what Abu Dawud transmitted from Abdullah ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, from the Prophet ﷺ, who said: "The prayer of a woman in her house is better than her prayer in her chamber (hujrah), and her prayer in her inner room (makhda') is better than her prayer in her house." [[Sunan Abi Dawud no. (580).]]

Imam Ahmad said: Yahya ibn Ghaylan narrated to us, Rishdin narrated to us, Amr narrated to me, from Abu al-Samh, from al-Sa'ib, the freedman of Umm Salamah, from Umm Salamah, may Allah be pleased with her, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that he said: "The best of the mosques of women is the innermost part of their houses." [[Al-Musnad (6/297).]]

Imam Ahmad also said: Harun narrated to us, Abdullah ibn Wahb informed me, Dawud ibn Qays narrated to us, from Abdullah ibn Suwayd al-Ansari, from his paternal aunt Umm Humayd, the wife of Abu Humayd al-Sa'idi, that she came to the Prophet ﷺ and said: "O Messenger of Allah, I love to pray with you." He said: "I know that you love to pray with me, but your prayer in your house is better than your prayer in your chamber, and your prayer in your chamber is better than your prayer in your courtyard, and your prayer in your courtyard is better than your prayer in the mosque of your people, and your prayer in the mosque of your people is better than your prayer in my mosque." She said: So she ordered that a mosque be built for her in the furthest and darkest part of her house, and she used to pray in it until she met Allah, the Mighty and Majestic. [[Al-Musnad (6/371). They did not transmit it.]]

This is so. It is permissible for her, however, to attend the congregation of men, on condition that she does not harm any man by displaying adornment or wearing perfume, as is established in the two Sahihs (al-Bukhari and Muslim) from Abdullah ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Do not prevent the female servants of Allah from the mosques of Allah." [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (900) and Sahih Muslim no. (442).]]

Al-Bukhari and Muslim transmitted it, and Ahmad and Abu Dawud have: "And their houses are better for them." [[Al-Musnad (2/76) and Sunan Abi Dawud no. (567), from the hadith of Abdullah ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both.]] And in another narration: "And let them go out while they are unscented (tafilat)," meaning: they have no fragrance.

It is established in Sahih Muslim, from Zaynab, the wife of Ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to us: "When one of you women attends the mosque, let her not touch perfume." [[Sahih Muslim no. (443).]]

And in the two Sahihs from Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her, that she said: The women of the believers used to attend the Dawn Prayer with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, then they would return wrapped in their mantles (murut), so that they could not be recognized because of the darkness (ghalas). [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (578) and Sahih Muslim no. (645).]]

And in the two Sahihs also, from her, that she said: If the Messenger of Allah ﷺ had seen what the women have newly introduced, he would have prevented them from the mosques, just as the women of the Children of Israel were prevented. [[Sahih al-Bukhari no. (869) and Sahih Muslim no. (445).]]

* *

His saying: ﴿men whom neither trade nor sale distracts from the remembrance of Allah﴾, like His saying: ﴿O you who believe, let not your wealth or your children distract you from the remembrance of Allah. And whoever does that, those are the losers﴾ [al-Munafiqun: 9], and He, may He be exalted, said: ﴿O you who believe, when the call is made for prayer on the day of Jumu'ah, hasten to the remembrance of Allah and leave off trade. That is better for you, if you only knew﴾ [al-Jumu'ah: 9].

He, may He be exalted, says: The world, its adornment, its finery and the pleasures of its trade and its profits do not distract them from the remembrance of their Lord, who is their Creator and their Provider. And those who know that what is with Him is better for them and more beneficial than what is in their hands, because what they have will perish and what is with Allah remains. For this reason He said: ﴿Trade and sale do not distract them from the remembrance of Allah, and the establishment of prayer, and the giving of zakah﴾, meaning: they give precedence to His obedience, His will and His love over their own will and love.

Hushaym said, from Sayyar: I was told, from Ibn Mas'ud, that he saw some people of the market, when the call to prayer was made, leaving their trading and rising to prayer, and Abdullah said: These are among those whom Allah mentioned in His Book: ﴿men whom neither trade nor sale distracts from the remembrance of Allah﴾. [[Narrated by al-Tabari in his Tafsir (18/113).]]

Likewise Amr ibn Dinar al-Qahramani narrated, from Salim, from Abdullah ibn Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, that he was in the market when the prayer was established, so they closed their shops and entered the mosque. Ibn Umar said: It was concerning them that this was revealed: ﴿men whom neither trade nor sale distracts from the remembrance of Allah﴾. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Jarir. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (18/113).]]

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Muhammad ibn Abdullah ibn Bakr al-San'ani narrated to us, Abu Sa'id, client of the Banu Hashim, narrated to us, Abdullah ibn Bujayr narrated to us, Abu Abd Rabb narrated to us, who said: Abu al-Darda', may Allah be pleased with him, said: I used to stand on these steps and trade on them, making three hundred dinars every day, and I attend the prayer in the mosque every day. Indeed, I do not say that this is not lawful, but I love to be among those about whom Allah said: ﴿men whom neither trade nor sale distracts from the remembrance of Allah﴾.

Amr ibn Dinar al-A'war said: I was with Salim ibn Abdullah, and we were heading to the mosque. We passed by the market of Madinah, where the people had stood up for prayer and covered their goods. Salim looked at their goods, with no one near them, and then recited this verse: ﴿Men whom neither trade nor sale distracts from the remembrance of Allah﴾. Then he said: "They are these people."

Sa'id ibn Abi al-Hasan and al-Dahhak said likewise: "Trade and sale do not distract them from coming to the prayer at its time."

Mutar al-Warraq said: "They used to buy and sell, but whenever one of them heard the call to prayer while the scales were in his hand, he lowered them and went to the prayer."

Ali ibn Abi Talhah reported from Ibn Abbas regarding ﴿neither trade nor sale distracts them from the remembrance of Allah﴾: "It means the obligatory prayer (al-salat al-maktubah)." Al-Rabi' ibn Anas and Muqatil ibn Hayyan said the same.

Al-Suddi said: "It means the prayer in congregation."

Also from Muqatil ibn Hayyan: "Such things do not distract them from attending the prayer, and from establishing it as Allah commanded them, and from observing its appointed times and what Allah entrusted them to guard in it."

* *

His saying: ﴿They fear a Day in which hearts and eyes will be turned about﴾ means the Day of Resurrection, the day in which hearts and eyes will be turned about, that is, from the severity of terror and the magnitude of its horrors. As Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And warn them of the Approaching Day, when hearts will rise up to the throats, choked with grief﴾ [Ghafir: 18]. And Allah the Exalted said: ﴿He only delays them until a Day when eyes will stare fixedly﴾ [Ibrahim: 42]. And Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And they give food, despite their love for it, to the needy, the orphan, and the captive, saying: "We feed you only for the sake of Allah. We desire no reward from you, nor thanks. Indeed, we fear from our Lord a Day austere and distressing." So Allah will protect them from the evil of that Day and will give them radiance and happiness, and will reward them for their patience with a garden and silk﴾ [Al-Insan: 8–12].

Here Allah says: ﴿that Allah may reward them for the best of what they did﴾, meaning: these are among those whose best deeds are accepted from them, and whose evil deeds He overlooks.

* *

His saying: ﴿and increase them from His bounty﴾ means He accepts the good from them and multiplies it for them, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, Allah does not wrong even the weight of an atom; and if it is a good deed, He doubles it and gives from Himself a great reward﴾ [An-Nisa: 40]. And Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Whoever comes with a good deed will have ten times its like﴾ [Al-An'am: 160]. And He said: ﴿Who is it that would lend to Allah a goodly loan so that He may multiply it for him many times over?﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 245]. And He said: ﴿And Allah multiplies for whom He wills﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 261], just as He said here: ﴿And Allah provides for whom He wills without account﴾.

It is reported from Ibn Mas'ud that milk was brought to him, and he offered it to his companions one by one, and none of them drank it because they were fasting. Ibn Mas'ud, who was not fasting, took it and drank it. Then he recited the saying of Allah the Exalted: ﴿They fear a Day in which hearts and eyes will be turned about﴾. Related by al-Nasa'i and Ibn Abi Hatim, from the hadith of al-A'mash, from Ibrahim, from Alqamah, from him [[Mentioned by al-Mizzi in Tuhfat al-Ashraf under no. (9435), and attributed it to al-Nasa'i in al-Mawa'iz.]].

Ibn Abi Hatim also said: My father related to us, Suwayd ibn Sa'id related to us, Ali ibn Mushir related to us, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq, from Shahr ibn Hawshab, from Asma' bint Yazid, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "When Allah gathers the first and the last on the Day of Resurrection, a caller will come and call out with a voice that the creatures will hear: 'Let the people of the gathering know who is most worthy of honour. Let those stand up whom neither trade nor sale distracts from the remembrance of Allah.' They will stand up, and they will be few. Then all the rest of creation will be called to account." [[Also related by Hannad in al-Zuhd under no. (176), through Abu Mu'awiyah, from Abd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq, with the same chain. Abd al-Rahman ibn Ishaq is weak.]]

Al-Tabarani related, from the hadith of Baqiyyah, from Isma'il ibn Abd Allah al-Kindi, from al-A'mash, from Abu Wa'il, from Ibn Mas'ud, from the Prophet ﷺ regarding His saying: ﴿that He may pay them their wages and increase them from His bounty﴾ [Fatir: 30]: "﴿Their wages﴾ means He will admit them into Paradise, ﴿and increase them from His bounty﴾ means intercession for whoever is owed intercession, for those who did good to them in the world." [[Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir of al-Tabarani (10/248). The hafiz Ibn Kathir said when commenting on verse 173 of Surat al-Nisa': "This chain does not hold up; but when it is reported from Ibn Mas'ud as a mawquf (companion's saying), it is good."]]

These are two parables that Allah has struck for the two types of disbelievers, just as He struck two parables for the hypocrites at the beginning of al-Baqarah (at verses 17 and 19), one of fire and one of water, and just as He struck two parables for what settles in the hearts of guidance and knowledge in Surat al-Ra'd (at verse 17), one of water and one of fire. We have already discussed each of them in its place, sufficiently to make repetition unnecessary, and to Allah belongs all praise and grace.

As for the first of these two parables, it applies to the disbelievers who call others to their disbelief, who think that they stand upon something of deeds and beliefs, while in reality they stand upon nothing. Their example in this is that of the mirage seen in the low flat lands of the earth from a distance, as if it were a surging sea.

The qi'ah (plural qi'an) is the plural of qa', like jar and jirah. The qa' is also the singular of qi'an, as one says jar and jiran. It is the level, wide, spread-out land, and it is in such ground that the mirage (sarab) occurs, and it occurs only after midday. As for the al (the shimmering haze), it occurs at the beginning of the day, appearing like water between the sky and the earth. When one who is in need of water sees the mirage, he supposes it to be water and heads toward it to drink from it, but when he reaches it, ﴿he finds it to be nothing﴾. So likewise the disbeliever supposes that he has done a deed and that he has attained something. But when he comes before Allah on the Day of Resurrection, and Allah calls him to account for it and examines his actions, he will find nothing at all of it accepted, either because of lack of sincerity or because of not following the Law (shari'ah), as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And We will turn to what they did of deeds and make them scattered dust﴾ [al-Furqan: 23].

Here He said: ﴿and finds Allah with him, and He will pay him in full his account, and Allah is swift in reckoning﴾. It has been narrated in this manner from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, Qatadah and others besides them.

In the two Sahihs (Bukhari and Muslim) it is related that on the Day of Resurrection it will be said to the Jews: "What were you worshipping?" They will say: "We used to worship 'Uzayr, the son of Allah." It will be said: "You have lied; Allah did not take any son. What do you desire?" They will say: "O our Lord, we are thirsty, so give us drink." It will be said: "Do you not see?" Then the Fire will be displayed to them as if it were a mirage, its parts smashing one another, and they will set off and throw themselves into it. [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4581, and Sahih Muslim, no. 183, from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him.]

This parable is an example of those with compound ignorance (al-jahl al-murakkab, the ignorance that is ignorant of itself). As for those with simple ignorance (al-jahl al-basit, ignorance that knows it does not know), who are the stupid, foolish blind followers of the leaders of disbelief, the deaf and dumb who do not reason, their example is as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Or like darknesses in a deep sea﴾. Qatadah said: "It is the deep one." ﴿Covered by a wave, above which is a wave, above which is a cloud, darknesses upon darknesses; when he extends his hand he can hardly see it﴾, meaning he almost cannot see it because of the intensity of the darkness. This is the likeness of the heart of the disbeliever with simple ignorance, the blind follower who does not know where he is going and does not know the state of the one who leads him. Rather, as is said in the proverb to the ignorant man: "Where are you going?" He says: "With them." It is said: "Then where are they going?" He says: "I do not know."

Al-'Awfi related from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with both of them, regarding ﴿covered by a wave, above which is a wave, above which is a cloud﴾, that it means the veil that is upon the heart, the hearing and the sight. This is like His saying: ﴿Allah has sealed upon their hearts and upon their hearing, and over their sight is a veil, and for them is a great punishment﴾ [al-Baqarah: 7], and like His saying: ﴿Have you seen him who has taken his desire as his god, and Allah has sent him astray knowingly, and has set a seal upon his hearing and his heart, and placed over his sight a covering? Who then will guide him after Allah? Will you not then take heed?﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 23].

Ubayy ibn Ka'b said, regarding His saying ﴿darknesses, some above others﴾: he turns in five kinds of darkness: his speech is darkness, his deed is darkness, his entry is darkness, his exit is darkness, and his destination on the Day of Resurrection is toward darknesses, toward the Fire.

Al-Rabi' ibn Anas and al-Suddi said something similar to this as well.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And whomever Allah does not grant light, for him there is no light﴾, meaning: whomever Allah does not guide is lost, ignorant, bewildered, ruined and a disbeliever, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Whomever Allah leaves astray, there is no guide for him﴾ [al-A'raf: 186]. This is in contrast to what He said regarding the believers: ﴿Allah guides to His light whom He wills﴾. So we ask the Mighty Allah to place light in our hearts, light on our right, light on our left, and to make light great for us.

These are two parables that Allah has struck for the two types of disbelievers, just as He struck two parables for the hypocrites at the beginning of al-Baqarah (at verses 17 and 19), one of fire and one of water, and just as He struck two parables for what settles in the hearts of guidance and knowledge in Surat al-Ra'd (at verse 17), one of water and one of fire. We have already discussed each of them in its place, sufficiently to make repetition unnecessary, and to Allah belongs all praise and grace.

As for the first of these two parables, it applies to the disbelievers who call others to their disbelief, who think that they stand upon something of deeds and beliefs, while in reality they stand upon nothing. Their example in this is that of the mirage seen in the low flat lands of the earth from a distance, as if it were a surging sea.

The qi'ah (plural qi'an) is the plural of qa', like jar and jirah. The qa' is also the singular of qi'an, as one says jar and jiran. It is the level, wide, spread-out land, and it is in such ground that the mirage (sarab) occurs, and it occurs only after midday. As for the al (the shimmering haze), it occurs at the beginning of the day, appearing like water between the sky and the earth. When one who is in need of water sees the mirage, he supposes it to be water and heads toward it to drink from it, but when he reaches it, ﴿he finds it to be nothing﴾. So likewise the disbeliever supposes that he has done a deed and that he has attained something. But when he comes before Allah on the Day of Resurrection, and Allah calls him to account for it and examines his actions, he will find nothing at all of it accepted, either because of lack of sincerity or because of not following the Law (shari'ah), as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿And We will turn to what they did of deeds and make them scattered dust﴾ [al-Furqan: 23].

Here He said: ﴿and finds Allah with him, and He will pay him in full his account, and Allah is swift in reckoning﴾. It has been narrated in this manner from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, Ibn 'Abbas, Mujahid, Qatadah and others besides them.

In the two Sahihs (Bukhari and Muslim) it is related that on the Day of Resurrection it will be said to the Jews: "What were you worshipping?" They will say: "We used to worship 'Uzayr, the son of Allah." It will be said: "You have lied; Allah did not take any son. What do you desire?" They will say: "O our Lord, we are thirsty, so give us drink." It will be said: "Do you not see?" Then the Fire will be displayed to them as if it were a mirage, its parts smashing one another, and they will set off and throw themselves into it. [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 4581, and Sahih Muslim, no. 183, from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him.]

This parable is an example of those with compound ignorance (al-jahl al-murakkab, the ignorance that is ignorant of itself). As for those with simple ignorance (al-jahl al-basit, ignorance that knows it does not know), who are the stupid, foolish blind followers of the leaders of disbelief, the deaf and dumb who do not reason, their example is as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Or like darknesses in a deep sea﴾. Qatadah said: "It is the deep one." ﴿Covered by a wave, above which is a wave, above which is a cloud, darknesses upon darknesses; when he extends his hand he can hardly see it﴾, meaning he almost cannot see it because of the intensity of the darkness. This is the likeness of the heart of the disbeliever with simple ignorance, the blind follower who does not know where he is going and does not know the state of the one who leads him. Rather, as is said in the proverb to the ignorant man: "Where are you going?" He says: "With them." It is said: "Then where are they going?" He says: "I do not know."

Al-'Awfi related from Ibn 'Abbas, may Allah be pleased with both of them, regarding ﴿covered by a wave, above which is a wave, above which is a cloud﴾, that it means the veil that is upon the heart, the hearing and the sight. This is like His saying: ﴿Allah has sealed upon their hearts and upon their hearing, and over their sight is a veil, and for them is a great punishment﴾ [al-Baqarah: 7], and like His saying: ﴿Have you seen him who has taken his desire as his god, and Allah has sent him astray knowingly, and has set a seal upon his hearing and his heart, and placed over his sight a covering? Who then will guide him after Allah? Will you not then take heed?﴾ [al-Jathiyah: 23].

Ubayy ibn Ka'b said, regarding His saying ﴿darknesses, some above others﴾: he turns in five kinds of darkness: his speech is darkness, his deed is darkness, his entry is darkness, his exit is darkness, and his destination on the Day of Resurrection is toward darknesses, toward the Fire.

Al-Rabi' ibn Anas and al-Suddi said something similar to this as well.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And whomever Allah does not grant light, for him there is no light﴾, meaning: whomever Allah does not guide is lost, ignorant, bewildered, ruined and a disbeliever, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Whomever Allah leaves astray, there is no guide for him﴾ [al-A'raf: 186]. This is in contrast to what He said regarding the believers: ﴿Allah guides to His light whom He wills﴾. So we ask the Mighty Allah to place light in our hearts, light on our right, light on our left, and to make light great for us.

Allah informs that whoever is in the heavens and the earth glorifies Him, that is, the angels, humankind, the jinn, animals, and even inanimate things, as He says: ﴿The seven heavens and the earth and whoever is in them glorify Him. And there is not a thing except that it exalts [Allah] with His praise, but you do not understand their glorification. Indeed, He is ever Forbearing and Forgiving.﴾ [al-Isra: 44].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And the birds in flight﴾, meaning, while they are in flight they glorify their Lord and worship Him with a glorification He has inspired in them and guided them to, and He knows what they do. Therefore He says: ﴿Each has known its prayer and its glorification﴾, meaning, each has been guided by Him to its way and course in worshipping Allah, Mighty and Majestic.

Then He informs that He is Knowing of all of that, and nothing of it is hidden from Him. Therefore He says: ﴿And Allah is Knowing of what they do.﴾

Then Allah informs that to Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. He is the Judge who disposes of affairs, whose decree none can repel, and He is the God worthy of worship, to whom alone worship is due. ﴿And to Allah is the final return﴾, meaning the Day of Resurrection, when He will judge therein as He wills; ﴿that He may recompense those who did evil according to what they did and recompense those who did good with the best [reward]﴾ [an-Najm: 31]. He is the Creator, the Owner. Is it not that to Him belongs the judgment in this world and the Hereafter, and to Him belongs praise in the first and the last?!

The Exalted says that by His power He drives the clouds when first He brings them into being, while they are still thin. This is the *izjaa'* (gentle driving). ﴿Then He joins them together﴾, that is, He gathers them after they have been scattered. ﴿Then He makes them heaped up﴾, that is, piled upon one another, so that some of them are layered over others. ﴿Then you see the rain﴾, that is, the rainfall, ﴿coming out from their midst﴾, that is, from their inside. Ibn 'Abbas and al-Dahhak also read it as ﴿wa-kadha﴾ [[In manuscripts F and A: "wa-kadhalika".]].

'Ubayd ibn 'Umayr al-Laythi said: Allah sends the *mu'thirah* (the wind that stirs up the dust), so it sweeps the earth clean. Then Allah sends the *nashi'ah* (the wind that brings the clouds into being), so it creates the clouds. Then Allah sends the *mu'allifah* (the wind that joins the clouds), so it gathers them together. Then Allah sends [Allah] [[Addition from F.]] the *lawaqih* (the fertilising winds), so they impregnate the clouds. Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Jarir, may Allah have mercy on them both.

* *

As for His saying ﴿And He sends down from the sky mountains containing hail﴾: some grammarians said: the first *min* (من) is for *ibtida' al-ghayah* (the starting point of a limit), the second is for *al-tab'id* (partitive), and the third is for *bayan al-jins* (specifying the kind). This only fits the view of those exegetes who held that ﴿from mountains containing hail﴾ means that there are mountains of hail in the sky from which Allah sends down the hail. As for those who took "the mountains" here to be a metaphor [[In manuscripts F and A: "kinaya".]] for the clouds, the second *min* is also for *ibtida' al-ghayah*, but it is then a substitute (*badal*) for the first. And Allah knows best.

* *

As for His saying ﴿He strikes with it whom He wills and averts it from whom He wills﴾: it may mean by ﴿He strikes with it﴾, with what descends from the sky of the two kinds, hail and rain. Then ﴿He strikes with it whom He wills﴾ is a mercy to them, and ﴿and averts it from whom He wills﴾ means He withholds the rain from them.

It may also mean by ﴿He strikes with it﴾, with the hail, as a punishment upon whom He wills, because of what it does to their fruits, the destruction of their crops and their trees. And ﴿He averts it from whom He wills﴾ is a mercy to them.

* *

As for His saying ﴿The brightness of its lightning nearly takes away the sight﴾: that is, the light of its flash is so intense that it nearly snatches away the eyes when they follow it and look at it.

* *

As for His saying ﴿Allah turns the night and the day﴾: that is, He governs them. He takes from the length of this to add to the shortness of that, until they are equal, then He takes from this and gives to that, so what was short grows long and what was long grows short. Allah is the One who directs this by His command, His power, His might and His knowledge.

﴿Indeed in that is a lesson for those who have sight﴾: that is, it is indeed a proof of His great majesty, exalted is He, as Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed in the creation of the heavens and the earth, and the alternation of the night and the day, are signs for people of understanding﴾ [Al 'Imran: 190]. And what follows it of the noble verses.

And what follows it of the noble verses.

It mentions His complete power and great dominion in His creation of the various kinds of creatures [[added from manuscripts F and A]], with their differing forms, colours, movements and stillness, all from one water. ﴿Among them is one that walks on its belly﴾, like the snake and what resembles it; ﴿and among them is one that walks on two legs﴾, like man and birds; ﴿and among them is one that walks on four﴾, like livestock and all other animals. For this reason He said: ﴿God creates what He wills﴾, meaning by His power, for whatever He wills comes to be, and whatever He does not will does not come to be. For this reason He said: ﴿Indeed, God is over all things competent﴾.

He, may He be exalted, affirms that He sent down in this Qur'an clear, firm wisdoms and parables, very many [[In H: "wisdoms, judgments and parables". The wording from F and A is adopted.]] [[In F: "firm, of which there are many".]], and that it guides to understanding and comprehending them the people of intellect, insight and sound judgment. For this reason He said: ﴿And Allah guides whomever He wills to a straight path.﴾

Allah the Exalted informs us about the attributes of the hypocrites, who display the opposite of what they conceal. They say with their tongues: ﴿We believe in Allah and in the Messenger, and we obey,﴾ then ﴿a faction of them turns away after that.﴾ That is, they contradict their words with their deeds, saying what they do not do. Therefore Allah the Exalted said: ﴿And those are not believers.﴾

* *

His saying: ﴿And when they are called to Allah and His Messenger, that he may judge between them, behold, a faction of them turn away.﴾ That is, when they are asked to follow the guidance revealed by Allah to His Messenger, they turn away from it and are arrogant within themselves toward following it. A similar statement is His saying: ﴿Have you not seen those who claim that they believe in what has been revealed to you and what was revealed before you, yet they desire to seek judgment from the Taghut [false deities/tyrants], although they were commanded to reject it? And Shaytan wants to lead them far astray. And when it is said to them, "Come to what Allah has revealed and to the Messenger," you see the hypocrites turn away from you with aversion.﴾ [An-Nisa: 60–61]

In al-Tabarani, from the hadith (a reported saying or action of the Prophet) of Rawh ibn 'Ata ibn Abi Maymunah, from his father, from al-Hasan, from Samurah, raised to the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "Whoever is called to a ruler and does not respond, he is a wrongdoer with no right."
[Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir of al-Tabarani (7/225). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (4/198): "In it is Rawh ibn 'Ata. Ibn 'Adi declared him trustworthy, but the imams considered him weak."]

* *

His saying: ﴿But if the right is theirs, they come to him willingly.﴾ That is, when the judgment is in their favour and not against them, they come listening and obeying. This is the meaning of His saying ﴿willingly.﴾ But when the judgment goes against them, they turn away, call to other than the truth, and prefer to seek judgment from someone other than the Prophet (ﷺ) so as to promote their falsehood. Their compliance at first was not from a belief that this was the truth, but because it matched their desires. Therefore, when the truth opposed their aim, they turned away from it to something else. Hence Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Is there in their hearts a disease, or have they doubted, or do they fear that Allah and His Messenger will wrong them?﴾ That is: their situation is nothing other than a disease that is firmly settled in their hearts, or doubt about the religion has afflicted them, or they fear that Allah and His Messenger will act unjustly toward them in judgment. Whichever of these it is, it is pure disbelief, and Allah is Knowing of each of them and of what they harbour of these attributes.

* *

His saying: ﴿Rather, it is they who are the wrongdoers.﴾ That is: rather, they are the wrongdoers and the wicked, while Allah and His Messenger are free of what they suspect and imagine of injustice and oppression. Exalted is Allah and His Messenger above that.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Musa ibn Isma'il narrated to us, Mubarak narrated to us, al-Hasan narrated to us, saying: A man, if he had a dispute with another man and was called to the Prophet (ﷺ) while he was in the right, he would comply, knowing that the Prophet (ﷺ) would decide the matter in his favour with the truth. But if he wanted to wrong someone and was called to the Prophet (ﷺ), he would turn away and say: "I will go to so-and-so." So Allah revealed this verse, and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Whoever has a matter between himself and his brother, and he is called to a judge from among the judges of the Muslims but refuses to respond, he is a wrongdoer with no right."
[Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated it from al-Hasan as a mursal report (a report whose chain omits a companion), as in al-Durr al-Manthur (6/213).]

This is a gharib (unusual) hadith, and it is mursal.

Then Allah the Exalted informed about the attribute of the believers who respond to Allah and His Messenger, those who do not seek any religion other than the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Messenger. He said: ﴿The only statement of the believers when they are called to Allah and His Messenger, that he may judge between them, is that they say, "We hear and we obey."﴾ That is: hearing and obeying. Therefore Allah described them with success, which is attaining what is sought and being safe from what is feared. He said: ﴿And those are the successful.﴾

Qatadah said regarding this verse, ﴿that they say, "We hear and we obey,"﴾: It was related to us that 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit, who was one of the 'Aqabah and Badr participants and one of the chiefs (nuqaba') of the Ansar, when death approached him, said to his nephew Junadah ibn Abi Umayyah: "Shall I inform you of what is incumbent upon you and what is due to you?" He said: "Yes." He said: "Upon you is hearing and obeying, in your hardship and your ease, in what you like and what you dislike, and even if you are given less favour than others. And upon you is to uphold justice with your tongue, and not to dispute the affair with its people, unless they command you to disobey Allah openly. If you are commanded to do something that contradicts the Book of Allah, then follow the Book of Allah."

Qatadah also said: It was related to us that Abu al-Darda' said: "There is no Islam except with obedience to Allah, no good except in the community, and sincere counsel is due to Allah, to His Messenger, to the caliph, and to the Muslims in general."

He said: It was related to us that 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (may Allah be pleased with him) used to say: "The pillar of Islam is the testimony that there is no god but Allah, establishing the prayer, paying the zakat, and obedience to the one whom Allah has placed in charge of the affairs of the Muslims."

Ibn Abi Hatim narrated this. The hadiths and reports concerning the obligation of obedience to the Book of Allah [and the Sunnah of His Messenger, and to the rightly guided caliphs and the imams when they command obedience to Allah] are very numerous, far too many to be contained in this place.
[Addition from the manuscripts F and A.]

* *

His saying: ﴿And whoever obeys Allah and His Messenger﴾ That is: in what they have commanded him and in abandoning what they have forbidden him, ﴿and fears Allah﴾ regarding the sins he has committed in the past, ﴿and is mindful of Him﴾ regarding what he will face in the future.

* *

His saying: ﴿Those are the attainers of success.﴾ That is: those who have attained every good and been safe from every evil in this world and the Hereafter.
