Ibn Kathir's commentary on Surah 24, verses 53–54:

He, the Exalted, says, reporting about the hypocrites, who used to swear oaths to the Messenger ﷺ that, "If he (ﷺ) ordered them to go out (in the ghazw, the military expedition)," Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Say: Do not swear oaths﴾, meaning: do not swear.

* *

His saying: ﴿reasonable obedience (ta'atun ma'ruf)﴾. It has been said that its meaning (its taqdir, its implied sense) is: "Your obedience is a known obedience," meaning: your obedience is already known; it is merely words with no action accompanying them, and whenever you swear, you lie. As Allah the Exalted says: ﴿They swear to you in order that you may be pleased with them. But if you are pleased with them, indeed Allah is not pleased with the defiantly disobedient people﴾ [At-Tawbah: 96]. And He, the Exalted, says: ﴿They have taken their oaths as a shield, and they averted (others) from the way of Allah. Indeed, evil is what they used to do﴾ [Al-Munafiqun: 2]. Lying is part of their nature, even regarding what they choose, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Have you not seen those who practised hypocrisy say to their brothers who disbelieved among the People of the Scripture: "If you are expelled, we will surely leave with you, and we will never obey anyone against you, and if you are fought, we will surely support you." And Allah testifies that they are liars. If they are expelled, they will not leave with them; and if they are fought, they will not support them; and if they support them, they will surely turn their backs; then they will not be helped﴾ [Al-Hashr: 11–12].

It has also been said that the meaning of His saying ﴿reasonable obedience﴾ is: let your matter be a reasonable obedience, meaning: with what is reasonable, without swearing or taking oaths, just as the believers obey Allah and His Messenger without swearing. So be like them.

﴿Indeed, Allah is Well-Acquainted with what you do﴾, meaning: He is Well-Acquainted with you and with who obeys among those who disobey. So swearing and displaying obedience, while the inner state is contrary to it, even if it deceives the created being (the one sworn to), the Creator, the Exalted, knows what is secret and what is more hidden. Nothing of deception passes over Him; rather, He is Well-Acquainted with the inner thoughts of His servants, even if they display something contrary to them.

Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Say: Obey Allah and obey the Messenger﴾, meaning: follow the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Messenger.

* *

His saying: ﴿But if you turn away﴾, meaning: if you turn away from him and abandon what has come to you with it, ﴿then upon him is only that with which he has been entrusted﴾, meaning: conveying the message and discharging the trust; ﴿and upon you is only that with which you have been entrusted﴾, meaning: from that, and honouring it and acting upon its requirements; ﴿and if you obey him, you will be guided﴾. That is because he calls to a straight path ﴿the path of Allah, to whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. Unquestionably, to Allah do all matters return﴾ [Ash-Shura: 53].

* *

His saying: ﴿And upon the Messenger is only the clear conveyance﴾ is like His saying: ﴿Upon you is only the conveyance, and upon Us is the account﴾ [Ar-Ra'd: 40], and His saying: ﴿So remind; you are only a reminder. You are not over them a controller﴾ [Al-Ghashiyah: 21–22].

Wahb ibn Munabbih said: Allah revealed to one of the prophets of the Children of Israel, who was called Sha'ya': "Stand among the Children of Israel, for I will loose your tongue with revelation." So he stood and said: "O heaven, listen! O earth, be silent! For indeed Allah intends to decree a matter and arrange an affair which He will carry out. He intends to turn the settled land into desert, the thickets into the fields, the rivers into the deserts, and blessing into the poor, and kingship into the shepherds. He intends to send forth an unlettered one from among the unlettered, neither harsh nor coarse, nor clamorous in the markets. If he were to pass by the side of a lamp, he would not extinguish it with his calm; and if he were to walk on dry reeds, their sound would not be heard beneath his feet. I will send him as a bringer of good tidings and a warner, who does not utter obscenity. Through him I will open blind eyes, deaf ears and veiled hearts. I will guide him to every good matter, and I will bestow upon him every noble character. I will make tranquility his garment, righteousness his emblem, piety his inner nature, wisdom his speech, truthfulness and fidelity his disposition, forgiveness and kindness his character, truth his law, justice his way, guidance his leader, Islam his religion, and Ahmad his name. Through him I will guide after misguidance, teach after ignorance, raise up after lowliness, make known after obscurity, multiply after scarcity, enrich after poverty, unite after division, and join together nations scattered, hearts divided, and desires dispersed. Through him I will rescue a multitude of people from great destruction, and I will make his community the best community brought forth for mankind, enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong, monotheists, believers, sincere, affirming what My messengers have brought." Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim.[[Also narrated from Abdullah ibn Salam and Ka'b al-Ahbar, as in al-Shifa of al-Qadi Iyad (1/15).]]

Ibn Kathir's commentary on Surah 24, verses 53–54:

He, the Exalted, says, reporting about the hypocrites, who used to swear oaths to the Messenger ﷺ that, "If he (ﷺ) ordered them to go out (in the ghazw, the military expedition)," Allah the Exalted said: ﴿Say: Do not swear oaths﴾, meaning: do not swear.

* *

His saying: ﴿reasonable obedience (ta'atun ma'ruf)﴾. It has been said that its meaning (its taqdir, its implied sense) is: "Your obedience is a known obedience," meaning: your obedience is already known; it is merely words with no action accompanying them, and whenever you swear, you lie. As Allah the Exalted says: ﴿They swear to you in order that you may be pleased with them. But if you are pleased with them, indeed Allah is not pleased with the defiantly disobedient people﴾ [At-Tawbah: 96]. And He, the Exalted, says: ﴿They have taken their oaths as a shield, and they averted (others) from the way of Allah. Indeed, evil is what they used to do﴾ [Al-Munafiqun: 2]. Lying is part of their nature, even regarding what they choose, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿Have you not seen those who practised hypocrisy say to their brothers who disbelieved among the People of the Scripture: "If you are expelled, we will surely leave with you, and we will never obey anyone against you, and if you are fought, we will surely support you." And Allah testifies that they are liars. If they are expelled, they will not leave with them; and if they are fought, they will not support them; and if they support them, they will surely turn their backs; then they will not be helped﴾ [Al-Hashr: 11–12].

It has also been said that the meaning of His saying ﴿reasonable obedience﴾ is: let your matter be a reasonable obedience, meaning: with what is reasonable, without swearing or taking oaths, just as the believers obey Allah and His Messenger without swearing. So be like them.

﴿Indeed, Allah is Well-Acquainted with what you do﴾, meaning: He is Well-Acquainted with you and with who obeys among those who disobey. So swearing and displaying obedience, while the inner state is contrary to it, even if it deceives the created being (the one sworn to), the Creator, the Exalted, knows what is secret and what is more hidden. Nothing of deception passes over Him; rather, He is Well-Acquainted with the inner thoughts of His servants, even if they display something contrary to them.

Then He, the Exalted, said: ﴿Say: Obey Allah and obey the Messenger﴾, meaning: follow the Book of Allah and the Sunnah of His Messenger.

* *

His saying: ﴿But if you turn away﴾, meaning: if you turn away from him and abandon what has come to you with it, ﴿then upon him is only that with which he has been entrusted﴾, meaning: conveying the message and discharging the trust; ﴿and upon you is only that with which you have been entrusted﴾, meaning: from that, and honouring it and acting upon its requirements; ﴿and if you obey him, you will be guided﴾. That is because he calls to a straight path ﴿the path of Allah, to whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth. Unquestionably, to Allah do all matters return﴾ [Ash-Shura: 53].

* *

His saying: ﴿And upon the Messenger is only the clear conveyance﴾ is like His saying: ﴿Upon you is only the conveyance, and upon Us is the account﴾ [Ar-Ra'd: 40], and His saying: ﴿So remind; you are only a reminder. You are not over them a controller﴾ [Al-Ghashiyah: 21–22].

Wahb ibn Munabbih said: Allah revealed to one of the prophets of the Children of Israel, who was called Sha'ya': "Stand among the Children of Israel, for I will loose your tongue with revelation." So he stood and said: "O heaven, listen! O earth, be silent! For indeed Allah intends to decree a matter and arrange an affair which He will carry out. He intends to turn the settled land into desert, the thickets into the fields, the rivers into the deserts, and blessing into the poor, and kingship into the shepherds. He intends to send forth an unlettered one from among the unlettered, neither harsh nor coarse, nor clamorous in the markets. If he were to pass by the side of a lamp, he would not extinguish it with his calm; and if he were to walk on dry reeds, their sound would not be heard beneath his feet. I will send him as a bringer of good tidings and a warner, who does not utter obscenity. Through him I will open blind eyes, deaf ears and veiled hearts. I will guide him to every good matter, and I will bestow upon him every noble character. I will make tranquility his garment, righteousness his emblem, piety his inner nature, wisdom his speech, truthfulness and fidelity his disposition, forgiveness and kindness his character, truth his law, justice his way, guidance his leader, Islam his religion, and Ahmad his name. Through him I will guide after misguidance, teach after ignorance, raise up after lowliness, make known after obscurity, multiply after scarcity, enrich after poverty, unite after division, and join together nations scattered, hearts divided, and desires dispersed. Through him I will rescue a multitude of people from great destruction, and I will make his community the best community brought forth for mankind, enjoining what is right and forbidding what is wrong, monotheists, believers, sincere, affirming what My messengers have brought." Narrated by Ibn Abi Hatim.[[Also narrated from Abdullah ibn Salam and Ka'b al-Ahbar, as in al-Shifa of al-Qadi Iyad (1/15).]]

This is a promise from Allah to His Messenger (ﷺ) that He will make his ummah the khulafa' al-ard (successors on the earth), meaning the leaders of the people and their rulers. Through them the lands are set right and the servants submit to them. He will replace their fear of the people with security and authority over them. Allah, blessed and exalted is He, has done this, and to Him belong praise and favour. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) did not die until Allah had granted him Makkah, Khaybar, Bahrain, all of the Arabian Peninsula and the whole land of Yemen. He took the jizyah (poll tax) from the Magians of Hajar and from some border areas of al-Sham. Heraclius, king of the Romans, sent him gifts, as did the ruler of Egypt and Alexandria, who was al-Muqawqis, and the kings of Oman, and al-Najashi, king of Abyssinia, who ruled after Ashamah, may Allah have mercy on him and honour him.

Then, when the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) died and Allah chose for him what He had of honour, his successor Abu Bakr al-Siddiq took up the affair after him. He gathered together what had been weakened at his death, (peace be upon him), and firmly established and levelled the Arabian Peninsula. He sent the Islamic armies to the land of Persia in the company of Khalid ibn al-Walid, may Allah be pleased with him, and they conquered part of it and killed a multitude of its people. He sent another army in the company of Abu Ubaydah, may Allah be pleased with him, and the commanders with him, to the land of al-Sham. A third army went in the company of Amr ibn al-As, may Allah be pleased with him, to the land of Egypt. In his days Allah granted the Syrian army Busra, Damascus and their dependencies from the lands of Hawran and what lay around them. Then Allah, mighty and majestic, took him, and chose for him what He had of honour. He bestowed favour upon Islam and its people by inspiring al-Siddiq to appoint Umar al-Faruq as successor. Umar took up the affair after him with a complete standing, and after the prophets (peace be upon them) the sphere has not turned upon the likes of him in the strength of his conduct and the perfection of his justice. In his days the conquest of the Syrian lands was completed in full, and of the lands of Egypt to their end, and most of the province of Persia. He broke Kisra and humiliated him to the utmost degree, and he (Kisra) retreated to the farthest part of his kingdom. He subdued Caesar and wrested his hand away from the lands of al-Sham, so that he withdrew to Constantinople. The wealth of these lands was spent in the way of Allah, as the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) had reported and promised, upon him be from his Lord the most complete peace and the purest blessing.

Then, when the Ottoman state arose, the Islamic realms extended to the farthest east and west of the earth. The lands of the Maghrib were conquered to their farthest extent: al-Andalus, Cyprus, the lands of al-Qayrawan, and the lands of Ceuta bordering the Atlantic Ocean. From the east they reached the farthest lands of China. Kisra was killed and his kingdom was utterly destroyed. The cities of Iraq, Khurasan and al-Ahwaz were conquered. The Muslims slew a very great number of the Turks, and Allah humiliated their supreme king, Khaqan. Taxes (kharaj) were collected from east and west and brought to the presence of the Commander of the Faithful, Uthman ibn Affan, may Allah be pleased with him. This was by the blessing of his recitation, his study of the Qur'an and his uniting of the ummah upon the memorising of the Qur'an. For this reason it is established in the Sahih, from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), that he said: "Allah gathered the earth for me, and I saw its eastern and western parts, and the dominion of my ummah will reach what was gathered for me of it." So here we are, moving within what Allah and His Messenger promised us, and Allah and His Messenger spoke the truth. So we ask Allah for faith in Him and in His Messenger, and for standing in gratitude to Him in the manner that pleases Him with regard to us.

Imam Muslim ibn al-Hajjaj said: Ibn Abi Umar narrated to us, Sufyan narrated to us, from Abd al-Malik ibn Umayr, from Jabir ibn Samurah, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say: "The affair of the people will continue to be upright as long as twelve men govern them." Then the Prophet (ﷺ) said a word which was hidden from me, so I asked my father: "What did the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) say?" He said: "All of them are from Quraysh."

Al-Bukhari also narrated it from the hadith of Shu'bah, from Abd al-Malik ibn Umayr, with the same wording.

In a narration of Muslim, he said this on the evening when Ma'iz ibn Malik was stoned, and he mentioned other hadiths along with it.

This hadith indicates that there must be twelve just caliphs. They are not the Twelve Imams of the Shi'ah, for most of those had no authority at all. Rather, these are from Quraysh, who will rule and act justly. Good tidings of them occurred in the earlier scriptures. Furthermore, it is not required that they be consecutive; rather their existence in the ummah may be consecutive or scattered. Four of them came in succession: Abu Bakr, then Umar, then Uthman, then Ali, may Allah be pleased with them all. After them there was a interval, then some of them appeared as Allah willed, and then there may appear among them those who remain at a time known to Allah. Among them is the Mahdi, whose name matches the name of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and whose kunyah matches his kunyah. He will fill the earth with justice and equity, just as it was filled with tyranny and oppression.

Ahmad, Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i have also narrated, from the hadith of Sa'id ibn Jumhan, from Safinah, the freed slave of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The caliphate after me will be thirty years, then it will become a biting kingship."

Al-Rabi' ibn Anas narrated, from Abu al-Aliyah, concerning His saying: ﴿Allah has promised those among you who believe and do righteous deeds that He will surely grant them succession upon the earth, as He granted succession to those before them, and that He will surely establish for them their religion which He has approved for them, and that He will surely replace their fear with security﴾, and so on. He said: The Prophet (ﷺ) and his companions remained in Makkah for about ten years, calling to Allah alone and to the worship of Him alone, with no partner, secretly, while they were in fear, and they were not commanded to fight. Then they were commanded to emigrate to Madinah. They came to Madinah, and Allah commanded them to fight. They were there in fear, going to sleep and waking up with weapons, and by that state Allah changed what He willed. Then a man from among the companions said: "O Messenger of Allah, will we be in this state of fear forever? Will there not come a day when we are secure and lay down our weapons?" The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "You will not wait long before a man among you sits in a great gathering, reclining, with no weapon among them." Then Allah revealed this verse, and Allah made His Prophet victorious over the Arabian Peninsula, so they became secure and laid down their weapons. Then Allah, mighty and majestic, took His Prophet (ﷺ), and they remained in security during the rule of Abu Bakr, Umar and Uthman, until they fell into what they fell into. Then Allah brought fear upon them, so they took guards and police and changed, and therefore things changed for them.

Some of the early scholars said: The caliphate of Abu Bakr and Umar, may Allah be pleased with them both, is true in His Book, then he recited this verse.

Al-Bara' ibn Azib said: This verse was revealed while we were in great fear.

This noble verse is like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And remember when you were few and oppressed in the land, fearing that people would snatch you away, but He sheltered you and strengthened you with His help and provided you with good things, so that you might be grateful﴾ [Al-Anfal: 26].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿as He granted succession to those before them﴾, this is like what Allah, exalted is He, said about Musa, peace be upon him, when he said to his people: ﴿It may be that your Lord will destroy your enemy and make you successors in the land, and then He will see how you act﴾ [Al-A'raf: 129]. And He, exalted is He, said: ﴿And We wished to bestow favour upon those who were oppressed in the land, and to make them leaders and make them the inheritors, and to establish them in the land, and to show Pharaoh and Haman and their hosts from them what they feared﴾ [Al-Qasas: 5-6].

* *

As for His saying: ﴿and that He will surely establish for them their religion which He has approved for them, and that He will surely replace their fear with security﴾, this is like what the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to Adi ibn Hatim when he came to him as a delegation: "Do you know al-Hirah?" He said: I have not seen it, but I have heard of it. He said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, Allah will surely complete this affair until a woman rides out from al-Hirah and circles the House without anyone's protection, and you will surely conquer the treasures of Kisra ibn Hurmuz." I said: "Kisra ibn Hurmuz?" He said: "Yes, Kisra ibn Hurmuz, and wealth will be spent until no one accepts it." Adi ibn Hatim said: So this woman does indeed ride out from al-Hirah and circles the House without anyone's protection. And by Him in whose hand is my soul, I was among those who conquered the treasures of Kisra ibn Hurmuz. By Him in whose hand is my soul, the third (promise) will surely come to pass, for the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) has said it.

[Narrated by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. 3595.]

Al-Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Sufyan informed us, from Abu Salamah, from al-Rabi' ibn Anas, from Abu al-Aliyah, from Ubayy ibn Ka'b, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Give good news to this ummah of elevated status and eminence, of religion and victory, and of establishment in the land. But whoever among them does the deeds of the Hereafter for the sake of the worldly life will have no share in the Hereafter."

[Al-Musnad 5/134.]

* *

As for His saying: ﴿They worship Me and do not associate anything with Me﴾, Imam Ahmad said:

Affan narrated to us, Hammam narrated to us, Qatadah narrated to us, from Anas, that Mu'adh ibn Jabal narrated to him, saying: While I was riding behind the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), with nothing between me and him but the back of the saddle, he said: "O Mu'adh." I said: "At your service, O Messenger of Allah, and at your command." He walked for a while, then said: "O Mu'adh ibn Jabal." I said: "At your service, O Messenger of Allah, and at your command." [He walked for a while, then said: "O Mu'adh ibn Jabal," and I said: "At your service, O Messenger of Allah, and at your command."] He said: "Do you know what is Allah's right over the servants?" I said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "Allah's right over the servants is that they worship Him and do not associate anything with Him." He said: Then he walked for a while, then said: "O Mu'adh ibn Jabal." I said: "At your service, O Messenger of Allah, and at your command." He said: "Do you know what is the servants' right over Allah if they do that?" I said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "The servants' right over Allah is that He will not punish them."

They both narrated it in the Sahihayn (the two Sahihs of al-Bukhari and Muslim) from the hadith of Qatadah. [[Al-Musnad (5/242), Sahih al-Bukhari no. (5967), and Sahih Muslim no. (30).]]
* *
And His saying: ﴿And whoever disbelieves after that, then those are the defiantly disobedient.﴾ That is: whoever departs from My obedience after that has transgressed against the command of his Lord, and that alone is a grave sin. The Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, were the most upright of people after the Prophet ﷺ in carrying out the commands of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and the most obedient of them to Allah. Their victory was in proportion to them, and they made the word of Allah manifest in the East and the West, Allah strengthened them with a great strengthening, and they held authority over all the servants and lands. When people after them fell short in some of the commands, their dominance diminished in proportion to that. However, it is established in the Sahihayn, through more than one chain, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ that he said: "A group from my Ummah will continue to be victorious upon the truth; those who forsake them will not harm them, nor will those who oppose them, until the Day of Resurrection." In another narration: "Until the Command of Allah comes, while they remain as such." In another narration: "Until they fight the Dajjal (the Antichrist)." In another narration: "Until Eesa ibn Maryam (Jesus, son of Mary) descends while they are victorious." All of these narrations are authentic, and there is no contradiction between them.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 24, verse 56–57:

Allah, exalted is He, says, commanding His believing servants to establish the prayer (salah), which is worship of Allah alone with no partner, and to give the zakah (obligatory charity), which is kindness to the creation, to their weak and their poor. [They are to do this] while being obedient to the Messenger, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him, meaning: following him in what he has commanded them and abstaining from what he has forbidden them, so that perhaps Allah will show them mercy because of that. There is no doubt that whoever does that, Allah will surely show them mercy, as He said in another verse: ﴿Those – Allah will surely have mercy on them﴾ [At-Tawbah: 71].

And His saying ﴿Do not think﴾, meaning: [do not suppose], O Muhammad, ﴿that those who disbelieved﴾, meaning: those who opposed you and denied you, ﴿will cause failure [to Allah] upon the earth﴾, meaning: they cannot escape Allah; rather Allah is capable over them, and He will punish them for that with the severest punishment. Therefore He said: ﴿And their refuge is the Fire, and wretched is the destination﴾, meaning: in the Hereafter, ﴿wretched is the destination of the disbelievers, and wretched is the resting place and wretched is the bed.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 24, verse 56–57:

Allah, exalted is He, says, commanding His believing servants to establish the prayer (salah), which is worship of Allah alone with no partner, and to give the zakah (obligatory charity), which is kindness to the creation, to their weak and their poor. [They are to do this] while being obedient to the Messenger, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him, meaning: following him in what he has commanded them and abstaining from what he has forbidden them, so that perhaps Allah will show them mercy because of that. There is no doubt that whoever does that, Allah will surely show them mercy, as He said in another verse: ﴿Those – Allah will surely have mercy on them﴾ [At-Tawbah: 71].

And His saying ﴿Do not think﴾, meaning: [do not suppose], O Muhammad, ﴿that those who disbelieved﴾, meaning: those who opposed you and denied you, ﴿will cause failure [to Allah] upon the earth﴾, meaning: they cannot escape Allah; rather Allah is capable over them, and He will punish them for that with the severest punishment. Therefore He said: ﴿And their refuge is the Fire, and wretched is the destination﴾, meaning: in the Hereafter, ﴿wretched is the destination of the disbelievers, and wretched is the resting place and wretched is the bed.

These noble verses concern the seeking of permission (isti'dhan) by relatives from one another. What came earlier at the beginning of the surah concerns the seeking of permission by strangers from one another. Allah commanded the believers that their slaves (khadam), those whom their right hands possess, and their children who have not reached puberty (al-hulum) should seek permission from them at three times. The first is before the dawn prayer (salat al-ghadah), because people are then asleep on their beds. ﴿And when you put off your clothing at midday﴾, that is, at the time of the afternoon rest (al-qaylulah), because a person may take off his clothes at that time with his family. ﴿And after the prayer of 'Isha'﴾, because it is the time of sleep. Servants and children are therefore commanded not to enter upon the household at these times, lest the man be with his wife or engaged in similar activities. For this reason He said: ﴿Three times of privacy (awrat) for you. Neither upon you nor upon them is there any blame beyond these﴾, that is, if they enter at a time other than these times, there is no blame upon you for allowing them to do so, nor upon them if they see something at other than those times, because they have been permitted to enter, and because they are ﴿constant attendants (tawwafun)﴾ upon you, that is, in service and otherwise. Allowances are made for constant attendants that are not made for others. For this reason Imam Malik, Ahmad ibn Hanbal and the authors of the Sunan narrated that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said concerning the cat: "It is not impure; it is among the constant attendants upon you, or the constant attendants [of you]"[[al-Muwatta' (1/23), al-Musnad (5/296), Sunan Abi Dawud no. (75), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (92), Sunan al-Nasa'i (1/55), Sunan Ibn Majah no. (367).]].

Since this verse is muhkam (clear and definitive, not abrogated) and has not been abrogated (naskh) by anything, and since people's practice of it has been very little, Ibn 'Abbas denounced this among the people, as Ibn Abi Hatim narrated:

Abu Zur'ah narrated to us, Yahya ibn 'Abd Allah ibn Bukayr narrated to us, 'Abd Allah ibn Lahi'ah narrated to me, 'Ata' ibn Dinar narrated to me, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, who said: Ibn 'Abbas said: "The people have abandoned three verses and have not acted upon them: ﴿O you who have believed, let those whom your right hands possess and those who have not reached puberty among you seek permission of you three times﴾" [[An addition from F and A.]] up to the end of the verse; and the verse in Surat al-Nisa': ﴿And when the division [of inheritance] is attended by relatives and orphans and the needy, then provide for them from it﴾ [al-Nisa': 8]; and the verse in al-Hujurat: ﴿Indeed, the most noble of you in the sight of Allah is the most righteous of you﴾ [al-Hujurat: 13].

It is also narrated from the hadith of Isma'il ibn Muslim, who is weak, from 'Amr ibn Dinar, from 'Ata' ibn Abi Rabah, from Ibn 'Abbas, who said: "Satan overcame the people with three verses, so they did not act upon them: ﴿O you who have believed, let those whom your right hands possess seek permission of you﴾" up to the end of the verse.

Abu Dawud said: Ibn al-Sabbah ibn Sufyan and Ibn 'Abdah narrated to us—and this is his hadith—Sufyan informed us, from 'Ubayd Allah ibn Abi Yazid, who heard Ibn 'Abbas say: "Most of the people do not believe in it—the verse of permission—and indeed I command my slave-girl to seek permission to enter upon me."

Abu Dawud said: Likewise 'Ata' narrated it from Ibn 'Abbas, commanding it.[[Sunan Abi Dawud no. (5191).]]

al-Thawri said, from Musa ibn Abi 'A'ishah: I asked al-Sha'bi about ﴿Let those whom your right hands possess seek permission of you﴾. He said: "It has not been abrogated." I said: "But people do not act upon it." He said: "Allah is the One sought for help."

Ibn Abi Hatim said: al-Rabi' ibn Sulayman narrated to us, Ibn Wahb narrated to us, Sulayman ibn Bilal informed us, from 'Amr ibn Abi 'Amr, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas: that two men asked him about seeking permission at the three times of privacy which Allah mentioned in the Qur'an. Ibn 'Abbas said: "Indeed Allah is Concealing and loves concealment. The people had no curtains on their doors and no partitions in their houses, so a man might suddenly be surprised by his servant, his son, or his orphan in his charge while he was with his wife. So Allah commanded them to seek permission at those times of privacy that Allah named. Then later Allah brought curtains [[In F: 'afterwards with the curtains'; in A: 'afterwards the curtain'.]], and He expanded provision upon them, so they took curtains and partitions. The people saw that this had sufficed them from the permission they had been commanded to seek."

This is a sahih chain (isnad) to Ibn 'Abbas. Abu Dawud narrated it from al-Qa'nabi, from al-Darawardi, from 'Amr ibn Abi 'Amr with the same.[[Sunan Abi Dawud no. (5192).]]

al-Suddi said: Some of the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them, used to wish to have intercourse with their wives at these times, then perform ghusl and go out to prayer. So Allah commanded them to instruct the male slaves and the boys not to enter upon them at those times without permission.

Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: It reached us—and Allah knows best—that a man from the Ansar and his wife Asma' bint Murshidah prepared food for the Prophet (ﷺ), and people kept entering without permission. Asma' said: "O Messenger of Allah, how ugly this is! Indeed a servant enters upon a woman and her husband while they are in one garment, without permission!" So Allah revealed concerning that: ﴿O you who have believed, let those whom your right hands possess and those of you who have not reached puberty seek permission of you three times﴾ [[An addition from A.]], the verse.

Among what indicates that it is muhkam and has not been abrogated is His saying: ﴿Thus does Allah make clear to you the verses, and Allah is Knowing and Wise﴾.

Then He said: ﴿And when the children among you reach puberty, let them seek permission as those before them sought permission﴾. That is: when the children who used to seek permission at the three times of privacy reach puberty, it becomes obligatory upon them to seek permission in every circumstance, that is, in relation to those who are not of their household and in relation to the situations in which a man is with his wife, even if they are not at the three times.

al-Awza'i said, from Yahya ibn Abi Kathir: When a boy reaches the age of about ten (rabā'iyy), he seeks permission at the three times of privacy from his parents; when he reaches puberty, he must seek permission in every circumstance. Sa'id ibn Jubayr said the same.

Concerning His saying ﴿as those before them sought permission﴾, he said: that is, as the adults among a man's children and relatives sought permission.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 24, verse 61:

The scholars of tafsir, may God have mercy on them, differed concerning the reason for which the removal of blame from the blind, the lame and the sick is mentioned here. 'Ata' al-Khurasani and 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: it was revealed concerning jihad.

They took this verse here to be like the one in Surah al-Fath [[At verse 17.]], and that one is certainly about jihad, meaning: there is no sin upon them for not going out to jihad, because of their weakness and incapacity. As God the Exalted says in Surah al-Tawbah: ﴿There is no blame upon the weak, nor upon the sick, nor upon those who find nothing to spend, when they are sincere to God and His Messenger. There is no cause [for blame] against the good-doers. And God is Forgiving and Merciful. Nor [is there blame] upon those who came to you that you might provide them with mounts, and you said, "I can find nothing to mount you on," and they turned back while their eyes overflowed with tears out of grief that they could not find anything to spend.﴾ [al-Tawbah: 91, 92]

It was also said: what is meant here [[Addition from A.]] is that they used to avoid eating with the blind, because he cannot see the food and its good things, so someone else may get to it before him. Nor with the lame, because he cannot sit comfortably, so his companion would take precedence over him. And the sick do not eat as much as others, so they disliked eating with them lest they wrong them. So God revealed this verse as a concession in that matter. This is the view of Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Miqsam.

Al-Dahhak said: before the Mission (al-mab'ath), they used to avoid eating with these people out of disgust and revulsion, and so that they would not regard themselves as superior to them. So God revealed this verse.

'Abd al-Razzaq said: Ma'mar informed us, from Ibn Abi Najih, from Mujahid, concerning His words, the Exalted: ﴿There is no blame upon the blind﴾, to the end of the verse. He said: A man would take the blind, or the lame, or the sick, to the house of his father, or the house of his brother, or the house of his sister, or the house of his paternal aunt, or the house of his maternal aunt. The disabled would feel uneasy about this, saying: "They only take us to the houses of others [[In A: "their kinsfolk".]]." So this verse was revealed as a concession for them [[Tafsir 'Abd al-Razzaq (2/53).]].

Al-Suddi said: A man would enter the house of his father, or his brother, or his son, and the woman would offer him some food, but he would not eat, because the master of the house was not there. So God the Exalted said: ﴿There is no blame upon the blind, nor upon the lame, nor upon the sick, nor upon yourselves that you eat from your houses or the houses of your fathers﴾, up to His words: ﴿There is no blame upon you that you eat together or separately﴾.

* *

As for His words: ﴿nor upon yourselves that you eat from your houses﴾, He mentioned this, though it is well known, so that others might be linked to it in wording, and so that what follows might be equal to it in ruling. This includes the houses of one's children, since they were not specifically mentioned. For this reason, those who hold that a child's property is like his father's property have taken evidence from this. It has come in the Musnad and the Sunan, through more than one route, from the Messenger of God ﷺ that he said: "You and your property belong to your father" [[Musnad (2/179), Sunan Abi Dawud no. (3530) and Sunan Ibn Majah no. (2292), from the hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn 'Amr ibn al-'As, may God be pleased with them both.]].

* *

As for His words: ﴿or the houses of your mothers﴾, up to His words ﴿or that whose keys you hold﴾, this is clear. It may be used as evidence by those who make it obligatory for relatives to support one another, as is the view of Imam Abu Hanifa and Imam Ahmad ibn Hanbal in the well-known report from them.

As for His words: ﴿or that whose keys you hold﴾, Sa'id ibn Jubayr and al-Suddi said: this refers to a man's servant, whether a slave or a steward (qahraman), so there is no harm in his eating from the food entrusted to him, in a reasonable manner.

Al-Zuhri related from 'Urwah, from 'A'isha, may God be pleased with her, who said: The Muslims used to be eager to go out to battle (al-nafir) with the Messenger of God ﷺ, and they would hand over their keys to their guardians (damana'), saying: "We have made it lawful for you to eat whatever you need." But they used to say: "It is not lawful for us to eat, for they permitted us only without the goodwill of their hearts, and we are merely trustees." So God revealed: ﴿or that whose keys you hold﴾.

* *

As for His words: ﴿or your friend﴾, meaning the houses of your friends and companions, there is no blame upon you in eating from them when you know that this does not burden them and that they do not dislike it.

Qatadah said: When you enter the house of your friend, there is no harm in your eating without his permission.

* *

As for His words: ﴿There is no blame upon you that you eat together or separately﴾, 'Ali ibn Abi Talhah related from Ibn 'Abbas concerning this verse: This was when God revealed: ﴿O you who have believed, do not consume one another's wealth unjustly﴾ [al-Nisa': 29]. The Muslims said: God has forbidden us to consume one another's wealth unjustly, and food is more valuable than wealth, so none of us may eat at the home of another. So people refrained from that, and God revealed: ﴿There is no blame upon the blind﴾ [[After it in F, A: "nor upon the lame, there is blame".]] to His words: ﴿or your friend﴾ [[Before it in F, A: "or that whose keys you hold".]]. They also used to be averse and reluctant for a man to eat food alone until someone else was with him, so God granted them leave in that, saying: ﴿There is no blame upon you that you eat together or separately﴾.

Qatadah said: This clan of Banu Kinanah, in the Jahiliyyah, considered it a disgrace for one to eat alone, to the extent that a man would drive a herd of full-uddered camels while hungry, until he found someone to eat and drink with him. So God revealed: ﴿There is no blame upon you that you eat together or separately﴾.

This is a concession from God to eat alone or in company, although eating in company is more virtuous and more blessed, as Imam Ahmad narrated: Yazid ibn 'Abd Rabbih related to us, al-Walid ibn Muslim related to us, from Wahshi ibn Harb, from his father, from his grandfather, that a man said to the Prophet ﷺ: "We eat but are not satisfied." He said: "Perhaps you eat separately; gather together over your food and mention the name of God, and He will bless it for you."

Abu Dawud and Ibn Majah also narrated it through al-Walid ibn Muslim, with the same chain [[Musnad (3/501), Sunan Abi Dawud no. (3764) and Sunan Ibn Majah no. (3286).]].

Ibn Majah also narrated, through the hadith of 'Amr ibn Dinar al-Qahramani, from Salim, from his father, from 'Umar, from the Messenger of God ﷺ, that he said: "Eat together and do not separate, for blessing is with the group." [[Sunan Ibn Majah no. (3287). al-Busiri said in al-Zawa'id (3/77): "This chain is weak."]]

* *

As for His words: ﴿So when you enter houses, greet one another﴾, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, al-Hasan al-Basri, Qatadah and al-Zuhri said: Let some of you greet others.

Ibn Jurayj said: Abu al-Zubayr related to us: I heard Jabir ibn 'Abd Allah say: When you enter upon your family, greet them with a greeting from God, blessed and good. He said: I did not see him [Jabir] regard it as anything but obligatory.

Ibn Jurayj said: Ziyad informed me, from Ibn Tawus, that he used to say: When one of you enters his house, let him greet.

Ibn Jurayj said: I asked 'Ata': Is it obligatory if I go out and then re-enter that I greet them? He said: No, and I do not report its obligation from anyone, but it is more beloved to me, and I do not leave it except when forgetful [[In F, A: "forgetting".]].

Mujahid said: When you enter the mosque, say: "Peace be upon the Messenger of God." When you enter upon your family, greet them, and when you enter a house in which there is no one, say: "Peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of God."

Al-Thawri related from 'Abd al-Karim al-Jazari, from Mujahid: When you enter a house in which there is no one, say: "In the name of God, and praise be to God, peace be upon us from our Lord, peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of God."

Qatadah said: [When you enter upon your family, greet them, and when you enter a house in which there is no one, say: "Peace be upon us and upon the righteous servants of God."] [[Addition from F, A.]] for he was commanded to do so, and we were told that the angels return his greeting. The hafiz Abu Bakr al-Bazzar said: Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna related to us, 'Awbad ibn Abi 'Imran al-Jawni related to us, from his father, from Anas, who said: The Prophet [[In F: "Messenger of God".]] ﷺ enjoined five matters upon me, saying: "O Anas, perfect your ablution and your life will be increased; greet whoever you meet from my community and your good deeds will multiply; and when you enter—meaning your house—greet the people of your house and the good of your house will increase; perform the Duha prayer, for it is the prayer of the penitent before you. O Anas, show mercy to the young, honour the elderly, and you will be among my companions on the Day of Resurrection." [[Ibn 'Adi narrated it in al-Kamil (5/382) through Musa, from 'Awbad ibn Abi 'Imran al-Jawni, with the same. He quoted from al-Bukhari: "'Awbad ibn Abi 'Imran, from his father, is munkar al-hadith," then Ibn 'Adi said: "'Awbad's narrations are weak."]]

* *

As for His words: ﴿a greeting from God, blessed and good﴾, Muhammad ibn Ishaq said: Dawud ibn al-Husayn related to me, from 'Ikrimah, from Ibn 'Abbas, that he used to say: I did not take the tashahhud except from the Book of God. I heard God say: ﴿So when you enter houses, greet one another with a greeting from God, blessed and good﴾. So the tashahhud in prayer is: "At-tahiyyatu al-mubarakatu al-salawatu al-tayyibatu lillah, ashhadu an la ilaha illa Allah, wa ashhadu anna Muhammadan 'abduhu wa rasuluh, al-salamu 'alayka ayyuha al-nabiyyu wa rahmatu Allahi wa barakatuh, al-salamu 'alayna wa 'ala 'ibad Allah al-salihin." Then he supplicates for himself and gives the greeting.

Thus Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it, through the hadith of Ibn Ishaq.

What is in Sahih Muslim, from Ibn 'Abbas, from the Messenger of God ﷺ, contradicts this [[Sahih Muslim no. (403), its wording: The Messenger of God ﷺ used to teach us the tashahhud as he taught us a surah from the Qur'an. He would say: "At-tahiyyatu al-mubarakatu al-salawatu al-tayyibatu lillah, al-salamu 'alayka ayyuha al-nabiyyu wa rahmatu Allahi wa barakatuh, al-salamu 'alayna wa 'ala 'ibad Allah al-salihin, ashhadu an la ilaha illa Allah wa anna Muhammadan rasul Allah."]], and God knows best.

* *

As for His words: ﴿Thus God makes clear to you the verses, that you may understand﴾, when He the Exalted mentioned what is in this noble surah of firm rulings, perfected laws and established decrees, He drew attention to the fact that He makes the verses clear to His servants with a complete clarification, so that they may reflect upon them and understand them.

This is also a standard of conduct to which Allah guided His believing servants. Just as He commanded them to seek permission before entering, He commanded them to seek permission before leaving, especially when they are gathered with the Messenger, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him, for a collective matter, such as the Friday prayer (*Jumu'ah*), an Eid, a congregational gathering, or a consultation and the like. Allah, exalted is He, commanded them not to depart from him in such a state except after seeking his permission and consulting him. Whoever does this is among the complete believers.

Then Allah commanded His Messenger, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him, that if any of them asks his permission in this matter, he should grant it to him if he wills. For this reason He said: ﴿So permit whom you will of them, and ask Allah's forgiveness for them. Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful.﴾

Abu Dawud said: Ahmad ibn Hanbal and Musaddad narrated to us, both saying: Bishr, that is Ibn al-Mufaddal, narrated to us, from Ajlan, from Sa'id al-Maqburi, from Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "When one of you reaches a gathering, let him greet with peace; and when he wishes to rise, let him greet with peace. The first is not more deserving than the last."

It was also narrated in this way by al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i, from the hadith of Muhammad ibn Ajlan, with the same chain. [Sunan Abi Dawud, no. (5208); Sunan al-Tirmidhi, no. (2706); and al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan al-Kubra, no. (10201).] Al-Tirmidhi said: Hasan (good).

Ibn Abbas said, as related by al-Dahhak: "They used to say, 'O Muhammad! O Abu al-Qasim!' so Allah, Mighty and Majestic, forbade them from doing that, out of reverence for His Prophet, may the blessings and peace of Allah be upon him.[[In manuscripts F and A: "may Allah bless him and grant him peace."]] They then said, 'O Messenger of Allah! O Prophet of Allah!'" Mujahid and Sa'id ibn Jubayr also said the same.

Qatadah said: "Allah commanded that His Prophet ﷺ be held in awe, honoured, exalted, and esteemed."

Muqatil [ibn Hayyan][[Addition from F and A.]] said concerning His words, ﴿Do not make the calling of the Messenger among yourselves like your calling of one another﴾: "Do not call him by name when you call him, saying, 'O Muhammad!' and do not say, 'O son of Abdullah!' Rather, honour him and say, 'O Prophet of Allah! O Messenger of Allah!'"[[In F: "O Messenger of Allah, O Prophet of Allah."]]

Malik related from Zayd ibn Aslam, concerning His words, ﴿Do not make the calling of the Messenger among yourselves like your calling of one another﴾, that he said: "Allah commanded them to honour him."

This is one view, and it is the one most apparent from the context, as Allah the Exalted says: ﴿O you who have believed, do not say, "Ra'ina," but say, "Unzurna," and listen﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 104]. And He says: ﴿O you who have believed, do not raise your voices above the voice of the Prophet or speak to him loudly as you speak to one another, lest your deeds become worthless while you perceive not. Indeed, those who lower their voices in the presence of the Messenger of Allah — those are the ones whose hearts Allah has tested for piety. For them is forgiveness and a great reward. Indeed, those who call you from behind the chambers — most of them do not reason. And if they had patiently waited until you came out to them, it would have been better for them﴾ [Al-Hujurat: 2–5].

All of this falls under the category of adab (courtesy) in addressing the Prophet ﷺ, speaking with him, and speaking in his presence, just as they were commanded to give charity before privately consulting him.[[Addition from F and A.]]

The second view regarding this is that the meaning of ﴿Do not make the calling of the Messenger among yourselves like your calling of one another﴾ is: do not believe that his supplication against others is like the supplication of others, for his supplication is answered. So beware lest he supplicate against you and you be destroyed. This was related by Ibn Abi Hatim from Ibn Abbas, al-Hasan al-Basri, and Atiyyah al-Awfi. And Allah knows best.[[In F and A: "And Allah"]]

* *

As for His words, ﴿Allah already knows those among you who slip away, concealing themselves﴾: Muqatil ibn Hayyan said: "They are the hypocrites. Speech (meaning the khutbah, the sermon) was burdensome to them on the day of Friday. They would take cover behind some of the Companions, the companions of Muhammad ﷺ, until they left the mosque. It was not permissible for a man to leave the mosque on Friday, after the Prophet ﷺ had begun the khutbah, except with his permission. When one of them wanted to leave, he would gesture with his finger toward the Prophet ﷺ, and he would grant him permission without the man having to speak. For if any one of them spoke while the Prophet ﷺ was delivering the khutbah, his Friday prayer was invalidated."

As-Suddi said: "When they were with him in a gathering, some of them would hide behind others until they slipped away from him, so that he would not see them."

Qatadah said concerning His words, ﴿Allah already knows those among you who slip away, concealing themselves﴾, meaning: concealing themselves [from the Prophet of Allah and from his Book].

Sufyan said: ﴿Allah already knows those among you who slip away, concealing themselves﴾ — he said: "from the row." Mujahid said concerning the verse, ﴿Allah already knows those among you who slip away, concealing themselves﴾, he said: "Opposing (khilafan)."

* *

As for His words, ﴿So let those who oppose his order beware﴾: that is, the order of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. His path, his methodology, his way, his sunnah (practice), and his law (shari'ah) are what is meant. Statements and actions are weighed by his statements and actions: whatever agrees with them is accepted, and whatever contradicts them is rejected and returned to its speaker and doer, whoever he may be. As it is established in the two Sahihs and elsewhere, from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, that he said: "Whoever does an action that is not in accordance with our order, it is rejected."[[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. (2697), and Sahih Muslim, no. (1718).]]

That is: let whoever opposes the law of the Messenger, inwardly or outwardly, beware and fear ﴿lest a trial afflict them﴾, that is, in their hearts, through disbelief, hypocrisy, or bid'ah (innovation), ﴿or a painful punishment strike them﴾, that is, in this world, through killing, a prescribed punishment (hadd), imprisonment, or the like.

Imam Ahmad said: Abd al-Razzaq narrated to us, Ma'mar narrated to us, from Hammam ibn Munabbih, who said: "This is what Abu Hurairah narrated to us, who said: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'The parable of me and you is like the parable of a man who kindled a fire. When it illuminated what was around it, the moths and these creatures began to fall into it, and he kept trying to hold them back, but they overpowered him and plunged into it.' He said: 'That is my parable and yours. I am taking hold of your waist-wrappers to keep you from the Fire, saying, "Come away from the Fire!" but you overpower me and plunge into it.'" Both [Al-Bukhari and Muslim] related it from the narration of Abd al-Razzaq.[[Musnad (2/312) and Sahih Muslim, no. (2284). It is not in al-Bukhari through this chain.]]

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 24, verse 64:

He, exalted is He, informs that He owns the heavens and the earth, that He knows the unseen of the heavens and the earth, and that He knows what the servants do, in secret and in public. So He says: ﴿Indeed, He knows what you are upon.﴾ The word "qad" (قَدْ) here is for emphasis (tahqiq, affirmation and certainty), as He said before it: ﴿Allah certainly knows those among you who slip away, sheltering behind one another.﴾ And He, exalted is He, said: ﴿Allah certainly knows those among you who hinder others, and those who say to their brothers, "Come to us."﴾ [al-Ahzab: 18]. He also said: ﴿Allah has certainly heard the speech of she who pleads with you concerning her husband and complains to Allah, and Allah hears your mutual argument. Indeed, Allah is Hearing and Seeing.﴾ [al-Mujadila: 1]. He said: ﴿We certainly know that what they say grieves you, but they do not deny you; rather, the wrongdoers deny the signs of Allah.﴾ [al-An'am: 33]. He said: ﴿We see the turning of your face toward the heaven, so We will surely turn you to a qiblah that pleases you.﴾ [al-Baqarah: 144]. So all these verses contain the affirmation of the act by "qad," just as the muezzin says, affirming and establishing: "Qad qamat as-salah, qad qamat as-salah" (the prayer has indeed begun, the prayer has indeed begun). Therefore His saying, exalted is He, ﴿Indeed, He knows what you are upon﴾ means: He knows it, witnesses it, and nothing of it escapes Him, not even the weight of an atom. As He said, exalted is He: ﴿And rely upon the Mighty, the Merciful, who sees you when you stand, and your movement among those who prostrate. Indeed, He is the Hearing, the Knowing.﴾ [ash-Shu'ara': 217-220]. He said: ﴿And you are not engaged in any matter, nor recite from it any Quran, nor do you do any deed except that We are witnesses over you when you are involved therein. And not hidden from your Lord is an atom's weight on earth or in the heaven, nor anything smaller than that or greater, but it is in a clear register.﴾ [Yunus: 61] [[In F: "in the heavens and not in the earth", which is an error.]] He said, exalted is He: ﴿Then is He who stands over every soul in what it has earned...﴾ [ar-Ra'd: 33], meaning: He is Witness over His servants for what they do of good and evil. He said, exalted is He: ﴿Unquestionably, when they wrap themselves in their garments, He knows what they conceal and what they reveal. Indeed, He is Knowing of what is within the breasts.﴾ [Hud: 5] [[Addition from F, A.]] He said, exalted is He: ﴿Equal among you is one who conceals speech and one who speaks openly, and one who hides by night and one who goes forth by day.﴾ [ar-Ra'd: 10]. He said, exalted is He: ﴿And there is no creature on earth but that upon Allah is its provision, and He knows its place of dwelling and its place of storage. All is in a clear register.﴾ [Hud: 6]. And He said: ﴿And with Him are the keys of the unseen; none knows them except Him. He knows what is on the land and in the sea. Not a leaf falls but that He knows it, nor is there a grain within the darknesses of the earth or anything fresh or dry but that it is in a clear register.﴾ [al-An'am: 59]. The verses and hadiths on this are very numerous.

* *

As for His saying: ﴿And the Day they are returned to Him﴾, meaning: the Day the creatures return to Allah, which is the Day of Resurrection, ﴿He will inform them of what they did﴾, meaning: He will inform them of what they did in the world, great and small, minor and major, as He said, exalted is He: ﴿Man will be informed on that Day of what he sent ahead and kept back.﴾ [al-Qiyamah: 13]. And He said: ﴿And the record will be placed, and you will see the criminals fearful of what is in it, and they will say, "Woe to us! What is this book that leaves nothing small or great but has enumerated it?" And they will find what they did present, and your Lord does not wrong anyone.﴾ [al-Kahf: 49]. Therefore He said here: ﴿And the Day they are returned to Him, He will inform them of what they did. And Allah is Knowing of all things.﴾ All praise is due to Allah, Lord of the worlds, and we ask Him for completion.
